## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-04.md

# Router VPN continuation evidence — November 4, 2026 UTC

These checks began on November 3 in America/Chicago and continued into November 4.
This record distinguishes recovered authority, published source, executable
checks, native CI, release publication and live acceptance. It does not replace
the original requirements or declare the project complete.

## Authority recovered before implementation

The original August 11 user product/breakage message in `mm.md`, its explicit
instruction to retain both old and new scope, the numbered 312–356/C1–C7 audit
in the reconciled August 12 mega handoff, original August 13–14 external-node
and AI-provider requests in `New chat (1).md`, and the original August 19
map-first message in `Router VPN Progress Update.md` were read. The October 19
continuation contains the original Local/Server two-response average and
timeout rule. Saved context was used as an index, not proof of the repository.
The project-source surface was empty; accessible originals were recovered
through the user's files. Not every historical individual message was available.

The numbered 356-item audit is an organized requirement record, not 356
independently recovered verbatim user turns. The current explicit handoff also
preserves the READY retention and XOR corrections. No shortened handoff or
green source gate removes scope. Keep [REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md),
[the October 30 source reconciliation](RECONCILIATION-2026-10-30-SOURCES.md)
and `configs/current-requirements.json` as the existing ledger and contracts.

Original qualifications remain: #339 makes macOS signing/notarization optional
polish when practical; #335 node favorites and C3 multi-admin login are optional;
#321–322 retain feasible rare BSD/Unix packaging. This does not waive core
native platforms, legitimate iOS provisioning or truthful distribution claims.

## Recovery and publication identity

The initial live `main` was
`ee2bc64efa3335fd790f9dfbf2347b6181b6ff0a`, tree
`3601cac0f46190ce80b3aba035d6f2528a7c3882`. Its tree exactly matched the preserved
local `08cd3037c866ccadf9bcc9f464b6719add8e1295` snapshot: the first six recovery
units were already upstream under different API commit identities. They were
not replayed. Four subsequent preserved source units were compared, tested
within the available environment and published individually below.

Each published change used the current remote parent, a complete content tree,
an exact local/remote tree comparison and a non-force reference update guarded
by the expected parent. A fresh GitHub reference read verified every update.
The original recovery checkout was preserved. The shell's HTTPS push lacked
credentials; supported connected GitHub writes succeeded. This was not a
branch, force-push, PR, deployment or router-change operation.

The source cutoff for this record is
[`4d25725ccef863a1e800a18483372308cd5d6a9f`](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/commit/4d25725ccef863a1e800a18483372308cd5d6a9f),

## Native Linux receipt operation correction published at 2f31dfda

The explicit receipt path previously used the later operation for its original
descriptor/event fences but reused the constructor's context inside ordinary
link, address, route and rule readbacks. A completed MTU construction could
therefore reject a later valid read; that mixed context also failed to honor
the later operation throughout the full receipt.

The same captured operation now reaches every native dump and both final
checks. Construction wrappers keep their original startup context; no option
is rewritten and no new authority or deadline is created. Darwin/Windows
retain their existing synchronous native inventories and reject canceled
result adoption. The ordinary no-context command/Box projection callers remain
a separate follow-on, explicitly recorded in the native retirement contract.

The final focused native race passes in 1.032s. Four exact-source controls
independently substitute the old receipt, link, address and route context paths;
each fails the intended executable assertion without a compile failure or
unintended data race. Actual reprepare/read-only verification passes four tests
in 1.208s. Darwin ARM64 test-image and Windows AMD64 package-archive compilation
pass; neither is native execution. The expanded existing kernel-inventory case
requires fresh reads after canceled construction, and every mandatory native
MTU candidate now ends its construction operation before the real adopted-TUN
receipt. Those kernel cases remain required in CI and were not run locally.

The separate generated-command/TUN [run 41828373994](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/41828373994)
passes both exact-`2f31dfda` jobs: AMD64 `126568876844` and ARM64
`126568876427`. All six original cases include original-TUN retirement:
On-connect, Always, captured MTU, MTU rollback, resolver failure and wrong key.
Their native parent durations are 23.91s and 24.02s. This confirms the earlier
readback failures are closed for those cases; it does not prove the separate
three-case MTU transaction suite, later channel change or installed service.

propagation through those paths remains open and is not claimed by the new
explicit transaction/startup checks.

## Integrated original-caller observations

Commit `a94cde9d` connects the original observation context
through shipping command projections, native Box identity, inbound and network
receipts, physical owner/broker/PT observations, selected graph/cover proofs,
server leases and the actual pinned OpenVPN client/endpoint state.

- Context-aware capabilities are explicit. Missing support is an integration
  error, not permission to call an unbounded legacy reader.
- Pure caller cancellation/expiry cannot adopt a late receipt or retire a
  healthy connection. Confirmed owner/graph failure revokes the original
  admission immediately, including a real failure joined with cancellation.
- Revocation does not synchronously join held cleanup locks. Original owners
  retain cleanup and Close/Stop joins; replacement owners are not affected.
- External/Tor commands watch their original Stop capability independently of
  a blocked receipt reader. The watcher retains the original directory,
  session and source identity and is joined on exit.
- Linux network observations retain the original dump/ACK stream and exact
  interface/address identity. Sent requests are drained after cancellation.
  Darwin and Windows observations retain original locks and pre/post context
  checks; fixed OS inventory syscalls are not claimed interruptible.
- Tor heartbeat adopts one complete MTU/network receipt only after matching
  interface name, index and MTU, rereading the original MTU revision and checking
  the same caller. Mismatch, revision-only ABA and late cancellation preserve
  the prior receipt.
- Windows identity publishes its verified original owner once through an
  immutable atomic pointer. Observation never waits on its publication mutex;
  capture equality, validity, closing state and freshness remain required.
- Native dependency projection preserves exact pins and source/tamper checks.
  The shared observation-error classifier is projected narrowly, without
  exposing unrelated common-package files to native builds.

## Native MTU operation admission and original cleanup

Commit [`721511bb`](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/commit/721511bbf641dca3fcf0e3e5a310079996a6fced) connects bounded MTU capture, command-mailbox
admission, status, cancellation, cache commit, native replacement and restoration.
The accepted command retains its original lifetime and transported absolute
deadline; a short maintenance poll cannot cancel it or give it a new deadline.
Tor registration and worker publication share one generation. If an admission
acknowledgement arrives after the polling caller expires, that accepted worker
is still published for owned cleanup but is canceled before measurement.

Each admitted operation has one lazily activated cleanup allowance. Native
replacement, failed-candidate retirement, readback, physical rebind and rollback
share its remainder. A cleanup read cannot renew it. Late candidate results
cannot become winners, and a missing/expired allowance or replaced owner cannot
report successful restoration. A valid original owner still restores after
cancellation: the actual returned transaction is retained even when cancellation
prevented ordinary post-change observation. Unused rollback-reader closure cannot
publish an expired winner or resurrect the closed rollback reader.

The final combined prepared native composition includes the already-published
FD11 launch changes. It passed all 47 required parent/leaf verdicts under race
across generated mobilemtu, inbound manager, TUN, native command and Box
finalization packages. Both Darwin architecture TUN packages compiled with the
changed native control methods. The merged routing runner passed 39 checks and
the Tor audit passed 42 checks. Earlier focused causal controls rejected lost
authorized rollback, late publication, renewed cleanup, held manager/startup
admission, lost finalization retry and a live worker after late admission.

These results cover the accepted native MTU command and its transport. The
client snapshot/proof-dispatch closure is recorded in the later section below. The
installed persistent service still needs its actual operation worker and public
Retest/Cancel integration. Neither requirement is closed by this native unit.
The original Tor authenticated reply drain retains its separate five-second
ownership allowance; fixed native syscalls are not claimed hard-interruptible.

## Installed Linux service: original operation channel foundation

Commit [`f76382cf`](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/commit/f76382cf57fb9c12851b5962a108b49beaf31f51)
adds FD11 to the actual service launch and
fixed native child. The original sealed capture binds its device, inode, size
and layout. Startup verifies the child's acknowledgement against the exact
authenticated Ready receipt. Original FD10 retirement remains unchanged.

FD11 has a fixed 12,648,448-byte layout: a 64-KiB control region and 32 bounded
transaction records, each with separate Ready and retirement pages for the
original, candidate and rollback readers. A record reserves capacity before
construction; later reader bindings must describe the actual retained readers.
A failed partial reader can have retirement evidence without an invented Ready.
Raw evidence pages preserve the existing 16-KiB native receipt parser limit.

Work and cancellation use separate local locks and original process-level file
lock regions. Cancellation remains available when the work deadline has expired
or another process holds the work region. Shared inherited open-file-description
locks cannot substitute for those process locks. Stable reads, canonical frame
digests, original keys, non-reusable sequence/slots and exact retained descriptors
reject torn, replayed or substituted evidence. The native child closes FD11 only
after retiring its original native resources; the service joins its original
child before closing its copy.

Focused validation passed 59 standardengine race verdicts, including ten new
operation-channel parent tests, six original startup-fixture leaves and four
mandatory service-runner checks. The actual inherited child and process lock
tests execute real descriptor inheritance and interprocess locking. Replacing

## One captured service MTU run and shared cleanup deadline

The installed Linux service now keeps one optimizer run across its controller,
service and actual fixed native child. The original accepted work deadline is
bounded to 45 seconds; candidate commands cannot restart it. Either original
process can activate the same absolute cleanup deadline once, within the retained
eight-second allowance. Cleanup commands may restore only the run's captured
original MTU. The separate original Stop budget remains unchanged.

FD11 layout 3 binds each command and raw result to that exact run. The old layout
is rejected. Run closure requires both original observers to settle the actual
transaction history and the original child to observe and acknowledge its current
reader. A transaction cancelled before submission retains a permanent tombstone:
both real observer acknowledgements settle it without inventing a native result.
Lost Begin acknowledgements, delayed packets and closed runs cannot admit another
candidate or renew the cleanup clock. The existing 32 transaction slots and 32
retained run identifiers remain bounded and are never recycled on a live connection.

The optimizer's existing verified winner adoption under its controller mutex is
now the explicit completion boundary for Cancel. Cancellation accepted before
adoption performs the exact original-MTU rollback. After adoption, Cancel reports
that the committed result is finishing; it does not promise a rollback or cancel
another owner. A later request cancellation preserves that already-applied value
only after the original run joins successfully. Stop, invalidation, changed
ownership and closure failure still prevent a measured-success result.

## Original Node-to-standard service succession

The shipping standard connection captures the installed Node parent, selected
policy and private exit before Stop joins the original engine. Its retained
closed Node creator then reserves an immutable destination and durable intent.
The service authenticates the actual parent/installation/namespaces and complete
closed source inventory, prepares its own guard without starting an engine, and
returns its pinned successor inventory. Only the original Node creator can
remove its source table beside that exact successor in a stable native
generation. The service independently proves source absence before acknowledging
commit; normal Start resumes the same prepared owner and original deadline.

Source, destination, process birth/image, namespace, configuration and policy
identities remain distinct. Lost replies retain both original capabilities and
the actual result; metadata never reconstructs a creator. Abort verifies the
source guard remains present before releasing the prepared successor. Unknown
aborts fence delayed prepares, unrelated protocol scopes reject reverse
authority, and unresolved transfers block ordinary release/replacement/upgrade.
Committed current queries reobserve the original guard. An old native Finish
retry cannot clear a newer reservation. Unknown native deletion acknowledgement
stays pending rather than becoming fabricated removal evidence.

Integration review also identified three ordinary mutex waits in the existing
standard Start path. They now retain the captured work deadline. Prior-owner
admission happens before replacement publication, outside the application lock;
the application lock then rechecks the original map and operation. Peer movement

## Active Always service image coordination

The live installer/service protocol now composes the previously published
immutable-generation and native creator-transfer foundations. It retains the
old and new actual guards, fixed-role image/peer identities, original lock
open-file descriptions, canonical private-state inodes and captured profile.
Only after both same-policy creators are pinned does it yield global source SH
for exact code-only promotion. Native removal, saved-state publication,
activation, actual successor READY, original process/listener join and fresh
successor protection proof are distinct required stages. No stage reconstructs
a native creator from saved JSON.

Before source removal, abort proves the old creator and restores the exact
original code inodes before retiring the candidate. After acknowledged removal,
recovery can only complete the same successor. One absolute work allowance of
at most 120 seconds and one nonrenewable 30-second cleanup allowance are shared by
the original participants; these are implementation bounds, not recovered user

receipts and logs. The retrieved logs establish those executions; their uploaded
artifact bytes were not independently downloaded in this observation.

This is the generated **Node** command/TUN path, including selected DNS, encrypted
traffic and pre-acknowledgement TUN closure. It does not substitute for the new
standard-child idle-parent death fixture, the new direct-resolver kernel cases,
app-level Router proof, physical devices, or full release publication. The
aggregate release workflow for this SHA was cancelled after newer main work;
cancellation is not a release pass.

## Linux Local SS2022 entry to HTTP/HTTPS CONNECT final

The client and shared native compiler now admit the existing retained SS entry
owner for its separately captured HTTP/HTTPS CONNECT final on Linux. Admission
keeps Local execution, distinct entry/final identities and supported SS2022
methods, with both Start Layers Off and original On-connect/Always protection.
The existing graph/compiler retains a TCP-only physical entry and routes the
final connection and selected DNS behind it; it does not invent UDP support for
CONNECT. Original source fingerprints, credentials, proof ownership, final TLS
trust/name and complete Speed Lab restoration remain separate for both nodes.

Native fixtures use real SS2022 cipher/authentication and independent HTTP/HTTPS
CONNECT references. Wrong SS key/method evidence comes from the actual reference's
authenticated-connection counter; HTTPS trust/name refusal uses its actual TLS
alert. The new refusal counter is restricted to the Linux actual-entry loopback
fixture so the older strict Darwin wire schema is preserved. This is not a new
claim of Darwin execution. Previously unsupported-final negatives are changed
only where CONNECT becomes supported; unsupported HY2/SOCKS and other malformed
or unowned graphs retain rejection coverage.

The frozen runtime preparation is `b9930302` plus 13 owned source files, with all
2,044 expected native records and module metadata unchanged. Client/shared race
execution passes 96 named verdicts (26.643 and 5.069 seconds). The native group
passes seven physical-owner model verdicts in 1.196 seconds and 32 actual
cipher/CONNECT-reference verdicts in 28.068 seconds. Those groups preserve the
prior SS-to-SS cases. The old client admission body compiles and rejects 13
intended verdicts at the new valid-path assertion; the old native policy body
compiles and rejects three intended physical-policy verdicts. Neither control
uses a compile failure, timeout, panic or skip as evidence.

The final 17-file source composes that runtime work with the newer packet-peer
preparer mapping and the published parent/resolver runner changes through
`782e9f2a`. The physical runner passes 55 tests in 19.201 seconds, including its
actual bounded worker/ownership fixtures and causal controls. The installed-host
runner passes 41 tests in 112.397 seconds. Its prior 484 cases retain their exact
order, followed by 23 CONNECT cases (507 total); the nine reverse-transfer cases
remain unchanged. Compiled source-authority, native reference and receipt
inventories remain mandatory, with exact pass/receipt multiplicity and output
hashes. Later source/gate composition is not relabeled as a rerun of the entire
older native runtime. Exact-SHA installed kernel execution, platform builds,
publication, devices and off-LAN behavior remain separate evidence obligations.

Windows retained ordinary entries, other graph families, Server/Compare and
additional Start Layer compositions remain individual implementation work. No
original graph/platform requirement is removed by the bounded admission here.

## Conditional native bootstrap rule removal

The original cleanup read back a generation-bracketed inventory, then invoked a
separate nft subprocess to delete by handle. An intervening ruleset change could
replace that handle between observation and mutation. Cleanup now retains the
observed generation and submits a conditional atomic Netlink batch using the
same original native endpoint, table, output chain and acknowledged rule handle.
It revalidates the original lease before sending. A changed generation rejects
the transaction; begin/command/foreign acknowledgements cannot substitute for
the original committed batch receipt. A malformed or lost receipt retains the
uncertain endpoint and owner. Complete original baseline and rule-absence
readback still precedes closing the original socket and file.

The isolated source consists of `782e9f2a50a82693f05658c9efa0422a472610e4`
plus the eight files in this unit. Both root and normally prepared native
bootstrap/baseline suites execute 152 named verdicts under the race detector,
with no failures or skips (1.211 seconds and 1.194 seconds respectively). Native
preparation starts from pristine pinned core
`1ac1a339cb1223e9c70eae14c44411c75033c02d`, uses its own Xray checkout and the
ordinary preparer, and verifies all 177 copied source records unchanged after
execution. The compiled control that zeroes the batch generation fails the
intended wire-condition assertion. Three focused Python gates pass in 1.515
seconds, the strict namespace verdict inventory rejects missing/renamed/duplicate
or failed results, and restoring the old subprocess cleanup fails the exact
source-wiring assertion.

The actual-kernel fixture adds six mandatory scenarios: stale ruleset,
same-handle replacement, pre-send cancellation, committed removal, retired
handle and closed endpoint. It owns an unhooked table inside the required fresh
network namespace and verifies that the independent baseline remains intact.
The native gate requires every child verdict and the actual zero-generation
causal failure. These fixtures compile in the prepared engine; their privileged
execution remains exact-SHA CI evidence because the previously recorded local
namespace/proc launch mismatch is unresolved. Local wire/model results do not
stand in for that kernel execution.

Before publication, newer `6318a5c7`, `1938916a` and `7903b70d` source was
preserved. None changes these eight frozen implementation/gate paths. The latter
also advances the independent mobile graph work; its author-reported tests are
not represented as a fresh execution of this Linux suite. Kernel grant expiry,
recovery after a lost creation acknowledgement, full resolved policy execution,
current all-platform publication and physical/private acceptance remain open.

## Remaining implementation and acceptance

The complete original scope remains open. Apple captured per-hop profile
restoration, the persisted Start Layer fixture correction and macOS Performance
cancellation are now published with the bounded evidence in their rows. Other
original native UI, settings, Methods, recovery and graph requirements retain
their individual closure obligations; these sixty units are not a replacement scope.

The concrete Apple Home DNS substitution gap reported at `8fdc2ef7` is repaired
in `5b32bcf5` with the bounded evidence above. Intentional UDP/53 for Fastest node
measurement remains a different path. Android Home DNS now has its own published
repair in `f4d222cb`. The full 45-combination SOCKS layer feature is published
in `a08d7d6f`, preserving the final-only and entry-only contributor units. Its
updated complete native and host gates pass as recorded above; the separate
NAT repair `775ac68e` alone was not treated as feature acceptance. The newly failed persistence regression fixture above is now repaired in source;
its new exact-SHA CI evidence remains pending.

In particular, support for one entry/final graph does not prove every requested
protocol pairing, independent layer combination, local/server execution or
platform. Supported source must still be connected to the actual daily app,
owned lifecycle, complete restoration, native engine and relevant negative
controls. Unavailable capability with an honest reason is safer behavior, not
completion of the corresponding requested capability.

Concrete source implementation gaps remain in this same mobile imported-entry
direction: the newer concurrent `9cf424f3` supports CONNECT to paired SS2022
only with both layers Off and exact selected literal TCP DNS. CONNECT datagrams,
other DNS transports and independent layers, other paired final families and
Server/Compare still need implementation and evidence. The bounded OpenVPN
entry direction is now published as unit 46 with its exact graph/native/host
evidence above; it must not be carried forward as wholly absent.
They are not merely live-access or device-evidence gaps. See the
[precise open graph boundaries](MOBILE-IMPORTED-ROUTER-PATH.md#open-graph-requirements)
for the capability and selected-DNS constraints that a further implementation
must resolve without weakening original authority.

Remaining evidence is tracked separately:

| Boundary | Still required |
|---|---|
| One current source generation | All required workflow attempts at the selected exact SHA, authoritative native package matrix, nine matching ARM64 images, source/security/preflight checks, exact compose, archive parity, provenance/checksums and publication. A different SHA's pass is not interchangeable. |
| Matching-host native integration | Windows WFP/Wintun/installed/Portable ownership; macOS PF/utun/installer and actual Swift/SDK boundaries; Linux installed/kernel/TUN/resolver composition; Android/iOS native build and VPN host integration for each claimed path. |
| Physical device and network behavior | Install/permission, DNS/IPv4/IPv6, route/leak negatives, reconnect/network change, sleep/wake/on-demand as applicable, complete temporary-test restoration, actual hop throughput and MTU behavior, off-LAN interoperability. |
| Native visual and accessibility acceptance | Map-first UI, DPI, responsive/orientation behavior, touch/desktop controls, real permission-based location and accessibility on requested targets. |
| Private server/provider validation | Live benchmark, forwarding, Stop/Emergency Stop/Resume, updater rollback, configured AI Help providers and server-side credential/context boundaries. |
| Distribution | Legitimate Apple signing/provisioning, macOS notarization where required, and actual installation/launch/distribution evidence. An unsigned resignable IPA is not this proof. |
| Production and household safety | One deliberate exact-SHA Portainer deployment, live health/path checks, ASUS exact-port/JFFS revalidation preserving household connectivity, then final regression. |

Use [LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) and
`deploy/live-release-evidence.py` for SHA-bound hashed live evidence. No live
gate is marked complete by this document, and no completion percentage is used.

# Router VPN continuation evidence — November 6, 2026 UTC

## Scope and source identity

This is an implementation and evidence ledger, not a replacement for the user's
original requirements. The live starting branch was
[`b04eccee94f4cf3e83f978cbb74504e796c056a6`](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/commit/b04eccee94f4cf3e83f978cbb74504e796c056a6),
1,294 commits ahead of the older published `745b3e41` release. Old patches were
not replayed over that history. The published units below retain normal
`main` ancestry through
[`75897b4d7099b500762b6402ed967d4442f2705d`](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/commit/75897b4d7099b500762b6402ed967d4442f2705d).
For the local publication units, each remote tree was compared with its local
committed tree; exact validation cutoffs are recorded below. The later fixture-only
reconciliation during the workspace outage uses remote source review and CI,
without a claim of unavailable local execution. The remote branch was read back before adoption. A saved patch, local commit or API
schema was not counted as a successful push.

The November 5 recovery metadata remains intact. Six frozen Apple files could
be reconstructed and checked against their recorded hashes. Complete bytes for
the shared, Android, Windows and Linux drafts were not recovered from the old
workspaces. New work was made against current source and verified independently;
it is not described as an exact recovery of those absent drafts.

| Original source or passage | Recovered requirement authority |
|---|---|
| `mm.md`, including the August 11 product request and its surrounding conversation | Native daily-use applications, setup/application separation, complete profiles, measurements, protection, modes, DNS and deployment requirements. |

Preserved exact contracts include SMART AUTO, IPv6 On, AUTO encryption and
obfuscation requirements Off, Home AdGuard, fifty node samples, and
`(last_node_response_time + external_server_response_time) / 2` through each
candidate using the same external endpoint. Invalid candidates have no score;
the winner must be rechecked and its captured execution restored. READY package
retention remains thirty minutes without extension; Cancel/Delete/shutdown clean
immediately. Blank AdGuard Allowed Clients remains unrestricted. Client kill
switch failure is closed; ASUS forwarding failure preserves household Internet.
Production remains exact-SHA ARM64 image-only, without Docker socket access.

The native mobile results use the pinned production preparation chain, including
actual source/config equality and mandatory constructor/MTU parsing. They do
not substitute a copied miniature engine for the shipping composition. Actual
Swift execution found a missing runtime-selector admission and incorrect numeric
metadata conversion; both were repaired before the published matrix passed.

Windows native SS entry acceptance requires independent entry/final public TLS
proofs, different expected addresses, selected DNS, wrong-key and wrong-identity
rejection, cancellation, successor restoration and durable-commit refusal.
Both SS layers exercise all three ciphers with different credentials. The added
Hysteria2 final retains its independent password, TLS identity and trust bundle. A held
real final DNS TCP conversation makes the live physical-entry WFP grant observable;
already closed proof sockets are not evidence of current ownership. Two deliberate
production mutations must fail with their exact witnesses.

The provider cleanup fix authenticates the original receipt, drains at most
256 KiB of trailing stdout concurrently with joining that same process, and caps
diagnostics at 64 KiB. Both normal join and post-cancellation reaping are bounded.
Actual child-process tests cover a large trailer, overflow, failed exit and stalled
child. These portable tests and all seven native phases are mandatory in the
standalone Windows workflow and authoritative packaging path.

## Configured SS source and Apple runtime DNS follow-up

The configured SS declaration introduced in `29bf1fb5`, preserved-upgrade
verification in `66c81cde`, and native asset compatibility in `0752df09` bind the
original private source bytes to their captured node. Subsequent upstream
`3f9701e3` and `fd48f71c` add independent paired-owner validation and real
generated-store/capture fixtures. These changes remain in normal `main`
ancestry; this Apple follow-up was reconciled on `df96e9cc` without replacing
those newer paths.

Apple DNS preparation now validates the configured declaration before use and
keeps the original SS source unchanged. PacketTunnel verifies that source again,
then applies the saved resolver only to its runtime projection. An unset DNS
selection retains the complete original resolver, including its TCP port or
encrypted hostname/bootstrap graph. Explicit Home, custom, DoT, DoH and DoH3
policies use their captured transport, port, TLS identity and request path.
Resolver hostname bootstrap stays inside the selected proxy.

Manual Xray startup now carries its resolved AES source with the selected
candidate. The extension compares the complete candidate with the original,
allowing only the SS server-address resolution. Keys, ports, protocol fields,
DNS and other graph contents cannot be substituted; an already literal server
must retain the same IP identity, including equivalent IPv6 spellings. The
passive declaration is consumed only in that verified runtime projection.

Focused executable evidence for this follow-up:

- `deploy/test_ios_ss_service_dns.py`: **522 checks passed** using the shipping
  Swift DNS/capture/graph code and exact extracted PacketTunnel/launch bodies.
  This includes independent layer selections, IPv4/IPv6 Home transports,
  encrypted-hostname bootstrap, unset and explicit resolver policies, paired
  final graphs, malformed/stale/foreign metadata, and resolved-candidate
  credential/graph substitution controls. Two separately compiled source
  mutants were rejected for rewriting the original source and omitting the
  selected runtime DNS policy.
- `deploy/test_ios_xray_start_layer.py`: the existing actual Swift plus shared
  Go compiler suite passed **754 checks** with the updated launch handoff.
- `ios/RouterVPN/test_dns_policy_contract.py`, Python syntax checks and
  `git diff --check` passed. The macOS authenticated Start Layer workflow now
  requires the new Swift regression alongside its existing cases.

The local Linux Swift fixture uses the existing IP parser boundary and a real
Go SHA256-backed CryptoKit test module. It does not start NetworkExtension or
prove asynchronous host ownership, native packaged execution, peer traffic,
physical DNS/leak behavior, or Apple signing. Those gates remain separate.

### Android companion and resolved-candidate follow-up

The Android picker, ordinary native startup and Start Layer consumer now validate
the original two-asset SS declaration through a passive shared API. A hostname
can retain its captured service identity without being admitted as an unresolved
physical transport. The existing owned Xray resolver still performs resolution.
Its AES result stays with that candidate and is checked against the complete
original graph before attachment and again before consumption. A different
valid key, port, protocol or unrelated graph field cannot replace the original.
Only the verified runtime projection is staged; the saved private source remains
unchanged. Existing paired factory ownership checks are preserved.

The final focused shared race run passed in **3.231 seconds**, including the
published paired-owner controls. Actual shipping Android Java plus the shared
Go helper passed **77 checks**, including valid alternate-key substitution and
failure without staging. The existing no-sidecar Xray path passed **690 checks**.
Earlier compiler/javac processes were killed and are not counted as passes; the
final runs completed sequentially with bounded compiler/JVM heaps. The new Java
and shared checks are mandatory in native Xray CI. Existing Android OS doubles
remain explicit; a generated AAR, packaged application and device network run
still require their separate native evidence.

## Native SS reply fixture overflow

Exact-source Windows phase run `42194825405`, SS-entry job `127815824195`,
failed at `3f9701e3` because the independent DNS peer allocated prefix space
and payload bytes but no trailing authentication-tag space. The pinned SS2022
server then panicked while appending its 16-byte AEAD tag. This was a concrete
fixture failure before the required native path proof, not a successful rejection
or evidence that the complete SS graph worked.

The peer now obtains both front and rear space from its actual wrapped writer
and bounds both before allocation. `deploy/test_ss_packet_reply_headroom.py`
extracts the complete fixture method and runs the pinned SS2022 client/server.
Direct and CachedPacket/udpnat encrypted DNS replies decrypt to the original
question and expected answer; a modified tag fails real authentication. The
three-case race run passes in **1.013 seconds**. A separately executed old
allocation reproduces the exact `serverPacketWriter.WritePacket` overflow
requesting 16 bytes, and the regression runner then exits successfully.

No production transport, firewall grant, rejection witness or native timeout is
relaxed. The full Windows phase still needs execution at the repaired source;
the local encrypted round trip does not stand in for WFP or device acceptance.

### Native TCP connector completion observation and refusal regression

The Windows importer calls its native connector outside the identity gate and publishes the result through `finishNativeTCP` afterward. The existing actual successful-transition test deliberately exercises the interval in which the connector has returned while the stored phase is still Pending. Therefore the earlier AMD64 failed-inspection `phase=0` alone does not establish that Connect was still running. No causal repair is inferred from that ambiguity.

The original imported I/O object now retains a non-authoritative, mutex-protected copy of connector entry/return, fixed result class and numeric errno. Classification occurs outside the I/O mutex; only assignment/copying holds it, and the writer releases it before the existing finish hook. The fixture's failed-inspection diagnostic includes this observation and closing/closed flags. These diagnostic reads happen after the original inspection failure and are not an atomic record of that earlier instant. No observation field participates in admission, identity transition, cancellation or retirement, and no independent `SO_ERROR` read is added.

`TestDesktopSocketWindowsIdentityObservesRefusedConnectBeforePublication` keeps a TCP/IPv4 destination exclusively bound without listening, requires the original connector's actual refusal `10061`, and holds the identity gate until the returned observation is visible. It requires the original pending owner, refuses premature source close, and rejects any connected inspection. A nil inspection error must still supply the complete original bound identity; an actual ALE error is observed without being rewritten into success. The test then requires the original partial owner/error, failed-phase publication, joined close, keeper close and exact retirement. An actual retirement failure remains a required test failure.

The test is appended to the mandatory native inventory, preserving every existing positional mutation selector; the runner also checks its unique presence. The source inventory becomes 22 required native parent cases and 16 Python runner methods. ## 2026-11-06 — Bound and serialize the actual OpenVPN provider IPC lifecycle

The native OpenVPN fixture previously wrote requests without a shared operation deadline and then started a separate read timeout. A pipe blocked during Encode could outlive the observation, and simultaneous observers could consume each other's replies.

The original provider process now owns one serialized request/reply permit. The same absolute caller deadline bounds queue admission, write, strict reply framing and the successful worker join. Cancellation while queued does not write a request or stop the active caller. Once an exchange has entered, a failed write, read, frame or deadline irrevocably poisons that original process: cancel the child first, close both owned pipes, and join its worker and process under a separate bounded cleanup context. No replacement reader or process adopts the operation. Idle Close retains graceful EOF cleanup; active Close cancels first, and repeated Close is idempotent.

Existing 16 KiB newline framing, exact transport and original tuple checks, AppID attribution, provider lifetime and the 10-second initial/observation budgets remain unchanged. Error reporting records fixed failure classes and context errors without dumping requests or private configuration.

The existing mandatory provider-join tests remain intact. Eight additional real-pipe and owned-subprocess regression leaves cover normal/idempotent use, a genuinely queued deadline while the active exchange is latched, blocked reads, a 2 MiB blocked write, active Close, malformed replies, oversized replies and changed transport identity. The runner requires exactly one PASS for the parent and each leaf and rejects missing, duplicate, skipped, failed, race, panic or build results. Each failure checks that the original worker/process has joined and that its reader cannot be reused.

### Actual CONNECT producers and parsers after toolchain recovery

A separate execution against `2ff74fd3` now passes the previously blocked
Android/Swift CONNECT stages. Both Android protocol phases pass 1,220 checks,
emit nine original graphs each and reject their five existing causal mutations.
The actual Swift producer passes 943 checks and emits its own eighteen graphs.
All 38 shared/Android plus nineteen Swift native parser verdicts pass without
skips, alongside the 172 shared race verdicts. The 57 parser verdicts cannot
substitute for encrypted CONNECT reference traffic or OS-device acceptance.

The execution uses verified Temurin 21.0.13 with the unchanged Java 17 target,
official Swift 6.4.2 on Linux, Go 1.26.3, the pinned native core and prepared Xray.
Its 2,200-input source receipt is
`54418836ef4c28a4f43214770ddb1277671b202d0bb6bfb38830d477e3ee8f7b`.
Source, prepared-native and exported-graph identities are checked before and
after execution. A Linux Swift host result does not establish an Apple SDK
build, signing, notarization or distribution.

## November 12: mandatory installed Darwin ordered-host and public MTU gate

The installed-host acceptance runs twenty independent native cases on Intel
and Apple Silicon: the existing eighteen Linux ordered WG/AWG path scenarios
plus actual public MTU Auto, Cancel and Retest for three-node WG and four-node
mixed WG/AWG paths. The signed installed controller, retained native child,
physical source, encrypted peers, PF journal and utun are real native owners.
The shipping production local transaction is exercised while the public macOS
ordered capability remains gated; the same fixture automatically uses the
public handler after that capability is enabled.

Every case retains complete captured node/source identities, selected Home DNS,
actual per-prefix encrypted traffic, native heartbeat and the original joined
Stop/workspace receipt. Incorrect middle keys or AWG parameters, incorrect
proof/DNS, changed source and lost-prefix failures must reach their intended
boundary and clean up. A monitor's historical held PF receipt cannot substitute
for independently observed PF absence and unchanged kernel tunnel inventory
after public Disconnect.

The MTU cases use the actual installed optimizer and signed owner utility,
with a separately captured final-node UDP sink and actual byte counters. Auto
must adopt a measured winner. Retest reaches a deliberately held benchmark;

## macOS ordered child command and original capture identity

The shared native-process launcher now chooses the fixed child command from
the exact captured `macosprocess.Family`: the original empty External family
retains `routervpn-external`, and `ordered-node-chain-v1` selects
`routervpn-node-chain`. Unknown families return an error before parent
admission, dependency retention or image verification. The existing five
captured flag/value pairs are unchanged. `OpenCapture`, original inherited
descriptors, actual child creation, `BindCreated`, the sole waiter and native
cleanup remain the same shipping path.

The shared `macosprocess.NodeChainTransferSHA256` function accepts only a
complete original Selection with the exact ordered family. It hashes the
domain `routervpn-macos-node-chain-transfer-v1`, one NUL byte and the canonical
JSON of all eleven native capture fields. These include the original
session/source/configuration, caller UID, workspace device/inode, engine,
controller, catalog, input digests and family. Parent and child must obtain
that Selection from their retained native Capture after Current succeeds;
the digest supplies no independent admission, liveness or PF authority.

Six portable Go test roots cover 50 terminal cases: three exact command
mappings, thirteen rejected family aliases, cross-capture argument isolation,
one independent canonical digest vector, every original Selection field,
twelve incomplete captures and nine rejected digest families. Reflection
requires an explicit mutation for every Selection field. The fixed vector
was independently recomputed in JavaScript after checking standard empty
and abc SHA-256 vectors; the result is
`b658abcc3717b051b31fb6e61149eef56148b529be19cb8d4e748639a8152634`.
That computation is not execution of the new Go tests.

Source review verified that removing only the small caller changes recovers
the original Darwin launcher bytes; ordinary External arguments are exact.
The native preparer dynamically copies production macosprocess Go files and
includes the new source in its digest. Hosted compilation, the new portable
tests and native invocation remain required. Public ordered-macOS capability
is still closed while child-command and original-session
proof/MTU/retirement integration is completed; this unit does not certify an
operating ordered macOS tunnel.

before the foreign-context mutation. Neither log reported a compilation

`deploy/test_startup_race_groups.py` compiles the actual client race test
binary once and discovers its compiled inventory. All 29 existing focused
roots and 152 terminal cases remain required. The eleven expensive retained-

`go test ./... -timeout=15m` gate and 45-minute job bound remain unchanged.

from the split inventory. Real benchmark names from the compiled listing are

Start Layer: admission correctly returned HTTP 409 while the original
selected-DNS adoption still owned the connection/settings transaction.

while retaining `operationMu`. Connected/path-proof publication starts a
separate DNS worker, so those visible fields do not supply its join receipt.

is no longer running.

tracker and operation locks; the path observer stops; the worker cancels its
scope; only then does `work.done` close. The fixture does not retry its public
request, cancel DNS, disable a monitor, or reserve the transaction itself.

restoration assertion suffix are byte-identical.

shows that `synctest.Wait` returns while the operation is still reserved,
requires the normal temporary admission refusal, and then releases the guard
and joins the original completion receipt. It requires the connection and
DNS result to remain intact. The final Connected assertion reads under the
app lock. The focused race gate includes both this causal case and the
existing twenty-four-direction fixture, alongside all startup cases, without
changing its three-minute Go execution bound or the full-suite inventory.

exclusivity, DNS policy, timeouts and restoration behavior are unchanged.

## SOCKS authentication-downgrade EOF observation

Both standalone Linux engine jobs at `07c96a04` (`130794976283` AMD64 and
`130794976347` ARM64) reached the actual authentication-downgrade negative
case, then failed its peer-side EOF counter. The original client lower-owner
drain had already completed: its connection is removed only after actual
`Conn.Close` succeeds. A later fixture cleanup could close the peer locally
before its independent reader consumed remote EOF; `net.ErrClosed` correctly
does not satisfy that EOF-only proof.

The peer fixture now joins that exact atomic EOF observation after the
unchanged lower-owner drain and before peer cleanup, using the **same original
two-second drain context**. It never accepts local forced-close as EOF. Four
observation scenarios (already observed, delayed, withheld and expired) plus
their parent are mandatory verdicts from the already compiled race image.
The original twelve peer leaves/thirteen verdicts, fifty-one layered verdicts,
all native deadlines and the thirty-second Python-runner budget are unchanged.
The runner's missing/failed/skipped-verdict controls include the new scope.

path and cleanup order; removing only the new join/helper reproduces the
original Go template byte-for-byte. Python/Go/native execution of this
correction remains pending hosted CI, with no local execution claim.

The historical macOS external-path job `130356525080` reported that its
fresh private test root was not accepted by the system trust service before
the bounded command was killed. That log does not identify the exact hung
authorization syscall. Apple's [Big Sur security release note](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-big-sur-11_0_1-release-notes)
documents approval for administrator trust changes, and its [DTS clarification](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/671582)

Swapping the CLI for the same native trust API does not establish approval.
Per-object anchors or opaque forwarding cannot silently replace this gate:
the independent provider TLS, 50-response cancellation, distinct entry/final
proofs and actual PF policy must remain exercised. No trust or authorization
policy was relaxed in this continuation.

## Measurement meaning and ownership

The short live value is the median of three one-byte HTTPS responses from the
explicit speed endpoint through the original native external path. Timing
starts after DNS/TCP/TLS preparation. It is labeled HTTPS, expires in memory,
and does not become ICMP RTT, direct node reachability, a throughput result or
a durable 50-sample score. The selected DNS policy still governs the path.

The Apple, Android and desktop owners retain the session, node source, network, already
proved execution choice, native measurement and MTU lease until workers drain.
They revalidate before displaying a result. Partial, stale, cancelled,
mixed-type and incorrectly attributed responses cannot replace the current
result. Background probes reserve idle MTU ownership atomically with native
Auto/Retest start; explicit Speed Lab retains its existing cancellation and
drain contract. Final release resumes an initial Auto operation deferred by
that exact lease, including after a failed live sample. Explicit MTU Cancel
and replacement owners do not inherit that permission. Android and desktop
values expire after ten seconds; Apple values expire after fifteen seconds.
Desktop manual fifty-sample work takes priority, and live retries pause while
its original worker drains. Deterministic operation identities separate a
short live response from saved measurement receipts; replay cannot promote
one into the other. Each UI validates the exact request again before display.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-APPLE-CANDIDATE-CAPTURE.md

# Apple candidate capture and receipt validation — 2026-11-12

This follows the durable catalog publication component. It adds app-side original
source capture and strict metadata/receipt parsing. Extension and UI adoption are
not enabled by this component alone.

Capture enumerates every durable saved record, binds the full publication digest,
and retains unsupported rows without scores. Eligible rows use the shipping
paired/imported original-source compiler and its pure candidate validator. The
inventory excludes original prefix identities and uses the publication revision;
no caller-selected address, proxy port or synthetic proof is introduced. Only
original WG/AWG packet prefixes are accepted for TCP connection timing.

Receipt validation binds the original request, capture, prefix identity/position,
candidate identity/source and exact 120000ms lifetime. It requires one ready
candidate row, fifty completed TCP attempts, zero failures, complete/drained state,
finite ordered statistics and a trimmed mean inside the measured distribution.
An expired receipt cannot be renewed by reading it again.

`deploy/test_ios_node_candidates.py` passed **46 shipping Swift/shared Go capture
and receipt checks**: original paired and imported sources for all three SS2022
ciphers, unsupported source rows, lazy-prefix refusal, foreign/incomplete/expired
receipts and failed sample counts. It compiles actual Go original-source APIs;
the process bridge supplies only the gomobile boundary. Two causal variants are
rejected: bypassing shared candidate-source eligibility, and accepting a changed
expiry interval. No sockets, native session readiness or signed Apple application
execution are claimed by this source/receipt test.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-APPLE-CANDIDATE-CATALOG.md

# Apple candidate catalog publication — 2026-11-12

This unit supplies the source-lifetime boundary for the retained-prefix candidate
feature. It does not yet enable the extension factory or Performance UI.

The app's private node store now invalidates its protected app-group publication
before each durable record commit. Successful commits publish the exact complete
record digest, including unsupported transports. A failed private write leaves
the old candidate generation invalid. A later successful publication cannot
revive it, including when original record bytes are restored. Publication failure
after a successful private write leaves candidate measurement unavailable while
preserving the successful private-store/RAM adoption result.

The publication carries a persistent epoch and monotonic generation. App startup
also advances it. Candidate capture checks the actual encrypted durable records
against RAM, then checks the live complete-record digest. Each private request
file is created exclusively with mode0600 beneath a mode0700 app-group directory.
PacketTunnel will read the same helper and compare original publication bytes,
request bytes, device/inode and nanosecond modification/change timestamps. An
identical-byte replacement therefore invalidates an admitted request. Cleanup
refuses to unlink a replacement source. The helper rejects symlinks, non-regular
files, foreign ownership, oversized inputs and unsafe request names.

`deploy/test_ios_candidate_catalog.py` executes the shipping publication helper
against real files and the shipping private commit method with only the private
store write and app-group location substituted. It covers old/new/reverted source,
unsupported-record changes, failed writes, replacement and stale cleanup,
symlinks and private permissions. Two causal variants fail as required: removing
request-file identity comparison, and moving publication invalidation after the
private durable write. Linux SHA256 uses the existing OpenSSL-backed CryptoKit
shim; this is not signed iOS/app-group or NetworkExtension acceptance.

The existing `test_ios_node_store_transactions.py` executable store/model suite
and `ios/RouterVPN/test_private_json_store_contract.py` also pass.

Extension factory lifecycle, exact receipt validation, and Performance display
remain separate follow-up units. No candidate TCP timing or live Apple acceptance
is claimed by this publication-only component.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-APPLE-CANDIDATE-PERFORMANCE.md

# Apple retained candidate session and Performance view — 2026-11-12

This unit wires the previously tested catalog/capture/receipt components to the
original PacketTunnel NodeChain and the Performance view. It does not save or
activate another route; next-connection proposal adoption remains a follow-up.

## Ownership and cleanup

The extension registers one original plan/server/source owner before invoking the
actual generated `LibboxRouterNodeChainNewCandidateMeasurement` factory. The
catalog callback checks the original engine generation, plan/server references,
and live protected catalog/request-file bytes and replacement identities. Info
reads the retained plan's existing LaunchInput through the shipping capture
parser; it does not create another plan or WireGuard runtime.

Factory failures retain the exact cleanup arguments even when no handle returns.
Native close failure retains that owner. Cancellation before Open leaves a
registry tombstone so a late provider message cannot start work. Operations use
nonblocking admission to the per-session lock: repeated Close messages do not
queue behind a pending factory or callback. Exact native close acknowledgments
are also published to the protected app group, allowing the app to recover from
a lost provider reply. Those files contain no timing or private source. Bounded
receipt storage refuses capacity exhaustion rather than discarding another
pending owner's only recovery evidence. The app consumes acknowledged receipts.

Original NodeChain teardown invalidates and joins candidates alongside existing
proof, throughput and DNS owners. Failed joins continue through the existing
retained teardown gate. A stale cleanup cannot unlink a replacement request file
or retire another factory slot.

## Performance behavior

The app offers only the active original WG/AWG packet prefixes, then captures all
actual saved sources and compiles eligible candidates once. It holds the parent
MTU lease through native work, displayed results, cancellation and actual close.
Each result requires all fifty TCP connections and exact source/prefix/request
receipts. Valid rows sort by the 10% trimmed mean. Unsupported, failed, changed
and expired rows have no score. Fixed 120-second native expiry is never renewed.
The app polls native status while results are visible, preserving native
reader/proof freshness as well as live store checks. Selecting another prefix
invalidates the operation; other Performance actions cannot overlap it.

## Verification and boundary

- Real-file catalog/commit controls and two causal variants passed.
- Actual shipping Swift/shared-Go source and receipt cases passed (46 checks),
  including paired/imported sources for all three ciphers and two causal variants.
- Actual session/registry and engine request method passed original owner,
  failed factory, repeated failed close, cancel-before-open, late returned handle,
  nonqueued close, source mutation and exact durable recovery controls. Two causal
  variants fail when original owner checking or failed-factory cleanup is removed.
- Shipping async transaction passed foreign epoch, source mutation, cancellation
  after a late reply, repeated failed closes and lost-IPC recovery. Removing its
  exact epoch/owner comparison fails the causal control.
- The complete shipping app controller typechecks under Swift 6 with OS/store/UI
  declarations substituted; the SwiftUI source parses. Generated ObjC callback,
  factory, handle and scoped-cleanup signatures were checked against the actual
  gobind output. The original NodeChain has no Metadata method; Info uses its
  real LaunchInput API.
- The complete engine compiles with actual candidate session/publication source.
  Its existing ordered teardown suite passed 30 lifecycle checks and all three
  original causal variants, plus existing proof-cancellation and ordered
  measurement-delivery checks.

All four candidate test scripts are mandatory in the existing Apple shipping
runtime-contract gate. Linux execution doubles the Apple SDK/native-handle
boundaries and uses the existing OpenSSL SHA256 shim. These results do not claim
signed iOS NetworkExtension, actual mobile TUN traffic, or Apple SwiftUI SDK build
acceptance; those remain hosted build/native gates.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-APPLE-CANDIDATE-PROFILES.md

# Apple candidate timing to a future connection profile

This unit adds explicit future-profile preparation and saving to the retained-prefix Apple candidate view. It does not load the profile, edit linked node records, or change the active connection.

## Original source and ownership

Preparation starts from the original connection's captured launch input and selected final profile. The candidate must still have the exact member input that supplied its timing. The complete proposed graph is compiled through `IOSNodeChainCapture` and the shared Go compiler. Each retained prefix member's input and private identity source must match the original launch bytes.

A paired candidate replaces the suffix after the selected WG/AWG prefix. An imported candidate is admitted only after the first packet prefix and retains the original paired final node. The latter also requires exact original final profile, selected DNS policy, Shadowsocks assets and WG identity assets; a changed saved final cannot silently substitute a new policy. All three imported SS2022 methods compile through the original paired AES-256 final.

The existing shared compiler permits only an AES-256 SS2022 paired final. A measured paired AES-128 or ChaCha20 candidate therefore retains its valid TCP score but receives a clear future-profile refusal. This unit does not widen that native graph boundary.

## Adoption and persistence

The original in-memory score token, fixed receipt expiry, current catalog/source files, original connection/session and selected prefix are rechecked before preparation, after fresh native ownership observation, and immediately before atomic profile persistence. Selection generations reject late preparation or saving callbacks. Expiry and cancellation clear prepared proposals. Concurrent idle ownership observations are serialized with a bounded wait; native deadlines and cleanup ownership are unchanged.

The persisted record uses the existing complete connection-profile schema, with all ordered references, source kinds and per-node preferences. It contains no node credentials or private assets. ## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-DARWIN-LATE-OBSERVATION.md

# Retain Darwin native diagnostics through joined close, 2026-11-12

The macOS physical socket job [130883815005](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/43127680035/job/130883815005) at source `ab6c3609` failed `TestDesktopDarwinGuardianKernelSocketRetirementReusesCapacity` at sequential socket 19 after 74.98 seconds. Its first recorded loss was `control-receive-probe`, with `observed_ms=1794448153507`, `lost_ms=1794448156930`, `age_ms=3423`, and the idle/no-pending-frame error. No bounded native observation was printed. Those facts do not establish which native readback command or scheduling stage caused the probe to miss its deadline.

## Reproduced missing diagnostic

The failure fixture already reads observations before cleanup and after broker drain. However, successful policy Close closes the observation reader during broker drain. If the independent native cancellation observer reports after the initial trace, the final trace attempts to read a closed file and silently loses the bytes.

The existing executable observation regression omitted this actual close call from its modeled broker boundary. Adding the exact shipping `closeObservation` method and invoking it after the actual observer writes to the actual pipe reproduces the loss: the expected after-broker-drain observation is absent. This is a diagnostic lifecycle defect independently of the original native timeout's cause.

## Repair

Policy close now retains at most the existing 16 KiB read bound before closing its original reader. A synchronized diagnostic read consumes those final bytes once after close; repeated close preserves the unread snapshot and repeated read cannot replay it. The original nonblocking single-write reporter and full-pipe drop behavior remain unchanged. No observer can refresh Current, supply a permit, replace source ownership or alter any operation deadline.

The fixture uses the policy's bounded diagnostic read. Its executable regression now includes the actual close method and proves late delivery through the real pipe and cleanup stack. A mutation discarding bytes before close reproduces the missing snapshot; removing the final trace leaves unread retained evidence; removing the native observer and blocking the output pipe retain their existing causal failures. Original probe failure remains a failure in all diagnostic variants.

The two focused guardian runner tests passed in 8.569 seconds: all six observation variants and all four SOCKS cleanup-order variants execute real Go race-enabled subprocesses. `git diff --check` passed. This proves bounded diagnostic retention, not macOS PF acceptance or a fix for the original timeout. The native/probe/control/proof-age deadlines remain unchanged at 2/2/3/5 seconds. A current-source macOS run remains necessary to attribute the native timeout. Publishing this source change triggers the existing macOS physical socket workflow through its normal path filter.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-MOBILE-CANDIDATES.md

# Mobile retained-prefix candidate bridge

## Public contract

`RouterNodeChainNewCandidateMeasurement(plan, server, prefixPosition, inventory,
catalog)` returns a `RouterNodeChainCandidateMeasurement` bound to the original
`RouterNodeChain`, command server and proof reader. Inventory is the shared
schema-1 `NodeChainCandidateInventory` JSON, including its monotonic host catalog
revision and exact original source inputs. The underlying shared compiler admits
only literal, unlayered SS2022 candidate transports through a paired WG/AWG
prefix. No arbitrary destination or public dial method is added.

The required `RouterNodeChainCandidateCatalog.CurrentInventorySHA256()` callback
returns SHA-256 of the exact **current** inventory bytes. The host must observe
its actual stores/source files, original connection/server ownership and catalog
revision; returning the factory's copied digest is insufficient. Every mutation
advances the revision, including changing away and back. Unavailable source or
ownership returns an empty digest. The host must check this live guard again
before displaying/adopting a result. Host callbacks must not retain store locks
across native calls or reenter native ownership locks.

The handle exposes `Metadata`, `CaptureSHA256`, `Start(request,candidateID)`,
`StatusJSON`, `Cancel`, `Drain`, `Close`, and `NetworkChanged`. Results retain the
shared explicit TCP-connect label, complete fifty-sample requirement, captured
prefix and candidate identities, and expiry. They are not ICMP measurements or
candidate credential/private-node proofs.

## Lifetime and exclusion

An idle candidate handle may coexist with an idle hop measurement handle on the
same original chain. Both acquire the existing `measuring` activity hold, which
also excludes MTU mutation. No new native Box, WG identity or TUN is constructed.
An authorized MTU proof-reader replacement invalidates the old candidate handle;
the host closes it and creates a fresh handle against the current proved owner.

Live host catalog observations have the existing 1.5-second observation bound.
Only one foreign callback can remain outstanding per handle. A timeout retains
that exact callback for joining; it cannot silently become an unowned background
request. Measurement activity release waits for the actual callback to finish.
Status cannot certify drain or expose a completed result while callback work
remains. Bounded close uses the original caller deadline and retains the failed
join handle for retry. Closing a candidate alone preserves the idle hop handle;
original chain/network retirement invalidates and joins candidate ownership.

## Validation boundary

The native bridge fixtures execute original shared source parsing, all prefix
HTTP authentication, and public TLS proof with explicit fixture trust. Their
native routing/OS boundary is doubled. The positive path connects fifty real
loopback TCP sockets through the retained route adapter. Negative cases cover
foreign command servers, duplicate handles, catalog mutation, network changes,
slow foreign callbacks, repeated observation while a callback remains pending,
and shared MTU ownership through canceled worker drain.

This unit does not claim encrypted native candidate-path, Android NDK, Xcode,
package or device acceptance. Independent native peer and host UI adoption gates
remain required.

## Failed construction and eligibility

`RouterNodeChainCloseCandidateMeasurement(plan, prefixPosition, originalInventory)`
retries cleanup after a factory error left a late host callback retained on the
original plan. The host keeps the original arguments, session and parent lease
until this cleanup acknowledges drain. Exact capture matching prevents a late
cleanup from closing a replacement candidate. A missing slot acknowledges that
no candidate remains. This API follows completion of the original factory call;
host cancellation must still retain and join its in-flight factory operation.

`RouterNodeChainCandidateInputSupported(input)` returns only a boolean from the
same shared source compiler used by plan construction. It exposes no address or
credentials. Unsupported rows stay unscored; mutations to those rows still
advance the host's complete catalog revision and invalidate captured results.

Executed validation:

- All 14 original and new `TestRouterNodeChainBridge*` roots pass in the actual
  pinned libbox package with the race detector and the shipping
  `with_quic,with_wireguard,with_gvisor` tags: 2.259 seconds.
- All seven shared candidate roots, including paired/imported three-cipher
  eligibility and hostname/layer/UDP/oversize refusals, pass under race:
  5.823 seconds.
- Seven exact native preparation/ownership regressions pass.
- Shared and native chain files use the official preparation mapping; the
  scoped source inventory has 483 records. The surrounding dependency tree is
  the previously pinned mobile preparation, not a claim that all current
  desktop/native source families were revalidated by this mobile-only unit.

Actual SagerNet gobind v0.1.12 generated Java and Objective-C bindings from the
prepared libbox package successfully. Generated Java exposes:

```java

void routerNodeChainCloseCandidateMeasurement(
    RouterNodeChain plan, int prefixPosition, String inventory) throws Exception;
```

The generated Objective-C signatures use `int32_t` for position, the

# Original native Box teardown receipt

Apple ordered Server/Compare adoption needs to distinguish the start of native teardown from its completed result. The pinned Box closes `done` before closing its managers and TUN. The pinned daemon also removes its instance from the service slot before closing it, and previously discarded the returned close error. Neither observation proves that the original reader has joined.

## Narrow source change

The generated native owner adds `Box.RouterVPNCaptureCloseReceipt()`. Its opaque receipt is bound to the exact original Box. `JoinContext(ctx, originalBox)` waits for the original complete `Close` call to return and reports its retained error. An unstarted close, another Box, an expired caller, a duplicate Close, or the early `done` signal cannot supply a successful receipt. A panic never publishes completion. The original manager-close body is preserved, and duplicate Close keeps the existing `os.ErrClosed` behavior.

The daemon's exact pinned `CloseService` body now returns the original instance-close error and publishes its existing fatal status on that error. A successful close retains the existing idle transition. The strict preparer accepts only the complete original or complete owned daemon method, rejecting partial changes. Its existing native source inventory includes the new receipt and test templates.

The official native preparation completed on fresh clean local clones at sing-box `1ac1a339cb1223e9c70eae14c44411c75033c02d` and Xray `50231eaff98ccc31b5cbd247a721c16e97fe5ec1`, using this source unit based on `0edf2d05b0c063bf079f8f2f189b3b81becfdee4`. No tidied dependency guard was bypassed.

The native owner suite executes the actual pinned Box close and actual managers. Its explicit reference monitor has a complete Close implementation, and a held internal service exposes the real early-done/late-join interval. Both successful and failed original close results are checked. The complete owner inventory is now 14 roots and 28 verdicts; existing discovery, actual graph substitution, selected DNS epoch, application gate, failed acquisition, restoration and original managed-outbound cases remain required. Two new causal controls remove the actual join or discard the original close error; neither compiler failure nor a race counts as their expected rejection.

Nine preparation tests include an executable regression using the entire exact pinned daemon method and substituted service/native-instance boundary types. The discarded-error mutant must reach its specific runtime assertion. Six native verdict/inventory tests preserve omission, wrong failure and incomplete-child refusals. Windows ARM64 omits only the unsupported Go race flag in that portable daemon fixture, using the effective Go target; its real positive and causal test remain required.

Executed results: all 14 roots / 28 native verdicts passed with `-race`; both new native causal controls reached their exact intended assertions without a race or build failure. The strict native source digest remained `577549b0be4270fc91bf7b45a1b010f18e655e459d76f95e948ac338de17cf5e` before and after execution. All nine preparation and six verdict/inventory tests passed, including the compiled daemon error control. The five preexisting native causal controls remain in the mandatory runner; they were not needlessly repeated for this separate close-receipt unit.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-OPENVPN-NIL-DIAL.md

# OpenVPN concrete failed-dial ownership repair — 2026-11-12

## Observed failure and boundary

Windows AMD64 WFP run 43143660168, job 130936812106, source
4477b8f1c6858ef66172289eb8a75a73d3f5e9bd failed the TCP
`successor-and-original-restore` case. The native external engine attempted normal
failed-carrier cleanup and panicked in `gonet.(*TCPConn).Close` at a nil receiver.
The pinned OpenVPN `stackDevice.DialContext` returned the concrete
`(*gonet.TCPConn, error)` pair directly as `(net.Conn, error)`. On failure this
boxes a nil pointer into a non-nil interface. The same conversion exists in its
UDP dial and packet-listen methods.

The owned preparer now tests each concrete pointer before interface conversion,
returning a nil interface and the original error when the pointer is nil. It
preserves any actual non-nil carrier and its error. No outer cleanup error is
suppressed; no production deadline, ownership check, or WFP case is relaxed.
The exact pinned source blob remains
`9a0bd5edd56c4ef64f8d8ae335e2a6dfe4d921dc` at core
`1ac1a339cb1223e9c70eae14c44411c75033c02d`. Preparation accepts only the original,
the previous owned delivery-drain projection, or the complete new projection;
partial dial patches and foreign changes are refused.

## Actual pinned-stack reproduction and validation

A copied prepared core was used without changing the released original tree.
The official OpenVPN stack policy prepared the changed source and existing owned
fixture. This is scoped evidence for this pinned source projection, not a new
whole-core current-head source receipt or Windows WFP acceptance claim.

The new native fixture uses the actual gVisor/OpenVPN stack. On the prior source:

- Cancelled TCP dial returned a non-nil `*gonet.TCPConn` interface and
  `context canceled`.
- Removing the actual NIC while retaining the original configured source made
  TCP bind return a non-nil `*gonet.TCPConn` interface and `bad local address`.
- UDP dial and packet-listen returned non-nil `*gonet.UDPConn` interfaces with
  `cannot assign requested address`.
- The live UDP carrier control passed.

All four negative cases failed the nil-interface assertion on the old source.
After preparation, all five cases passed. The existing delivery-drain and live
capacity/cancellation roots also passed unchanged: three native test roots,
`-race`, **1.025s**. Command:

```sh
go test -race -p=1 -mod=readonly -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 \
  -tags with_openvpn,with_wireguard,with_quic,with_gvisor,routervpn_openvpn_remote_test \
  ./transport/openvpn -run '^TestRouterVPNOpenVPNStack' -count=1 -timeout=30s -v
```

The three preparer tests passed, including exact-pin enforcement, upgrade and
idempotency, each partial dial-patch rejection, foreign-source drift, and symlink
refusal before mutation. The existing remote OpenVPN runner already selects all
`TestRouterVPNOpenVPNStack` roots, so this regression joins its mandatory native
execution without an optional skip.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-OPENVPN-PROVIDER-PORT.md

# OpenVPN native provider port discovery, 2026-11-12

## Observed hosted failure

The Windows native external OpenVPN job [130886896340](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/43128208479/job/130886896340), source `0bd9d0238f615158f8cb9b30c304abb8dc7c04cc`, passed the complete TCP WFP group and UDP on-connect, always, successor/restore, trust rejection and control-key rejection. UDP reject/dns and the following cases failed before provider startup with:

```
routervpn-openvpn-provider phase=provider-port-reservation class=syscall errno=10013 network=udp4 operation=bind
routervpn-openvpn-peer phase=provider-serve class=test-failure
owned OpenVPN provider startup exchange failed owned OpenVPN provider lost bounded reply
```

The current fixture still selected an ephemeral TCP port and attempted to bind UDP to that same number for every provider. A TCP allocation does not establish that the same UDP port is usable. Microsoft documents that [dynamic client port ranges can differ between TCP and UDP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock/nf-winsock-bind), and [exclusive socket ownership can produce WSAEACCES](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/windows-sockets-error-codes-2). The log establishes the cross-transport probe failure; it does not identify which external Windows reservation owned that number.

## Repair and controls

The test provider now discovers its ephemeral port using the original captured provider transport only. UDP binds UDP port zero; TCP binds TCP port zero. The original unavailable TCP fallback remains independently reserved and owned on Windows. Distinct port-number checks and the existing native provider bind-collision handling remain. Selected-protocol access errors propagate immediately; they are neither retried nor converted into an available port. No production socket policy, timeout, WFP rule, rejection case, or negative control changes.

The new native test has eight mandatory verdicts covering both actual TCP/UDP allocations, unselected-transport refusal sentinels, immediate selected access-error propagation and unknown-transport rejection. The Windows witness invocation now requires all eight. The runner executes the exact current Go allocator and native test bodies in a race-enabled subprocess. A forced TCP selection for UDP fails the unselected-transport sentinel; hiding access errors fails the error-propagation assertion. The current source passes.

All eight focused `OrdinaryOpenVPNScope` runner tests passed in 6.362 seconds, including actual race-enabled socket tests and both causal mutants. `git diff --check` passed. This local Linux evidence does not claim actual Windows WFP acceptance; the original hosted native gate remains required.
