## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-PREFIX-CANDIDATES.md

# Retained-prefix candidate TCP measurement core

The original August 19 custom-node/map request asks for candidate latency through
the selected prefix. Its source attribution and wider all-device scope remain in
[the November 12 ledger](CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12.md). This unit supplies
the shared captured-source and measurement core; it does not establish native
host/UI adoption, encrypted candidate-path acceptance or complete delivery of
that requirement.

## Captured authority

`NodeChain.NewCandidatePlan` takes an original sealed chain, a prefix position
and the complete original candidate inventory with its host catalog revision.
Each candidate is parsed through the real paired NodeProfile or imported
external-policy compiler. Its literal TCP address and port come from that
validated source. Neither the measurement API nor Start accepts an arbitrary
destination, route tag, credential, replacement engine or WireGuard identity.

The current slice supports a retained paired WG/AWG Fast/AWG Strong prefix and
literal SS2022 candidates with Start Layer Off. All three verified SS2022
ciphers retain their original key lengths and source. UDP-only transports have
no guessed TCP port. A lazy SS prefix cannot claim a destination TCP connection
measurement from its upstream socket establishment; that broader prefix family
requires a different proved measurement capability.

The source hash binds the whole inventory, catalog revision, prefix position,
source/configuration identities and original proof. The host must implement a
fresh `CandidateInventoryCurrentContext` observation; a copied inventory alone
does not prove the current host catalog. Every operation also retains the five
native identity fields, original chain/controller pointer and original reader.
An observed integrity loss revokes this service even if the old value is later
restored. Host revisions must advance across change-away-and-back operations.

## Measurement and lifecycle

Each request chooses only a captured candidate ID and performs exactly fifty
new TCP connection establishments through the original prefix. A failed,
timed-out, stale or incomplete sample leaves that candidate without a score.
The receipt carries complete distribution statistics and the 10%-trimmed mean;
its label is `routed-tcp-connect`, not ICMP, HTTPS response time or candidate
credential/node proof. The source's private address and credentials are absent
from public status.

The existing 90-second request and five-second default drain bounds remain.
The original MTU hold survives cancellation, late dial completion and blocked
socket Close. Public results remain unavailable until actual worker/socket
drain. A successful receipt expires after 120 seconds; repeated reads do not
extend it. A native or catalog change invalidates the receipt before adoption.
No Local/Server comparison scoring formula or selected resolver is changed.

## Executed verification and remaining boundary

- Five hopmeasure test roots passed with Go 1.26.3 and the race detector in
  1.053 seconds. They perform fifty real loopback TCP connections, reject a
  failed subset score, retain late dial and blocked-close ownership, enforce
  receipt expiry and reject forged prefix/target inventories.
- Six shared NodeChain candidate roots passed with the race detector in
  5.477 seconds, including eighteen paired/imported/cipher/prefix combinations,
  exact source and endpoint preservation, all identity/reader/catalog losses,
  twelve invalid-source cases and original MTU ownership through cancellation.
- Those shared tests retain actual authenticated HTTP and public TLS proof
  fixtures while explicitly doubling the native route adapter. They do not
  certify encrypted WireGuard/AWG candidate traffic or a physical device.

Shipping mobile factories, desktop IPC, source-revision adoption, chooser
presentation/sorting and mandatory encrypted native witnesses remain separate
integration work. Other imported protocols, layers and prefix families remain
in the requirement ledger. A safe refusal is not counted as implementation of
those families, and this core is not a claim of a green complete release.

## Independent GTK negative-response fixture

The exact 7be4 Linux job (131596687443 in
[run 43337286034](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/43337286034))
compiled the explicit C guards successfully, then exposed the next real GTK

asserts that its source still has the original accepted flag and complete result.
The production Save guard and existing named-profile/path assertion remain.

compiled with GCC and linked against the installed real JSON-GLib: the corrected
expression passed; the original shallow copy failed the new source-isolation
witness. Python compilation and diff checks passed. The complete GTK widget
sequence still requires hosted execution; this focused library check does not
substitute for it.

The subsequent exact 2bc1dcd3 Linux job (131601452748 in
[run 43338705271](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/43338705271))
completed successfully, including the complete actual GTK/Speed Lab widget

hosted Linux repair check, not the complete release or physical-device gates.

## Checked intervals for ordinary ordered private and public proofs

The Windows prefix investigation exposed a related ordinary ordered-path timing
producer: both paired private HTTP and imported-middle public TLS proofs used
raw `time.Since`, which could publish `Proven=true` with a zero `ResponseMS`.
The ordinary readiness record does not contain this field, so this is a proof
timing defect, not a claim that ordinary readiness has the same prefix-heartbeat
refusal. The separate candidate-prefix investigation remains separately scoped.

`NodeChain.provePrefix` now uses the existing checked `hopmeasure.Interval`.
Windows uses its original checked performance counter. An unavailable,
unchanged, regressing or unrepresentable interval is rejected; no minimum
latency is manufactured. Both original proof branches retain their selected
outbound, identity/source checks, five-second per-prefix deadline and final
native-owner observation, including when clock readback fails. Earlier valid
proof rows remain distinguishable from a later failed operation.

The immutable `d294da4a` plus two-file validation retained 5,094 source hashes.
The corrected two new roots passed all ten root/child records for actual HTTP
and TLS, positive measured intervals, failed capture before target I/O, invalid
completion after target I/O and cancellation. Nine existing elapsed/clock roots
passed all 27 records, including same-tick, regression, changed domains and
integer-range rejection. Six original proof/lifecycle roots had already passed
all 23 records in the first attempt, including wrong identity, DNS, TLS, source,
engine/network substitution, dead-middle retirement and joined cancellation.

That first attempt failed only the new fixture's expectation for `Complete`:
the existing runtime deliberately marks a failed operation terminal with
`Complete=true`, `Stage=failed` and `Ready=false`. Only those new assertions were
corrected. The first log and source are retained; it is not described as an
overall passing run. A separately compiled control that ignores the checked
Duration error failed both paired and imported completion witnesses. Original
production deadlines and lifecycle behavior were unchanged. These are source
and real HTTP/TLS fixture results with an explicit native routing boundary,
not Windows counter execution, kernel TUN, packaged or device acceptance.

## 2026-11-13 — Make Apple target omission controls independent of host inference

The exact-main iOS smoke run 43447497538 at `7049f8e4c475b283ea5f7dae3e3c6c8696c93deb`, job 131960685723, exposed the full diagnostic: the original Apple target probe succeeded, and the omitted-CPPFLAGS control also exited zero for the ARM64 device slice. ## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-TLS-CARRIER-CLOSE.md

# HTTPS carrier cancellation: close the original lower connection first

## Observed failure

Hosted run 43138281697, job 130919154614, source 35d79f3 failed
`TestRouterVPNImportedHTTPSRealityVisionNativeTraffic/off--aes-256-gcm+xor-whitening/cancel`.
The native final had already joined its retained streams and original physical
registry. The later XOR Start Layer owner cleanup returned:

```
tls: failed to send closeNotify alert (but connection was closed anyway):
write tcp4 127.0.0.1:37230->127.0.0.1:36135: i/o timeout
```

The log establishes an alert-write timeout, not which concurrent deadline setter
won that particular schedule. An earlier expired application write alone was
also tested and does not reproduce this alert failure: Go's alert write does not
simply return the stored application-write error. That hypothesis was rejected.

## Repair and scope

A concrete standard-library `*tls.Conn` returned by the captured detour now has
its exact `NetConn()` closed before TLS alert teardown. Both close results are
joined. The existing bounded error-tree classifier accepts only `net.ErrClosed`
leaves; it is unchanged. There is no timeout suppression, arbitrary wrapper
unwrapping, alternate dial, ownership replacement, or deadline increase.

This applies the existing physical-before-cipher teardown order to the TLS
carrier itself. Other connection types retain their existing close behavior.
Unknown TLS wrappers and real lower-close failures continue to fail cleanup.
The native default HTTPS client constructs a standard-library TLS connection;
a buffered CONNECT response can introduce a separate wrapper, which is not
implicitly unwrapped by this repair.

## Executed evidence

The new `TestCancelledOwnerJoinsExpiredTLSWriter` performs a certificate-verified
TLS handshake and an actual HTTP request/response over original loopback TCP.
Its lower writer then sets the actual socket deadline in the past immediately
before forwarding the TLS alert write. It never manufactures an I/O error. The
old implementation fails with the same `closeNotify ... i/o timeout` branch.
The repaired direct-TLS path closes the original socket first and joins cleanup.

Controls preserve an opaque carrier's actual alert timeout, a lower close that
fails without closing its descriptor, and a lower close that returns a timeout
while still open. The fixture independently verifies those descriptors remain
open until its own cleanup. Generic timeout and mixed closed-plus-timeout errors
also remain failures. Repeated Close, cipher release, key erasure, and rejection
of subsequent authenticated writes are checked.

- Complete `internal/startwhitening` race suite: PASS, 11.240 seconds.
- Existing retired-TLS test, new four-scenario real-TLS test, and complete strict
  close-error controls, ten race repetitions: PASS, 1.374 seconds.
- The existing exact native HTTPS cancellation leaf was attempted with captured
  shared source fixtures locally. It stops before traffic with
  `route ip+net: netlinkrib: operation not permitted`. This is not native
  acceptance; the hosted native gate remains required.

The physical macOS follow-up is separate: run 43140152150 at 0f1305a was still
pending/queued when this unit was completed. This change makes no PF deadline or
macOS ownership claim.

## CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12-WINDOWS-ARM-ALLOCATOR.md

# Execute the complete provider allocator regression on Windows ARM64

Windows physical bootstrap run 43143660168 at 4477b8f failed its ARM64 scope
checks before native WFP execution. The actual allocator regression invoked
`go test -race`, and Go returned `-race is not supported on windows/arm64` for
both the unchanged implementation and its two causal mutations.

The runner now asks the selected Go compiler for its effective GOOS/GOARCH. It
omits only the unsupported race flag for Windows ARM64. Every original positive
allocator verdict, both broken allocators, original execution deadlines and
error assertions remain required. Other targets retain the race flag.

Two focused runner tests pass in 3.640 seconds. One executes the actual allocator
and mutations with the normal Linux race build. The other supplies only the
Windows ARM64 compiler-target observation while actually compiling/executing all
three fixtures on the local host without race, verifies all three invocations
occur, and preserves their original timeout/count arguments. This is evidence
for target selection and complete execution, not Windows ARM64 or WFP acceptance;
the hosted ARM64 gate remains required.

## Windows SS-to-Hysteria2 certificate-refusal fixture

Published repair: `81d1523b7c092bf8e6171e08c6babd0fda5a4dee`.

The Windows native WFP run `43120160283` at historical `0e934245` failed in
`hysteria2/reject/final-trust`: the retained peer terminated before sending its
initial receipt. Source comparison found the same fault-admission block still
present in the current tree. Its parent constructed the wrong-certificate
scenario, but the peer rejected the `final-trust` name as unknown before the
actual Hysteria2 TLS refusal could run. The peer now accepts that fixture fault
only for its original SS-entry family with a captured Hysteria2 final.

The regression compiles and executes the actual peer admission block. It
reproduced the old failure, then passed the corrected case while rejecting
missing/foreign final and provider families. Three executable causal controls
reject the original omission and each removed family boundary. The complete
six-test `OrdinarySSEntryScope` group passed in 3.064 seconds. The existing
actual encrypted Windows/WFP certificate-refusal case, required verdicts,
proof counters and deadlines are unchanged and still require hosted execution.

This ledger reconciles the current candidate work with the original user

implemented, or certify a current release or physical device.

## Original requirement and retained meaning

The original user message in **Router VPN Progress Update(1).md**, August 19,
2026 at 20:29:03, lines 3814–3821, requests timings to the other nodes through
the already selected node, repeated as the path grows. The same message asks
for common SOCKS, HTTP and Shadowsocks imports and whole-profile Add, Load,
Delete and Update. The recovered source identity is
`libfile_e1633becf82c8191bc9145f9fee0b865`. The historical audit identifiers
214–224 and 336 are secondary indexes, not a substitute for this original
wording. The broader source inventory remains in the
[November 12 ledger](CONTINUATION-EVIDENCE-2026-11-12.md).

The retained candidate measurement performs fifty new TCP connection
establishments through the original proved WG/AWG packet prefix. It uses the
actual imported endpoint from the original validated private source. A complete
50/50 result reports its distribution and trimmed mean as
`routed-tcp-connect`. It is not ICMP, a proxy authentication check, a TLS
handshake measurement, Mbps, or a fresh path proof. Failed, stale, incomplete or
unjoined results have no score.

The normal expiry, original catalog generation, session, reader, source-file
and cancellation guards remain in force. A changed-away-and-back source cannot
revive an old result. Neither saved history nor a successful TCP result supplies
new credentials, a routing capability, an execution choice or current native
readiness. The Local/Server formula and common external probe target are
unchanged.

## Complete future profile transaction

The five-file desktop profile change is published at `1fdaeea0`. The proposal
retains the candidate's actual SOCKS5 mode instead of labeling it Shadowsocks.
Both connected and prepared Save select the existing typed SOCKS5 compiler;
the original paired/imported SS2022 path retains its generic compiler. The
candidate catalog commits alone do not establish Save for every admitted
protocol.

The subsequent three-file CONNECT addition is published at `658414f3`, on the
actual published `d0b99255` runtime and `1fdaeea0` profile dependencies. It
preserves `http-connect` and `https-connect` separately and routes the same
connected/prepared Save helper through the typed CONNECT compiler. Its schema 4
does not acquire generic NodeChain or paired-node identity. The original paired
final's SS UoT-v2 service declaration and selected Home DNS remain required.
This closes the earlier pending CONNECT candidate Save description for that
bounded graph; it does not admit arbitrary insertion positions or transports.

A candidate result and a complete connection profile have different authority.
The full proposed path must compile from the current original sources before
Save. Its record references the correct private nodes instead of copying their
secrets. A changed candidate source between Test and Save invalidates the
operation; a later explicit Load uses the still-linked current node credentials
and the saved complete policy. Save must not replace the active session, node
catalog or runtime.

Both the connected and the prepared workflow share this requirement. Prepared
Save additionally requires the original temporary owner to have joined and
returned Home to DOWN. The existing profile transaction remains atomic:
publication failures roll back the new record and cannot mutate another
connection or the original catalog.

### Darwin Auto MTU probe ownership

The shipping Python optimizer now binds its private identity HTTP connection
and UDP benchmark socket to the exact authenticated native MTU reader using
XNU `IP_BOUND_IF`/`IPV6_BOUND_IF`, with socket-option readback before connection.
An ordinary Home LAN response cannot replace this tunnel path when protection
is Off. The original MTU capability remains authoritative across a controlled
utun replacement; an already-open probe never retargets a successor. The
optimizer and adoption use that original capability instead of treating an
ambient Home LAN route as the measurement owner.

The original owner is checked around HTTP proof and each UDP measurement
round. A changed identity/index/MTU, retired operation, refused binding or
incorrect readback rejects the result. HTTP has a preconnected literal socket,
bounded body, no proxy and no redirect. Native checks run outside the recorded
RTT/throughput intervals. Existing candidate selection, rollback, operation
timeouts and Linux/Windows probe behavior are retained.

HTTP/UDP implementation, omitted socket readback and acceptance of a replaced
reader. Socket and native-owner boundaries are explicitly doubled in the
portable probe suite. Actual XNU binding, private-peer Auto/Cancel, the new
paired macOS host and complete exact-SHA release acceptance remain separate
mandatory native work; these results do not claim physical-device acceptance.

   [run 43700305208](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/43700305208):

   release execution remains separate; the five-second proof deadline and
   ordinary retransmission policy were not relaxed.

   all six baselines and 39 of 43 compiled controls before the combined

## CONNECT entry execution and private server pairing foundation

This unit implements the shared execution and server foundation for an
original three-member HTTP/HTTPS CONNECT graph: the paired WG/AWG entry,
the independently captured imported CONNECT member and a paired Shadowsocks
2022 final node. It preserves the original schema-four CONNECT source instead
of converting it into a generic packet graph or substituting a synthetic
WireGuard middle. Explicit typed constructors and observers retain the exact
source pointer, original proxy credentials, HTTPS name, selected DNS and
session owner. Generic schema-one/two constructors remain closed to this
source family. The initial server suffix uses the final node's independent,
key-bound UoT-v2 declaration and requires its final Start Layer to be Off;
broader layer/graph combinations remain requirements to implement.

Local/Server/Compare preparation uses the existing owned runtime, lease,
measurement and proof lifecycle. Restoring a proved choice retains that
choice and does not rerun Compare: Local performs no acquisition PUT, while
Server acquires one fresh owned lease. The original observer and public-host
measurement authority are retained. Native CONNECT construction, sockets,
registry factories, half-close and teardown distinguish Local, Server and
SOCKS owners. Pre-close validates the original source and instance, joins
owned raw connections and refuses stale/mixed constructors. Removing the
Local-on-execution guard fails the intended negative case.

During integration, a real paired-path regression was found at the optional
physical-proof call site: a typed nil pointer passed through the newly sealed
interface became a non-nil interface and correctly failed validation. The
call site now declares the sealed optional interface directly. No typed-nil
exception was added to the validator. The original paired desktop test
passed on the baseline, failed with the intermediate source, then passed
with this correction. Those three observations and the retained original
source are recorded separately.

### Operator and generated runtime integration

The router agent explicitly dispatches schema four through the typed CONNECT
server compiler. Private registry readers still authenticate the original
paired entry and reject foreign node/public-key identities; they do not
borrow the imported proxy's credentials as the paired entry identity.
The pairing script accepts the corresponding exact three-member plan with
two suffix members and preserves canonical source digests, bounded private
files, atomic staging, original inode checks and rollback. The operator
instructions identify the literal proxy endpoint, HTTPS verification,
independent final UoT-v2 declaration and current final-layer boundary.

Shipping native preparation registers the actual CONNECT factories and

## Independent imported interiors in Server and Compare

The schema-six foundation now has production worker, native Box, mobile-host
and desktop-host adoption for its supported paths. A paired packet entry can
retain independent literal Shadowsocks 2022 imports at interior positions,
with supported paired packet hops between them and a paired Shadowsocks final.
Every import retains its own original credentials and Start Layer Off. The
existing two-to-eight-member capability bound still applies. A custom imported
entry uses its distinct schema-seven Local implementation; this change does
not grant it Server or Compare capability.

The actual native construction retains the original preparation, per-position
Shadowsocks clients, managers, resolver and selected route. Desktop construction
also retains its original platform-specific physical owner, command capture,
reader and MTU transaction. Missing, copied, reordered or changed owners fail
closed. The worker derives its sparse paired packet key positions from the
same original inventory instead of treating imported credentials as packet
keys. Provisioning validates this typed source before writing private files.

Android and iOS use the typed native CommandServer constructor, preparation
and saved-choice factory. Windows, macOS and Linux enable the selected editor
path only when both the controller and every imported profile advertise the
specific capability. The generic execution capability cannot grant access to
this family.

Selected hop measurements carry the exact native seven-field capture, including
the original Local source identity and complete ordered imported-position
inventory. The UI and saved history preserve the actual Local or Server winner,
target, generation, labels and each source seal. The original measurement must
prove retirement while the MTU owner is still held before its receipt can be
saved. A saved Compare choice reopens that winner without rerunning Compare.
The legacy six-field capture retains its previous restrictions.

Repeated serialization of large immutable source strings exceeded the existing
mobile measurement admission budget. The original digest is now reused only
when every originally hashed scalar, string and copied short inventory still
matches. Mutable provider maps are freshly compared against independent decoded
copies. A copy can enable this comparison only if encoding it reproduces every
original byte; unusual numeric spellings, integer rounding and different Go
value types retain the original serializer as the fallback. Object keys, array
order, signed zero, nil versus empty values and every originally sealed scalar
remain significant. Live native and desktop physical ownership is freshly
validated. Authorized mobile projections and the final desktop physical
projection capture their own canonical snapshots after resealing. Changed-input
checks require the same digest behavior and refusal as the original serializer,
including values whose initial encoding cannot survive decoding as a
floating-point number. No product deadline was increased.

The desktop construction additionally consolidates repeated static checks into
one fresh complete validation per call, retaining the original preparation,
physical policy, source and native graph pointers plus the exact derived
configuration and metadata. Actual native observations remain bracketed by
their original source checks. An already-validated multiple-import family no
longer repeats the unrelated absent SOCKS and CONNECT family checks. Its
desktop preparation snapshot independently copies the mutable metadata
prefixes and roots, and saved-choice reconstruction refreshes that snapshot
only after the original final reseal. Changed owners, metadata and saved
choices still fail the original canonical validation.

The ordinary selected desktop packet path also keeps independent snapshots of
its original, derived and local graphs. The fast comparison retains every
original per-node position, source, mode, profile identity and proof identity
check. In particular, a Go named-string value can encode to the same JSON as
an ordinary string while failing the original runtime identity lookup; all
three such substitutions must still fail. Eighteen equivalence and changed-
input cases pass under the race detector, and removing the restored identity
checks reproduces all three failures. This optimization applies only to the
original ordinary desktop packet preparation and changes no capability or
timing limit.

An additional failed-measurement bug was reproduced: a nil concrete shared
measurement was converted into a nonnil interface and retained as a close
obligation. The bridge now normalizes that exact absent result; real partial
owners remain retained and must finish cleanup before another measurement.

## Candidate timing through the selected packet prefix

The retained Server/Compare runtime now constructs candidate plans through the
same independent-import source registry. The chooser preserves the actual
packet positions, including packet hops after an imported transport. Every
candidate measures fifty TCP connection establishments. An imported proxy may
carry that route, but its lazy connection is not relabelled as a packet stop.
The original requested execution and selected winner remain unchanged; this
measurement neither repeats Compare nor replaces Last.

The Android and iOS app/host paths retain the exact original source, native
CommandServer, selection epoch, target inventory and entire proposed future
path. Their existing ordinary, SOCKS, CONNECT and OpenVPN owners keep their
separate capability rules. The desktop chooser preserves sparse positions and
allows an idle dialog to switch from a saved-prefix test to a connected-prefix
test. An active test or pending cleanup retains its existing dialog owner.

The desktop parent uses a two-stage native exchange. Prepare captures the
original selected publication and full source inventory; only the original
child can provide the live candidate capture. Start binds the exact published
metadata bytes and catalog generation. Results are considered only after the
original request has been consumed and every worker has joined. Source,
metadata, pulse, request and cancellation cleanup retains the producer's file
identity. A replaced file is preserved and keeps cleanup pending until the
original retirement can finish.

The child stages a result and publishes it without replacing an existing
receipt. It retains that original result's identity and bytes through cleanup
retry. The parent checks that the request has been consumed both before and
after reading a result, so a provisional result cannot be adopted while the
child still owns the request. It removes the original result only after the
other captured files have retired; a changed or foreign result keeps the
measurement pending. Independent controls reproduce both the old publication
overwrite and acceptance of a replaced result when their guards are removed.

Disconnect now recognizes the exact files produced by all three existing
desktop measurement exchanges, including the selected candidate result and
its narrowly defined staging names. Cleanup remains blocked until the native
owner has joined. Four filesystem cases exercise each measurement family and
foreign lookalikes; the original workspace code reproduces the refusal to
retire a valid selected-latency workspace. The corrected race test removes
the captured files and directory before releasing the held MTU transaction.

Candidate grant/status calls now share the selected attempt's lease RPC gate.
Cancellation can return promptly while retaining the original entered worker.
Another grant, status or renewal must wait for that same worker to join; the
authenticated candidate DELETE retains its independent stop capability.
Removing this retention reproduces the original ordering failure. Nine original
lease, proof-clock, renewal, status and cancellation roots pass with 64 distinct
race-test records after the change.

Explicit Save compiles the complete next path with the typed independent-import
constructor. Its policy record supports the same paired entry, independently
captured SS2022 interiors, paired final and supported layers as the live source.
Load verifies the linked original private records and restores the requested
execution without connecting. Imported-entry Server/Compare and other
unsupported shapes remain refused. The new six-root parent component passes
41 exact records under the race detector, including all three selected outcomes,
public Save and cold Load, 21 metadata refusals, pre-construction cancellation,
result replacement and exact-file workspace cleanup retry. The child publications
and kernel are modeled in this parent component;
native connection and physical acceptance are separate gates.

The native builder includes both selected-candidate gates and their complete
source and fixture inventories on every matching desktop host. The parent
runner requires all 41 records and rejects omitted, duplicated, skipped and
foreign records. The child runner preserves its original per-process limits
and verifies the original test image, projected source and private fixture
files before and after each phase. Replacing a file with identical bytes at a
different inode is also refused. All seven child-runner suites, three parent-
runner suites and five existing selected-latency runner suites pass on the
combined source. These runner checks verify gate behavior; actual native
execution and its original timing budgets remain required separately.

The pinned Linux child component subsequently passes all seven required phases
and 28 terminal records under the race detector with one Go processor, after
all performance and typed-identity repairs. Its four fifty-connection cases
finish in 75.19 seconds for Server, 64.24 for Compare retaining Server, 53.20
for Compare retaining Local and 33.25 for the ordinary entry. Eleven refusal
cases, original-generation exclusivity and six publication controls also pass.
A separately compiled guard-removal image fails the exact replaced-inode
assertion, which the strict runner requires. Source generation adds nine
passing records. This uses actual routed localhost TCP and native component
owners with modeled TUN, physical packet and remote-process boundaries; it
does not establish encrypted namespace or installed-device acceptance. The
separate Windows identity-fixture edit above changes the broader preparation
manifest and retains its own platform verification requirement.

## Selected per-hop and final throughput

Server and Compare measurements now retain the original selected execution,
selection epoch, MTU, ordered private members and measurement owner for the
complete throughput operation. Each original hop and the final path transfers
exactly 8 MiB in each direction. The completed result must retain every original
position and its real byte and elapsed-time counters; a partial row, another
selection, an unjoined worker or a stale capture cannot become a completed
throughput result. This operation remains separate from fifty-sample candidate
TCP timing and from choosing or saving a future route.

The desktop parent publishes the request only into its own native workspace.
The child writes the completed selected result through a synced staging file
and a non-replacing link. The parent requires the original result identity and
bytes, the absence of the retired request before and after readback, and exact
cleanup before publishing history. Existing mutable progress files do not
substitute for this completed-result ownership.

The shared source checks transfer 240 MiB across the five-position mixed
fixture and 384 MiB across the six/eight-position fixtures. The prepared native
component adds 144 MiB over all three selected outcomes. Its canonical race
suite passes 11 roots and 55 records, with separately compiled controls that
reject replacement by an identical-byte file, a copied measurement and a
foreign trial. The parent race suite passes 10 roots and 61 records. These
components use actual HTTP traffic while declaring their modeled physical,
TUN and remote-process boundaries.

The mobile facade freezes that same selected capture at the start of its
8 MiB operation and revalidates the original complete transfer before returning
final rates. Progress and cancellation keep their original join information
without exposing partial transfer rows. iOS keeps a scoreless retirement
acknowledgement and rereads successful results only through the same live
native owner; replacing the provider cannot replay an earlier success. The
normally prepared mobile race image passes all three selected outcomes with
144 MiB of authenticated native HTTP traffic. An independently compiled
capture-check omission exposes foreign results and fails the exact required
assertion. Existing failed-close, late-acquisition and shutdown-order cases
also pass. These are native component and host tests with modeled physical
tunnel and remote-worker boundaries, not signed-device acceptance.

The encrypted Linux acceptance inventory additionally requires a sparse
selected-throughput case: four original worker positions, each transferring
8 MiB in each direction, for 64 MiB total. Its strict runner has 32 passing
parser and omission checks, and the real native test image compiles. The local
executor refuses the namespace needed to execute this acceptance case. A
separate userspace encrypted loopback check transfers 48 MiB through actual
WireGuard and Shadowsocks components; it does not replace the required native
namespace result.

## Additional source and lifecycle regressions

The original selected-latency controller could wait indefinitely for cleanup
of a measurement it had never issued after encountering an existing candidate
or measurement lease. Ordinary and selected exchanges now expose the request
only after their original publication succeeds, and the controller enters the
drain path only for an issued request. The regression covers both occupied
mailboxes through the public API, preserving the foreign work and MTU owner
and publishing no score or history. Its race cases and the 38-check Windows
strict-runner suite pass without changing the original deadlines.

The saved imported-path fixture now distinguishes a valid newly captured
positional policy from an attempt to restore changed positions into the
original request. The public Save/Load cases pass for literal imported paths
and retain hostname-interior refusal. Removing the original restore equality
fails the matching causal control. The recovered Speed Lab audit also reads
the selected controller that its predicate actually traces; all 29 checks
pass with the original negative controls preserved.

iOS session identity now recognizes the complete multiple-import schema 6
source, while retaining its private-member identity and exact UTF-8 source
checks. The real Go source compiler and Swift identity/session composition
pass 138 added checks, 1,091 preserved checks and all fourteen independently
compiled source, identity and normalization controls. This closes an app
identity failure that occurred before a valid multiple-import selected route
could be used.

## Full selected candidate trials from an unsaved draft

The recursive candidate interaction now has a separate complete-graph
Server/Compare purpose. It captures the unsaved ordered draft and original
linked sources, starts one temporary selected trial, measures through an
eligible original packet stop, and retains the chosen execution and epoch
until the complete original shutdown. Only then can a measured hop be added
back into the unchanged draft. This does not save a profile, update Last or
turn a temporary test into an ordinary Connected session.

Desktop controllers retain an exact private preparation association through
native staging, platform activation, candidate metadata/results and cleanup.
Cancelled requests that never reached native admission retain their requested
execution but acquire no selected winner. A held child or changed physical
network prevents result adoption. The combined race suite passes the existing
10 roots/61 records plus the separate new 3 roots/21 records on one unchanged
source image. The original compiler, per-test and enclosing gate deadlines
remain intact; the new draft phase has its own mandatory bounded invocation.
The kernel, child process and physical observer are explicit test boundaries.

The Windows, macOS and GTK editors preserve the submitted execution and
complete suffix when adding a measured node. Their executable form and editor
tests cover Server, Compare selecting Server and Compare selecting Local,
including a packet stop after an imported interior. GTK uses real widgets;
WPF and AppKit handles are controlled boundaries in the portable tests.
Rendered native installation and screen-size acceptance remain separate.

Android gives an unsaved selected source a one-use opaque temporary runtime
purpose. Ordinary Connect, Local-prefix construction, restoration and Last
cannot borrow it. The real Java/shared-Go source composition passes 312 new
checks, and the shipping host lifecycle passes 1,094 checks across ordinary,
SOCKS, CONNECT, OpenVPN and multiple-import sources with four compiled omission
controls. Existing connected candidates pass 1,091 checks, the original Local
flows pass 374 checks and 38 controls, and external comparison passes 440
checks and twenty controls after repairing its duplicate compiler fixture.

iOS retains the complete selected draft separately from its original Local
prefix purpose. It disables On Demand before saving temporary preferences,
starts explicitly after readback, and restores the original preferences after
the native session joins. A temporary manager created from original absence
is removed only after its original owner and configuration are verified.
The composed Swift draft flow passes 104 checks and five compiled controls.
The actual candidate-position getter and provider dispatcher are exercised
for all supported source families; original Local and ordinary launch checks
remain required and passing in their independent suites.

At this revision desktop selected draft timing supports the packet-capable
ordinary, Shadowsocks, OpenVPN and multiple-import source families. Its typed
SOCKS/CONNECT selected entry remains an implementation gap. Android and iOS
retain entry position zero for those typed sources and refuse later typed
positions; imported streams and the final path do not become packet stops.

## CI and queue evidence at the starting revision

The GitHub audit found 38 completed workflows at the starting SHA: twenty
successful and eighteen failed, covering 33 failed jobs. The authoritative
[aggregate run](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/44613035097)
contained 59 successful jobs, eight failed, three cancelled and 45 skipped.
An unrelated successful audit cannot substitute for that release result.

GitHub also returned 257 old workflow records as queued. All 257 individual
jobs endpoints returned zero jobs. There were no current in-progress,
waiting or pending jobs. Cancellation was requested for every old record;
GitHub returned HTTP 409, stating that the run had not been queued yet.
A force-cancellation request returned the same result. Those historical
records were not deleted and are not reported as cancelled. They did not
contain allocated or waiting runner jobs at the time checked.

## Remaining validation and implementation

Physical-network inspection is denied for some existing controller fixtures
in the local executor; the tests and product guards were preserved. The
[hosted custom-exit run](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/44966498118)
at `1484f8a901d557801787e5280abd2b17d4a45e60` completed all 2,453 controller
test roots, recording 19,459 passing test receipts and 25 explicit skips for
separate native gates. Its later common-package step failed on the two stale
Android audit markers corrected above. That controller result is not a pass
for the whole workflow or its skipped platform acceptance. Focused source,
compiled-host, race and cross-compilation results describe only the paths
actually checked.

The earlier ARM Darwin ordered-child jobs lost contact with GitHub; the Intel
jobs reached the enclosing one-hour limit. GitHub's annotation for diagnostic
job `137036659402` explicitly records lost hosted-runner communication and
lists process termination, resource starvation and blocked network access as
possible causes. The generated-child fixture exercises a full-host firewall
baseline. The missing terminal logs do not identify which cause occurred or
the exact failing native operation.
The production firewall and release gate remain intact; a successful build
or scoped component test cannot replace full native acceptance.

The supported selected throughput and draft implementations above do not
finish arbitrary protocol, hostname, Start Layer or imported-entry placement,
longer ordered graphs, or complete linked candidate catalogs beyond the current
64-target native inventory. Desktop typed selected-entry timing also remains
open as specified above. The documented graph-position and two-to-eight
capability boundaries remain implementation limits, not user-accepted final
scope. A larger catalog must preserve the original full revision, selected
trial and comparability across its bounded measurements; silent truncation
does not satisfy that requirement.

Final package, image and compose publication must come from one passing
source generation. Physical devices, off-LAN behavior, rendered accessibility,
private server and AI providers, legitimate iOS provisioning, deployment and
ASUS household preservation retain their separate
[live evidence requirements](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md).

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-22-EXTENDED-EXECUTION.md

# Original extended execution and native UI integration — November 22, 2026

This continuation follows the [release repair](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-22-RELEASE-REPAIR.md)
published as source commit `f913197e4340d02ca728ea276008fa7e6c62161a`.
The [current requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md) and the recovered original
requests remain binding. A successful source test, a modeled native boundary,
and an installed device are different kinds of evidence.

## Original extended route

The existing qualified longer Local family is extended to explicit Server and
Compare: an original paired WireGuard entry, independently linked literal
SS2022 interiors, and an original paired SS2022 final, with Start Layer Off
throughout. The source retains the original keys, endpoint identities, private
boundaries, DNS policy, individual public positions and complete node order.
The existing physical traversal ceiling is 96. This does not admit unqualified
protocol combinations or change their existing limits.

The Server lease retains the digest of the complete original route. Its compact
acknowledgement preserves the original 4 KiB request and 8 KiB response budgets.
The original worker still owns the encrypted suffix, fresh authenticated
readiness, private files, final proof and joined retirement. Compare keeps the
existing target selection, validity checks, scoring, final recheck and frozen
winner.

The physical ceiling does not promise a 96-node Server lease. The actual
sixteen-node nonce-bound request is 2,834 bytes and fits the unchanged 4,096-byte
control limit. The corresponding 96-node request is 14,034 bytes; its descriptor
alone is 26,539 bytes and also exceeds the existing 16,384-byte Last limit.
The actual policy/discovery path now checks encoded request capacity before
binding or acquiring a remote lease and returns a precise size error. It does
not publish an unusable 96-node Server/Compare Last. The 96-node construction,
map and history checks below establish those data paths only; native selected
traffic is qualified separately at nine and sixteen nodes.

Capacity checks also cover the genuine ready/IPC representation, staged capture
and grant before acquisition. A matching 24-node source with 128-byte imported
IDs has a 3,954-byte request, but its minimum ready JSON and IPC are 9,001 and
9,095 bytes, exceeding the unchanged 8,192-byte boundary. It is now refused
before lease acquisition; the corresponding 64-byte-ID source remains valid.
No synthetic readiness or enlarged wire budget is used to admit it.

The native preparation exposes the qualified original node count and its
bounded serialized status size. These are construction metadata, not readiness
or traffic authority. Actual measurement still requires the original live
native owner, generation, complete selected projection and frozen choice.

## Public controls and saved data

Android, Apple and desktop controls use that same original family in selection,
profile Save/Load, connected status, measurements and restored references. They
do not turn an ordinary Local capture into a selected execution capture.

The desktop selected latency envelope uses `extended_original_nodes` only with
its complete `selected_capture`. It cannot coexist with `extended_local_nodes`.
The selected capture remains schema six for independent imported interiors,
with every public position, original source digest and actual selected
execution retained. Source-qualified serialization bounds are calculated from
the original count; legacy envelopes keep their previous bounds.

Extended selected throughput publishes `ordered_original_source`, containing
the selected source, configuration, generation, concrete execution and complete
ordered node IDs. GET preflight and POST result must match that object, the
original opaque capture, the live owner and every measured row. Each direction
still requires exactly 8 MiB per node and a real positive duration.

### Startup and current path response

Desktop scheduled Server/Compare connection and Last replay now use the same
protected selected transaction as an interactive connection. Last stores the
original requested mode, proved concrete winner, target, source digests and
member references. Replay requires fresh ownership of the same private
sources and cannot fall through to a new comparison or Local preparation.

The older native compiler included usage counts and measured-history fields
in its source bytes. A successful connection updated those fields and made
the saved source impossible to recreate on restart. The private startup record
now retains an explicit allowlist of those noncredential compiler fields.
They are restored only in the compiler's private copy after current profile
tokens and private files validate. Current device MTU, fixed/manual policy,
Start Layer and credentials keep their original authority. A sixteen-node
Server restart and both frozen Compare winners pass, including changed late
profiles, SS keys, Start Layer, manual MTU and forbidden compiler fields.

The verified new Last is also committed under the original publication guard
before Connected is published. A failed private-store write cannot silently
retain an older winner while claiming the new connection succeeded. The
controlled write-failure case joins the new child, returns to Off, restores
both disk and memory usage records and preserves the earlier valid Last.

Both desktop live-response endpoints previously attempted legacy proof
proxies that the ordered native route did not install. They now request fresh
short private HTTP measurements through the retained native owner. The Map
and Connect consumers preserve their requested sample counts and the existing
ten-second bound. The final reply must authenticate the original private node;
a paired entry also supplies its own private response. An imported entry has
no private API and cannot produce a fabricated private entry reading.

The complete ordered graph, every original profile token, selected capture,
winner, generation, request and MTU owner are rechecked. Completed raw worker
results cannot publish while original native socket or scope cleanup remains
owned. Android and iOS already use fresh authenticated requests through their
retained VPN/PacketTunnel connection for the current full-path value; recorded
prefix measurements remain distinct.

Both desktop handlers now choose their backend from the same captured graph
that their operation validates. A graph change between capture and dispatch
returns a conflict before either legacy proof lane receives an authenticated
request. Positive lane witnesses and ordered-to-ordinary and reverse changes
exercise that boundary.

Windows and GTK had been polling the Connect and Map endpoints concurrently,
competing for that single native measurement owner. macOS repeated the request
in separate telemetry and globe observers and could apply an older callback.
The active route now supplies one fresh, route-bound result to both displays.
Endpoint, sample count, complete route and freshness checks remain; disconnected
draft requests and external public HTTPS retain their separate behavior.

Windows distinguishes an explicitly Off draft from an unknown or changing
route, and does not dispatch two native operations when its displayed route
is absent. GTK's periodic telemetry now retains asynchronous profile,
forwarding and both controller-status reads; it waits for the two same-round
statuses before choosing one measurement. Its original native HTTP worker is
joined before reuse. Selection, mutation generation, all route IDs, endpoint,
mode and expiry checks reject delayed or foreign delivery. Current single-node
RTT is still measured when a multihop draft is saved, and a draft cannot display
an active-path reading.

The generated GTK shell's separate status, Home, settings, protection, event and
diagnostics timers also performed blocking reads. Their periodic paths now
share one retained refresh owner and consume bounded asynchronous responses.
The actual profile-settings response carries the profile ID of its source;
settings, protection and Home cannot borrow another selected profile's data.
Original Stop retry intent, event cursors and action-time authorization checks
remain intact. Shutdown/layout-only execution admits no new telemetry workers,
and window destruction joins the exact workers it owns.

### Complete history within its resource bounds

Repeating a 96-node selected capture in all 96 saved receipts exceeds the old
1 MiB desktop history file limit. Desktop extended history now uses a private
schema-two descriptor table. It stores the complete original descriptor once
and retains every receipt, its actual generation, and the digest of its exact
original capture separately. Reopening reconstructs the capture, verifies that
original digest, and applies the same strict receipt validators. A valid-looking
generation copied from another record cannot relabel the original result. The
public API and legacy schema-one history remain compatible;
the desktop 1 MiB and 128-receipt limits remain unchanged.

Historical matching also compares the complete independent-import descriptor.
Matching visible node IDs alone cannot associate an old result with a changed
public source digest. Missing or duplicated descriptors, wrong descriptor
digests, foreign references and missing generations are rejected.

Android retains its original legacy entry/store budgets and grants additional
serialized capacity only to validated extended selected captures. iOS saves
extended histories by original source and position, preserving each receipt's
generation, winner, atomic publication and rollback. Both platforms exercise
all 96 positions through fresh storage and reopening.

## Map and privileged desktop repairs

The desktop graph's immutable map inventory previously stopped at eight even
when a longer native route was connected. It now retains all original IDs up
to the existing physical ceiling. Its route token includes the complete
inventory and normalizes the connection instant to UTC.

Windows had a second eight-ID rejection, a finite palette indexed without
wrapping, and a loaded getter that returned one nested array. GTK retained the
long IDs but could index beyond its eight colors. Android mislabeled imported
ordered nodes as private Router nodes, hiding their markers and segments.
The actual consumers now preserve complete source-qualified inventories and
the correct node kinds. macOS's globe parser also accepts the complete
authenticated original route, retaining endpoint, uniqueness and route-token
checks. Unknown coordinates still leave a gap.

macOS's privileged journal validates every original saved member for longer
routes, including the exact WireGuard/private entry, literal-SS/public
interiors and private SS final. Its larger private envelopes are bounded by
that inventory; other families retain their original budgets. This also fixes
the earlier journal rejection of multiple independent SS interiors. Saved
protection, IPv6 and Home LAN policy are still checked before mutation. No PF
permission, fail-closed rule or native retirement requirement is weakened.

The shipping macOS candidate HTTP transport had also omitted the draft
endpoints that its editor actually used. Its allowlist now validates the real
draft endpoints and their complete original member IDs, tokens, branch/scope,
eligible packet prefix and body shape. Unsupported SS interiors do not become
packet-prefix candidate owners.

The exact `f913197` Windows ARM64 MAX control job reached its expected native
rejection and completed the owned process-tree join, then failed to remove the
original executable with Windows sharing error 32. Image retirement now permits
only a sharing error during acquisition to settle within a separate, fixed
ten-second file-cleanup window. An original Windows handle denies write/delete
sharing, supplies the original regular-file identity and bytes, and deletes that
same opened file. A pathname substitution cannot redirect deletion. Other
errors, replacement, persistent locking, failed close or an unproved native join
still fail and retain ownership/workspace. No foreign process is terminated.
The native command result, causal verdict and process-join deadlines remain
unchanged. Twenty-four portable retirement/driver checks pass; the four actual
Windows tests remain platform-gated. Actual Windows external-reader
coverage is registered in the required native runner and awaits that source's
hosted execution.

The generated Darwin child runner also had an independently reproduced
reporting stall: optional stage notices could block on a full original stdout
pipe before the native subprocess deadline started, and final error reporting
could block afterward. Optional reporting now respects descriptor backpressure
and restores its flags. The complete native transcript pump, verdict validation,
private receipt writer and protection/retirement rules are unchanged. Fifty-eight
Python checks passed, including actual filled-pipe controls. The unavailable
hosted final result does not establish that this defect caused either cancelled
Intel job; the combined native step also performs preparation, compilation and
component checks before its bounded native command.

The Darwin workflow now gives those original preparations, source controls,
components and native acceptance independent jobs under their existing bounds.
Both processors still require every original phase and the complete native
transcript. The PF/utun job performs its own current-host signed prerequisite
and checks the freshly prepared source against all three original compiled
images before running the actual native harness. Exclusive same-run workspaces
preserve the absolute module-source bytes across disposable hosts. Failed-job
retries can use only valid original producers from the same run and revision,
with matching image and proof retention. These orchestration checks do not
substitute for the next hosted PF/utun result.

Android standalone workflows reached their 15-/30-minute aggregate ceilings
before finishing their full workload. Complete phases/programs are now divided
between independently bounded jobs, with strict required aggregates. The runtime
truth gate retains all 101 original invocations in eight disjoint shards and is
required by both the authoritative source audit and APK job on the same workflow
SHA. Only their duplicated sequential runtime-truth copies were removed. The
original per-test deadlines and required tests remain intact.

The standalone Windows source job also reached its 30-minute aggregate ceiling
after its complete baseline and 40 or 34 of 64 mutation verdicts. Each original
architecture now has a complete baseline phase and two disjoint 32-control
phases. Required completion regenerates the pinned source and verifies the
original case inventory, executable records, architecture, commit and workflow
run. Native protection and recovery keep their eight- and six-minute deadlines,
and the WFP kernel matrix remains a separate required gate.

On `3d1743a`, the Windows ARM64 succession group and amd64 ownership-controls-2

that the entire later release matrix or physical-device acceptance has passed.

## Native follow-ups after `4ac33a9` publication

The next native preflights exposed two narrow Windows test-driver regressions.
The physical runner assumed the unchanged Off-socket bind callback occupied
one source line. Its extraction now accepts the original and normal Go
formatting while requiring the unique original constructor, import, captured
socket and complete bind arguments. All 84 runner checks passed, including
the original compiled UDP4/UDP6 callbacks and both negative controls.

The process-image validator assumed a generated Go test driver always carried
a `.test` package suffix. Inspection of the pinned Go 1.26.3 compiler and an
actual original Windows PE established that this package-main test retains
`router-vpn/cmd/client` as its build-information path. The validator requires
that exact value and the unchanged compiler, native target, race, checkptr,
tags and CGO settings. It also reads all 200 unique original test roots from
the original executable and rechecks file identity and digest before and
afterward. A regular command with the same module metadata cannot satisfy
that inventory. The actual command/test distinction was exercised with the
pinned compiler, and all seven phase tests plus 23 release-gate tests passed.
The original build and execution deadlines remain unchanged; actual Windows
producer and consumer acceptance still belongs to the next exact-SHA run.

A completed Android libbox diagnostic also found an older shared mobile
fixture that expected incompatible SOCKS/CONNECT construction to succeed
before being refused by `Box.New`. The shipping shared-context guard correctly
refuses the second construction earlier. The unchanged fixture reproduced
that exact failure locally against pinned core
`1ac1a339cb1223e9c70eae14c44411c75033c02d`. The corrected test checks the real
nested public construction in both orders, verifies an independently valid
SOCKS original, and combines those independent owners only to test the
additional `Box.New` refusal. Its original instrumented native registries
must still show zero acquisition. All twelve native CONNECT roots and their
subcases, including the TLS sibling, passed with the four original shipping
mobile tags in 1.830 seconds of native execution. The separate build/run took
23.558 seconds. Both Android and iOS packaging execute this template; no
shipping constructor or admission rule changed.

## Release and live acceptance

The exact final source still needs the authoritative native/package/image/
compose workflow and actual publication. Earlier workflow receipts are
diagnostic evidence for their recorded source, not for subsequent edits. No newly
released installer or physical-device acceptance is asserted by this record.

The remaining [live acceptance evidence](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) must belong
to the final released SHA. In particular, source/host fixtures do not prove
off-LAN devices, private production services, applicable Apple provisioning,
production deployment, or ASUS household fail-open behavior.

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-22-RELEASE-REPAIR.md

# Native release repair and verification — November 22, 2026

This change repairs failures observed on source commit
`6498bd53054ed7d733eb5a5694d00a06e2702b2f`. Its
[authoritative Build all run](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/45005915700)
finished with 64 successful jobs, 11 failures, one cancellation and 44 skipped
jobs. Release publication was skipped. The most recent published prerelease
when this repair was prepared still targeted
`745b3e41e5a78d734391976af9b7cd0637660a0b`; that release is not evidence for
this change.

## Repairs

| Boundary | Observed failure and change |
| --- | --- |
| Windows isolated native account | Native source shutdown could block in `NetUserSetInfo` even though preparation had already disabled the account. After independent native readback verifies the same SID and ownership comment, an already-disabled account now needs no second write. Enabled accounts still follow the original write and readback path. Account removal, absence verification, retained ownership after failure and shutdown deadlines are preserved. |
| Windows account regression | The native test retains the real account reader and original cleanup API, but removes the setter only from a local API copy. Repeated quarantine must not call it. Foreign SID/comment inputs must still fail. The causal control accepts only the exact setter call site; unrelated crashes, races, skips, timeouts and failed test-owned recovery cannot satisfy the evidence parser. |
| Windows candidate heartbeat fixture | The fixture used pathname `os.Rename`, which failed while a Windows reader held the previous heartbeat. It now uses the retained directory's `Root.OpenFile` and `Root.Rename`, matching the shipping parent publisher. The immutable source, file identity and live-pulse checks remain required. |
| Darwin CONNECT startup fixture | The shared mailbox-refusal test demanded the ordinary packet-policy field even for a typed CONNECT owner. It now checks the exact retained physical policy and requires exclusive policy ownership, while preserving the no-resource retirement and joined native-owner checks. |
| Windows Hysteria2 Start Layer evidence | A valid benchmark can retain one SS2022 association for all fifty requests. The former test incorrectly required a new association during the benchmark. The peer now counts each successful native SS2022 packet authentication separately. Fresh raw, authenticated and forwarded packet counters, original layer mode/private destination, actual TLS/DNS requests and credential refusals remain required. |
| Windows OpenVPN entry lifecycle | On ARM64, the successor case inherited almost all of a 180-second alarm already spent on earlier starts. Each original entry lifecycle leaf now runs against the same immutable binary with its own unchanged 180-second alarm. Exact leaf inventory, refusal families, causal controls and result validation are retained. |
| Native compiler identity | Imported-trio and physical-controller gates could find an older bootstrap `go` on PATH, then disable automatic toolchain selection before resolving the pinned compiler. They now share the existing exact compiler-identity capture: select Go 1.26.3, verify its root and native host, and bind compilation and `test2json` to that executable before switching to local-only toolchain mode. |
| Android ABI contract | A stale opaque digest rejected the legitimate paginated candidate metadata method. The contract now checks the complete explicit set of nineteen candidate signatures, including `metadataPage(int)`, and separately checks each typed execution factory. Missing, mistyped, duplicate and foreign-owner signatures are rejected. |
| Mobile Go suite scheduling | The growing shared/native suites exhausted a package-wide alarm before later independent tests began. The runner compiles the actual original package once, discovers every selected root from that binary, and validates the actual `test2json` result with independent original alarms. The nine expensive typed-suffix trials are partitioned by whole protocol branch; an exact complement retains every other and future branch, and the combined receipts must contain the complete required inventory without duplication. Android/iOS tags, race settings, linker flags, package selection and product operation deadlines remain unchanged. Other shared packages still execute unfiltered. Preparation digests and Gradle inputs include the runner and its regression. |
| Swift native capture fixtures | Test bridges omitted newly shipping extended-node metadata and private-JSON validation. They now call the actual Go implementation for those operations and compile the shipping receipt/validation sources. The existing independent imported-prefix path is tested through its own selector. |
| Windows profile mutation fixture | The ordered-source adversary now mutates the actual selected fixture profile, so it reaches the shipping ownership rejection instead of a stale lookup. |
| Darwin first-grant diagnosis | The Intel PF failure did not reveal whether its shared caller deadline expired before or after the guardian completed the grant. The existing private, nonblocking fixture observer now records the first Off grant's phase and durations; the caller records its own elapsed time and context error. This changes no PF decision, privilege, permission, connection deadline or production output stream. |

## Verification before the source update

- All 34 combined recovered-requirement, native UI, map-first, profile,
  transaction, household-safety, download-retention and release-orchestration
  audits passed. The orchestration audit also executed its required nested
  publication, provenance and source-safety checks. These are source and
  composition results, not a percentage of the user's requirements completed.
- The Windows identity driver passed 27 cases. The changed native identity
  package compiled for Windows amd64 and arm64 with pointer checking enabled.
  Independent review verified that the new early return follows actual native
  SID/comment/disabled-state readback, and that final account removal still
  requires the original identity.
- The native selected-candidate runner passed eight driver cases. The Darwin
  lifecycle runner passed seventeen cases. The actual extracted startup and
  retirement fixtures passed their original baseline and causal controls.
- The Windows physical orchestrator passed all 83 tests, including actual Go
  test filters and complete result validation. A separate exact-inventory
  check compared the partitioned OpenVPN entry leaves with an unfiltered
  compiled fixture.
- The real SS2022 UDP layer peer passed retained-association datagrams for AES
  and AES with XOR whitening, plus wrong-key, wrong-destination and
  wrong-whitening controls. This is peer evidence; it does not replace WFP
  enforcement on Windows.
- Pinned compiler-selection runners passed their 13, eight and five cases.
  Android workflow validation passed all 34 cases, and the existing actual
  AAR guard passed 62 boundary cases.
- Swift fixtures invoked the real Go compiler/validator: typed CONNECT passed
  1,747 checks and six controls; ordinary CONNECT passed 1,206 checks and three
  controls; SOCKS passed 636 checks and three controls; the ordinary host
  passed 153 checks and five controls. OpenVPN passed 576 checks and imported
  Shadowsocks passed 783, each with four original-capture controls.
- The mobile grouped runner passed its real compiled test-inventory fixture
  and negative controls, and the existing source-group runner passed all 23
  checks. All 35 roots in the actual prepared Android native chain selection
  passed, with 156 distinct passing root/descendant results and zero skips.
  The former eight-hop HTTPS timeout passed in 16.33 seconds. The previously
  timed-out shared independent-final-layer root also passed all nine exact
  subcases with its original individual budget. The complete shared wildcard
  suite remains a separate release gate.
- Darwin readback baseline and causal checks passed, and the tagged package
  compiled for both Darwin architectures. Native PF execution remains a
  hosted Darwin check.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Acceptance still required

The exact new main commit must pass the hosted Windows, macOS, Linux, Android
and Apple build/runtime gates and the authoritative package/image/compose
publication chain. A cross-compile or source fixture does not prove an actual
Windows WFP/account lifecycle, macOS PF/utun lifecycle, rendered WPF/AppKit
interface, or mobile-device tunnel. The previous lost-runner annotations do
not establish a resolved runtime cause.

Source inspection also confirms that the generated Darwin child test installs
the shipping full-host PF baseline inside the same hosted VM as the Actions
runner. Its deliberate fail-closed retention can block that runner's network
control channel if verified cleanup is unavailable. This is an observability
and isolation issue to resolve, not proof of the exact historical disconnect.
A weaker shipping firewall or an artificial Actions-network permission would
not establish the original full-host safety behavior.

Longer Server/Compare paths and still-unimplemented protocol combinations
remain part of the requested work. The existing qualified longer Local
capability does not waive them. Experimental evidence is not presented as
available UI behavior.

The separate [live acceptance gates](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) still require
actual installed-device, off-LAN, visual, private-server/provider, applicable
Apple provisioning, production deployment and ASUS fail-open evidence tied to
the released source. No release-success or physical-acceptance assertion is
made by this source repair record.

## Linked candidate inventories

The ordered candidate path previously either truncated lists at 64 or refused
larger lists. Its native metadata and source resources already have byte
budgets; the row count was an additional restriction. The shared constructor,

Tests exercise 65, 128, 129, 479 and 513 distinct original identities,

The constructor retains the entire original catalog revision and every exact
private input. It still rejects duplicate identities, changed source seals,
unsupported TCP endpoints and oversized native messages. A catalog view does
not create a connection, choose a Compare winner, release a measurement lease,
or authorize a result from another native owner.

- Native observations repeatedly serialized unchanged source graphs,

## Release evidence and remaining acceptance

The previous main build
[44980195829](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/44980195829)
finished with 63 passed, four failed, three cancelled and 45 skipped jobs.
Its release publication was skipped. The separately scheduled macOS physical
socket workflow passed, but the generated-child full-host ARM run lost runner
communication. The original diagnostic retained its pre-PF checkpoint only.

The historical 257 records displaying queued state each have zero jobs. Repeated
cancel attempts report that they are not queued; they are not counted as
cancelled or treated as evidence that current native work is running.

Publication and live acceptance must be tied to the new immutable main SHA.
The authoritative native/package/image/compose gates remain required, including
the hosted macOS generated child, Windows WFP/WPF, Android and Apple builds.
The [live evidence requirements](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) remain separate:
installed-device network behavior, off-LAN methods, rendered accessibility,
private server/provider functions, applicable Apple provisioning, deliberate
production deployment, and ASUS household forwarding/fail-open behavior.
Neither a source audit nor a passing fixture certifies those outcomes.

The subsequent [native release repair record](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-22-RELEASE-REPAIR.md)
documents the failures observed after this source update, their repairs and
the remaining exact-commit native/live acceptance requirements.
