<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-23-native-repair"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-23-NATIVE-REPAIR.md

# Native repair and map follow-up — November 23, 2026

This change follows main `8124eb3b30653493ef61c87ca36709cfe28433bc` and the
failed native jobs from that generation. The requirements remain those in
[Current Requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md) and
[Reconciled Requirements](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md). Source implementation,
controlled executable checks, native platform execution, published packages
and installed-device acceptance have separate evidence.

The subsequent [route measurement and longer paired Local changes](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-23-ROUTE-MEASUREMENTS.md)
record their additional source qualifications and validation boundaries.

## Application and runtime changes

| Area | Resulting behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Android map | A retired ordered session stops its packet animation immediately. Opt-in device location uses monotonic age, expires, rechecks permission and retires its callbacks when hidden or detached. Intermediate hops have position colors; custom nodes retain their outline; routes and moving packets wrap at the date line. The map draws the shared offline Natural Earth outlines and ships their original attribution. |
| Windows and Linux maps | Native cached land geometry, ocean boundaries and graticules use the existing node projection. Date-line routes and packets take the short path. Disconnect and captured-route retirement stop old packets before a later map refresh. Package verification requires the exact shared geometry and attribution. |
| iOS saved routes | Provider reopening binds an independently selected final Start Layer to its original saved credentials, including the paired Hysteria2 final path. Local, Server, Compare and captured candidate-prefix handoffs use the same check. |
| Darwin shutdown | Cancelling the native socket policy wakes its idle guardian immediately. Existing in-progress probes still finish through the original retirement path. |
| Naive engine lifetime | Stream accounting starts before native construction and ends at native termination. Client closure cancels late and already-published streams, joins concurrent close callers, drains admitted socket callbacks and DNS/relay workers, and checks native shutdown before destroying an engine. Failed shutdown retains the remaining handles for retry. The pinned upstream source and checksum verification still bound the derived module. |

## Native verification repairs

Windows ownership controls now run in four bounded groups. The WPF editor runs
in six groups with all 33 original negative witnesses required by its aggregate
validator. No individual test deadline is increased. Socket fixtures wait for
their original operations to settle before taking one strict WFP/kernel read;
the OpenVPN TCP rejection case observes the actual connected descriptor before
its rejected control-key handshake closes it.

Darwin Ready validation requires the parent plus all 20 binding/MTU leaves.
The HTTPS CONNECT retirement fixture distinguishes a clean real credential
refusal from a separately exercised native half-close error. Native command
tests are discovered from the compiled package and partitioned into disjoint
batches under the original race settings and execution deadlines. Failed native
test diagnostics retain the initial fault site as well as the process tail.
Native fatal output is retained even when the process cannot emit a final
per-test verdict. Three older source assertions that required the Android wall
clock now require its monotonic animation clock and current-session guard.

The Android geography test runs independently in the authoritative runtime
shards and the relevant pull-request workflow. APK delivery validation compares
both map assets byte-for-byte with the release source.

## Evidence available before the hosted release run

- Android checks exercised the shipping map and session code through controlled
  Canvas/location boundaries, including complete 9- and 96-node paths,
  retirement, location expiry and date-line traversal. Both map classes compiled
  against Android API 36. AAPT2 packaged the exact geometry and attribution.
- The shipping Windows editor callbacks passed in PowerShell Core on Linux,
  including all six positive groups and 33 negative witnesses. The separate
  profile fixture passed 5,064 checks. The production WFP policy and observer
  compiled for Windows AMD64 and ARM64.
- Swift/Go capture checks exercised saved-layer substitution, provider handoff
  and candidate-prefix rejection. Darwin tagged packages cross-compiled; a
  controlled Go race test exercised the production guardian wakeup.
- Twelve Naive policy tests passed, including eight race-enabled runs of nine
  compiled pinned-client lifecycle tests and ten causal negative controls. The
  native symbol results were controlled; these tests did not transmit encrypted
  traffic through the actual Cronet library. The transformed production package
  compiled for Linux AMD64 with CGO and Darwin AMD64/ARM64 with purego.
- Native delivery/signing boundary checks passed 5,219 assertions. The combined
  map, release materialization, Compose, Windows gate, Darwin phase and recovered
  requirement checks passed. These are not substitutes for native release jobs.
- The composed Linux GTK app and native Cairo fixture compiled. Controlled
  rendering checked inland and water positions, both map sizes, short route
  segments and seven local owner-retirement cases. Windows' composed geometry,
  packet and cancellation functions passed in PowerShell Core. Its native
  WPF bitmap checks are required in the hosted workflow. Both desktop archive
  formats reject missing, changed, ambiguous or oversized map assets.

The broad local Go run was not green: physical-interface inventory was denied
in this workspace, and two large packages reached their cumulative ten-minute
timeouts. The interrupted leaves passed individually. Diagnostic overlays
confirmed that ambiguous observer/child-cleanup failures occurred before any
observer or child was acquired because physical-network capture was denied.

## Release and acceptance

The authoritative [build-all workflow](../.github/workflows/build-all.yml)
must produce and verify packages, manifests, ARM64 images and production Compose
for the same complete source SHA. Real Windows WFP/WPF, Darwin native execution,
encrypted Naive H2/H3 traffic and the prior Linux ARM64 crash outcome still
require that run. [Live release evidence](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) continues to
track installed-device routing, leak protection, off-LAN interoperability,
applicable signing and deployment acceptance. This record does not establish
those installed-device outcomes. Additional route qualifications are recorded
separately in the linked continuation above.

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-23-route-measurements"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-23-ROUTE-MEASUREMENTS.md

# Original route measurements and longer paired Local paths

This work continues the [native repair and map changes](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-23-NATIVE-REPAIR.md).
It addresses two recovered requirements: measure the next candidate through
the previously chosen nodes, and preserve longer compatible routes through
the native editor, saved profiles, connection, measurements and history.

Source qualification, controlled encrypted-peer tests, hosted native gates,
release artifacts and installed-device acceptance are separate evidence.
The [current requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md) remain binding.
The [November 24 continuation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-24-MIXED-PREFIXES.md)
adds qualified ordinary WG/AWG and routed-hostname response prefixes and the
longer contiguous mixed Local source family.

## Candidate measurements through the original prefix

Packet prefixes continue to measure fifty fresh routed TCP connection
handshakes. A qualified Local Shadowsocks prefix can instead measure fifty
authenticated replies from an independently paired candidate's private agent.
These are separate metrics, with separate result kinds and labels:

| Captured metric | What one sample measures | Candidate requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routed-tcp-connect` | TCP connection establishment through the captured packet prefix | An original supported saved endpoint |
| `routed-candidate-response` | Connection and cipher establishment plus the candidate's authenticated private response through the captured stream prefix | Original paired SS2022 credentials, Start Layer Off, node identity and private agent key |

The stream response uses a fresh 128-bit nonce. Request and response HMACs use
separate domains and bind the nonce to the original node identity. The bearer
secret is never sent as the request credential. The server checks the actual
tunnel peer; forwarded-address headers do not acquire access. A reply from a
different node, key or nonce cannot complete the sample. The nonce's freshness
belongs to the original client request; the endpoint does not claim a global
server-side replay cache.

The source, configuration, node catalog, selected prefix, native owner and MTU
ownership remain captured for the entire operation. A lazy stream dial alone
does not produce a response score. All fifty samples, the correct measurement
kind and joined socket cleanup are required. The existing expiry and trimmed
mean rules remain in place. TCP and private-response scores are never pooled.
An imported candidate without an attributable private proof endpoint remains
unmeasured rather than receiving a fabricated node RTT.

Stream qualification is Local, with an original unlayered paired WireGuard
entry, contiguous independently imported literal SS2022 members through the
chosen prefix, and an original unlayered paired SS2022 final. Positions one
through six retain the ordinary source authority. Later positions require the
complete original extended schema-six family: every interior must be an
independently imported literal SS2022 member, every Start Layer must be Off,
and the entire route must remain within the physical traversal bound. A late
measurement cannot borrow authority from a valid shallow prefix when another
member of its captured route has changed.

This qualification does not confer response authority on Server/Compare,
hostname imports, a mixed packet/stream prefix or other Start Layers. The
native capability determines which prefixes the applications offer.

### Choosing a measured final

For desktop drafts, an imported stream at the original penultimate position
can offer **Save profile with this final**. This is an explicit named profile
write. Its complete proposed path preserves every earlier node and replaces
only the original final with the measured paired SS2022 candidate. Home and
the current draft remain unchanged. The user loads the saved profile for a
future connection through the existing profile flow.

The catalog and committed receipt carry `proposal_action: save-final-profile`.
The original request, view token, candidate, path and source inventory remain
bound to the save. A delayed successful write is retained even when Close or
Cancel is waiting for native cleanup. The saved profile ID remains visible
until that original cleanup finishes. Ordinary packet-prefix insertion keeps
its existing separate editor action and ownership checks.

iOS retains its existing complete future-path proposal and recompiles it from
the original sources. Single-import and multiple-import preparation must reopen
with their own exact native source family; one family cannot borrow another's
sealed launch record.

## Longer paired WireGuard Local paths

The additional extended family uses an original schema-one paired source at
every position, standard WireGuard at every prefix, and a paired SS2022 final.
Every Start Layer is Off and execution is Local. Original node identities,
private keys, endpoint targets, profile tokens, source digests and the complete
order remain independent and captured. This does not broaden the existing
ordinary protocol combinations or the separate imported Server/Compare family.

The original physical traversal bound remains 96. It is a resource and input
bound, not a promise that an arbitrary route can carry packets at a given MTU.
The native compiler must prove the complete nested packet envelope. Captured
MTU, native readback, rollback and final DNS/identity proof remain required.

Controlled encrypted-peer tests exercised nine total nodes at MTU 2000 and
sixteen total nodes at MTU 3000, including 64 KiB upload and download, final TLS
and DNS, all prefix identities, authenticated MTU, wrong late-prefix credentials
and wrong final credentials. The sixteen-node route at MTU 2000 was correctly
refused. These tests do not establish a suitable MTU on an ordinary WAN, an
installed TUN session or physical-device acceptance. Larger source/editor
fixtures establish preservation and bounds, not encrypted traffic at every
possible depth.

Late packet-candidate measurement requires the sealed original extended Local
plan. A sixteen-node source exercises closed-prefix preparation at position
eight and fifty routed samples. Ordinary unsealed callers retain their
existing position bounds.

### Complete profiles, results and history

Editors and Save/Load retain every node and source token through the entire
qualified path. A changed late member, wrong family, unsupported layer,
Server/Compare substitution or over-bound source cannot reuse that capture.

Extended Local latency inventories distinguish two complete families: all
private paired nodes, or private endpoints with every interior imported.
Mixed inventories cannot borrow either family's receipt. Private-node results
keep their private endpoint, measurement label and latency budget. History
remains bound to its source/configuration and current results also require the
original generation and native session.

Desktop throughput identifies the new family with the strict optional boolean
`paired_wireguard: true` inside `ordered_local_source`. Its absence preserves
the existing imported family. It is unavailable in `ordered_original_source`.
GET and POST must preserve the exact source object, ordered capture and every
node. Paired rows use private cumulative labels; imported interiors use their
public benchmark labels. A changed source flag or mixed labels cannot be shown
as a valid result.

## Verification and release boundary

The shared response fixture uses the pinned native SS2022 cipher on every
traversed imported prefix and the paired candidate. Positive runs use fifty
fresh nonces, including a nine-node connected source and a sixteen-node closed
source. Every traversed imported peer independently decrypts all fifty
connections before the candidate returns its authenticated reply. The suite
also passes with the Go race detector. Negative cases cover wrong late-prefix
or candidate cipher, agent key, node identity, replay, catalog/route changes,
a changed original member beyond the measured prefix, and blocked close or
cancel. The fixture's WireGuard physical transport is controlled; it does not
substitute for the separate native packet/TUN gates.

The named-final transaction also runs through the actual desktop HTTP handler
and profile store at three, nine and sixteen nodes. It preserves every earlier
node, writes the reviewed candidate as the final in a distinct named profile,
keeps Home unchanged, and preserves the committed result across a repeated
Save or late Cancel. These transaction tests are separate from the native
cipher qualification.

Shipping Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS source/callback suites check
their actual capture, proposal, receipt and persistence logic. Linux's headless
source and receipt checks do not claim widget execution. Full GTK/WPF/AppKit,
generated mobile SDKs and native platform networking still belong to the
authoritative hosted release matrix.

Two hosted failures found during this continuation have concrete fixes. The
Windows physical runner now retires its original verified executable by file
identity and digest after its owned process joins, including bounded handling
of Windows sharing violations. Failure to prove retirement still fails the
gate. The iOS OpenVPN profile fixture generator now emits a complete Swift
statement and uses the actual original capture accessor; its source checks
continue to execute.

The [build-all workflow](../.github/workflows/build-all.yml) owns publication
of matching packages, manifest, ARM64 images and production Compose for one
complete SHA. [Live release evidence](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) remains required
for installed-device routing, leak protection, off-LAN interoperability,
applicable signing and deployment acceptance. This document is not a claim
that a release run or those live acceptance checks have completed.

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-24-client-regression-repair"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-24-CLIENT-REGRESSION-REPAIR.md

# Native builds and saved client settings — November 24, 2026

This repair continues the [reconciled requirements](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md),
the recovered original map-first requests, and the October 12 comparison.
It preserves the existing mode catalog, measured route ownership, profile
operations, generic packages, native protection checks and release gates.
The CUSTOM action and deletion defects also existed in the October 12 baseline;
their age does not remove them from the requested working product.

## User-facing repairs

- Android protection and multihop controls now use actual click callbacks.
  Accessibility clicks apply the preference; rendering a checkbox does not.
- Android Home DNS rendering no longer acts like a new user selection.
  Opening an editor retains the saved Home choice, the editor opens the chosen
  DNS mode, and successful Save refreshes Home. The saved node generation is
  checked at commit so an older editor cannot overwrite a newer profile.
- Windows, GTK and AppKit Router Settings now retain the displayed profile ID
  and policy revision. Loading another saved setup or changing the same node
  makes an old form stale. The controller checks the captured source again
  under its commit lock and applies preferences to the current record, keeping
  independent latency and effective-MTU readbacks.
- Desktop and Android CUSTOM creation commands use a distinct action ID,
  leaving a real preset named `new` available. Cancelling a builder or failing
  to open it restores the actual saved mode. Programmatic refreshes do not
  replace the saved choice.
- The iOS swipe and context-menu Delete buttons share the same guarded
  operation. Deleting the active preset resets that choice to SMART AUTO;
  deleting another preset preserves the selection. AppKit and WPF deletion
  target the captured original preset rather than an unrelated edited name.
- WPF Save & Connect carries the exact newly saved layers through the
  asynchronous Home refresh and verifies the selected Router node before
  requesting a connection. Save alone remains separate from Connect.
- Named connection profiles preserve CUSTOM display names, including case,
  spaces and Unicode, together with their exact captured layer set. Ordinary
  protocol identifiers keep their existing validation. An older profile with
  no captured CUSTOM layers is refused before applying it, with an instruction
  to select the intended preset and update that profile.
- Android profile restoration enforces the existing 64-preset and 512 KiB
  bounds before changing state. Replacement at capacity remains valid; a
  historical over-capacity list can recover through an explicit preset Delete.

## Native build and test repairs

The original hosted failures were inspected at source SHA
`3f3da4c1a44d60cc3e8b3547bf9d2c88c7c6f8f7`.

- The desktop OpenVPN projection fixture now contains the original pinned
  Shadowsocks files required by the real preparation transform. The pinned
  source checks and repeated-preparation controls remain required.
- The Android ABI guard on Windows selects native Git Bash and supplies its
  fixture by standard input. It retains the four missing-ABI negative checks.
- The hostname profile regression test now accepts the two newly supported
  first-stream hostname shapes with routed TCP DNS, then exercises the original
  refusal and no-write checks after removing that required DNS ownership.
- The iOS candidate fixture includes its complete shipping predicate closure.
  The candidate prefix value is compiled into both the app and PacketTunnel
  target. Native NSError output arguments use Swift inout bridging. These
  changes address the ten diagnostics in the original
  [Xcode job](https://github.com/Eabusham2/router-vpn/actions/runs/45339817038/job/138260624152).
- The PF journal harness retains all 136 cases and 55 deliberate defects. Each
  positive case has its own original 30-second watchdog instead of sharing one
  30-second limit across the whole suite.
- The H3 reference peer retains its authenticated UDP relay through WFP
  inspection, using the pinned native timeout. The existing two-association
  test sends again through both original relays after six seconds and checks
  their eventual retirement. Production WFP inspection is unchanged.

## Darwin foreign PF readback

Empty foreign PF queues can be checked through the already pinned XNU ABI
without spawning a separate pfctl process for each probe. This is a read-only,
uncached check of all relevant filter or translation selectors, repeated with
matching tickets. Recursive queries also require no child anchors.

A nonempty queue, a changed ticket, or an unsupported ioctl returns to the
existing pfctl inspection. Other errors refuse the proof. Own-anchor, global
PF and legacy-rule checks retain their existing paths. Cancellation is checked
after the synchronous native call; the implementation does not claim to
preempt a kernel ioctl at a wall-clock deadline.

The mandatory isolated macOS fixture now also installs real loopback-scoped
NAT and RDR rules, checks that neither receives an empty-queue proof, and
verifies cleanup restores its originally absent anchor. The actual kernel
fixture and 130-cycle guardian retirement run still require macOS execution.

## Evidence and release boundary

Targeted compiled Java, Swift, PowerShell and Go checks exercise the affected shipping
callbacks, profile save/load transactions, candidate captures and native
preparation paths. The controller regression slice passed after integration.
The Go HTTP lifecycle tests reproduced the original name corruption and
rejection before checking Save, Update, persisted readback and Load. The WPF
callback suite passed 1,009 checks and rejected all 23 deliberate defects.
The final Android store suite passed 508 checks in 46 isolated cases. Its
ordered CONNECT prefix case passed all 510 checks with the CI fixture setup
and original watchdog after an earlier umbrella invocation timed out.
The Darwin queue model passed 76 checks and rejected five deliberate defects;
it does not replace the required kernel tests. The iOS source checks do not
replace an Xcode build with the real generated framework.

The complete local Go source run stopped when the workspace denied physical
network inspection in
`TestControllerShutdownCancelsSpeedLabIntentWithoutRestoringConnection`.
The guardian Unix-socket fixture also encountered a local permission refusal.
Neither result is counted as a pass, and neither gate was removed or weakened.

Publication must use the authoritative `build-all.yml` chain on one exact
`main` SHA, including native tests, all ten packages, ARM64 images and the
verified production compose. Its GitHub delivery is an exact-SHA prerelease.
Physical device behavior, off-LAN interoperability, applicable Apple
provisioning, private server/provider checks, deliberate production deployment,
ASUS fail-open revalidation and final regression retain their separate
[live evidence requirements](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md).

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-24-hostname-fast"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-24-HOSTNAME-FAST.md

# Complete hostname routes and original AWG2 Fast selected execution

This continuation addresses compatible route families still excluded by the
earlier source. Original requirements #214–224 and #336, the August 13/14
external-node requests and the August 19 recursive selected-prefix request
remain binding. Neither an eight-node implementation boundary nor a passing
source audit reduces those requirements.

## One original hostname followed by additional streams

A Local route can retain one imported SS2022 hostname as its first stream
immediately after a nonempty contiguous prefix of paired WG/AWG packet nodes.
The remaining original stream members may be literal imported SS2022 nodes or
independently paired Shadowsocks intermediates, followed by the same paired
Shadowsocks final. All Start Layers in this mixed family remain Off. The
original source-size, endpoint/key identity, MTU and 96-position physical
traversal bounds still apply.

The hostname retains its saved numeric Custom TCP resolver. Both resolution
and the imported outbound use the same immediately preceding original packet
node. A separate resolver, direct fallback, moved hostname or altered suffix
cannot borrow the original capture. Named Save/Load, startup Last, linked
source reopening, measurement and recursive insertion retain the complete
route on the desktop, Android and Apple clients.

The native compiler binds an answer validator to that particular imported
outbound's existing resolver. It checks the exact address batch consumed by
each actual dial, including cached and CNAME-derived answers. An address that
would collide with an original peer at the same port is refused before use.
Different peers may legitimately use the same port; there is no blanket
unique-port restriction. Cancellation, NXDOMAIN, a substituted resolver and a
later rebinding response do not acquire a successful measurement receipt.

Controlled native tests exercise a nine-member AWG2 Fast route containing the
hostname, a paired stream intermediate, later literal imports and the original
final. They transfer 8 MiB in each direction, retain warm cached CNAME
resolution, and reject a colliding CNAME/address answer, NXDOMAIN, rebinding
after earlier success and a changed later key. Closed-prefix measurement at the
hostname and connected measurement through a later stream each require fifty
fresh authenticated replies and joined cleanup. Source and consumer tests
also cover four, nine and sixteen members. These are controlled native peers,
not evidence of installed-device or off-LAN acceptance.

## Longer selected routes with their original Fast entry

The longer selected family now admits exactly one original AWG2 Fast packet
entry, independently captured literal public SS2022 intermediates, and the
original paired SS2022 final. Explicit Server and Compare execution preserve
that complete original source. A Compare result can select either measured
winner; loading Last, reading history or restoring a retained session cannot
repeat the comparison or silently change the selected route.

The separate native classifier rejects a hostname, a paired stream
intermediate, another packet node, Strong in this longer selected family, an
altered member or an active Start Layer. The existing shorter families and
the separately qualified Local families retain their own rules. This is a
qualified addition, not a claim that every protocol sequence is implemented.

The MTU combiner verifies the original Amnezia packet endpoint and every
original prefix plan. It cannot raise the captured Local packet ceiling when
the Server route is selected. The original source, TUN tag, execution epoch
and remote lease remain bound through pause and readback; a missing
replacement reader is a refusal. Source/configuration checks do not substitute
for positive interface readback on the actual host.

The mandatory canonical native runner preserves all eighteen earlier selected
cases and adds fifteen Fast cases. It includes nine- and sixteen-member
Server/Compare response paths, both forced Compare winners, complete
per-position latency, 8 MiB transfers in each direction at each original
position and MTU pause/refusal checks. The runner compiles the complete original
worker bodies and checks their bytes, original source, executable identities,
authenticated endpoint responses, parameter continuity and joined remote
leases. Pruned experimental registries are not release evidence. Both Linux
architectures remain mandatory in the complete release pipeline.

The local Linux amd64 qualification completed all fifteen Fast cases and
seven hostname cases against the complete registered worker with the race
detector. Every case retained the original 85-second fixture lifetime,
90-second Go alarm and 105-second parent deadline, with source and executable
identity checks before and after execution. The Fast latency cases retained
450 nine-member and 800 sixteen-member samples; the two complete throughput
cases transferred 400 MiB in aggregate across both directions and all original
positions. These totals describe test workloads, not physical WAN performance.
A separate overlapping latency repeat exhausted the fixture lifetime and
failed closed. Its failed receipt is retained alongside the successful serial
replay; no timeout or cleanup requirement was relaxed.

## Consumer and integration checks

The actual Go desktop parent tests exercise named Save/Load with rollback,
retained selected Last restoration, source-bound history, the HTTP throughput
transaction, original per-position roles and Darwin policy capture at nine
and sixteen members. The complete MTU and relay packages pass separately.
Windows and GTK exercise their shipping editor and profile callbacks; GTK
uses real widgets and persistence with an explicit controller boundary double.
The Android combined native/JVM suite retains all twenty-six old and new
phases, 3,135 assertions and eight causal controls. Apple tests preserve
original nine- and sixteen-member selected captures, the legacy selected
inventory, named profile reopening and recursive hostname insertion controls.

Source audits check the new precise classifiers and retain tests that remove
or broaden their source, role, hostname, packet-count and traversal-bound
guards. They remain required checks. Consumer tests and source audits do not
establish physical TUN behavior or packaged-device acceptance.

## Reproducible mobile dependency fetches

The iOS hosted build failed while advertising all upstream Git refs before
the pinned source was fetched. The mobile preparation scripts now initialize
a fresh staging repository and fetch only the full immutable commit ID, with
no tags and a detached-HEAD equality check. Each of the three attempts uses
fresh staging; an incomplete checkout cannot become the dependency source.

When available, the current Actions checkout's GitHub authorization is scoped
to that exact official dependency fetch. It is not put in command arguments,
dependency remotes or the upstream build environment. Local real-Git tests
cover the immutable source, retry, failure cleanup and authorization scope.
All existing upstream source pins and package identity checks remain in place.

The complete required native, package, image and compose jobs must succeed at
one exact main revision before release publication. The thirteen physical and
private acceptance gates in [the live evidence contract](LIVE-RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md)
remain separate. No source change, local test count or GitHub artifact awards
those gates automatically.

## Later hostname Local diagnostic

For the August 19 through-prefix measurement request, the
`diagnostic/later-hostname-local-20261125` workflow exercises four- and
nine-member Local paths. Each starts with paired WireGuard or AmneziaWG,
then a literal imported Shadowsocks 2022 peer, then one imported Shadowsocks
2022 hostname. The nine-member path continues through the original literal
imports. A paired Shadowsocks exit owns final DNS and the private exit proof.
Every Start Layer is Off. The hostname's saved numeric Custom TCP resolver
and the hostname transport both traverse the immediately preceding literal
peer. Closed candidate measurements retain the complete route's peer-socket
exclusions, including the final socket.

The branch runs an original-classifier refusal for both depths, 18 encrypted
route cases and six closed or connected candidate cases. The native route
cases check eight MiB each way, an incorrect predecessor or suffix key, a
resolver reachable only through the wrong peer, NXDOMAIN, a conflicting
suffix answer and rebinding after a successful transfer. The candidate cases
require fifty authenticated responses or the expected cancellation or stale
catalog outcome. The Linux amd64 native receipt binds the Git commit, source,
compiled race image, original dependency pins and Rosenpass archive. A passing
receipt qualifies this controlled native topology. Shipping UI integration,
installed clients and off-LAN observations require separate evidence.

# Integrated route and release repairs — November 24, 2026

This continuation applies the current requirements, the recovered 1–356 audit,
C1–C7 corrections and the later user requests. It preserves the map-first
native clients, canonical mode inventory, captured selected DNS, explicit
connection actions, durable whole-connection profiles, original source
ownership and fail-closed native protection.

## Preserved work and corrected consumers

The integration retains the history of the existing Strong selected,
selected-private-stream, private-stream-depth, later-hostname and selected
Local private-response branches. The newer main-branch profile Load recovery,
DNS preservation and teardown fixes remain in the combined source.

The selected private-stream family keeps its precise qualification: one WG
entry, a literal imported Shadowsocks 2022 first remote member, exactly one
paired Shadowsocks 2022 interior after that member, other literal imported
interiors and the original paired Shadowsocks final. Every Start Layer is Off.
The native compiler still validates independent sources, identities, remote
ownership and control-message capacity. Broader Local private-stream shapes
do not acquire Server or Compare authority.

Desktop and mobile consumers must use that same qualification for their
editor, Connect, named Save/Load, selected capture and history. The Go parent
also retains private roles in startup Last and in macOS protection records.
An authenticated private hop keeps a private response measurement; it cannot
be relabeled as a public HTTPS benchmark.

The desktop transfer preflight and result retain the original selected role
inventory beside the source, configuration, generation, winner and node IDs.
The desktop latency parsers recognize the same precise private-stream family.
The iOS live progress callback also uses the validated active session's full
inventory, so a proved private interior remains visible in longer routes.
Source replacement, changed roles and unproved progress remain refusals.

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-24-MIXED-PREFIXES.md

# Original packet prefixes and imported stream routes

This continuation closes source gaps found while reviewing the
[recursive measurements and longer Local routes](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-23-ROUTE-MEASUREMENTS.md)
against the [surviving requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md). A compatible
ordinary route must not lose candidate measurement merely because its first
packet transport is AWG or because it contains more than one packet prefix.

## Measuring candidates after ordinary packet prefixes

An ordinary Local route can measure a candidate through one or more
independently paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast or AWG2 Strong members followed by
literal SS2022 streams. The selected stream can be an imported provider or
a paired Router node. All original members of a mixed-private route and its
paired SS2022 final have Start Layer Off. The complete original source, private
proofs, catalog generation, MTU ownership and cleanup remain bound to the
operation.

One ordinary hostname case also qualifies: a single imported SS2022
penultimate after one or more paired packet members, with its original
saved Custom TCP resolver. The native parser binds that resolver to the
immediately preceding packet outbound. The closed preparation preserves the
same resolver and outbound bytes. A failed routed resolution cannot fall back
to a different resolver or produce a candidate score.

The score remains fifty fresh authenticated private-agent responses through
the actual imported cipher and the candidate's own original SS2022 cipher.
It is not a TCP handshake metric. These additions do not grant response
authority to an imported candidate without a private proof endpoint or to
the selected Server/Compare candidate operation.

Native peer tests exercise fifty replies through one AWG2 Fast packet peer,
two WireGuard peers, six AWG2 Strong peers, and one WireGuard or two AWG2 Strong
peers followed by the original routed hostname import. Every original packet counter advances
and both stream peers receive all fifty connections. Negative tests cover
wrong packet or candidate keys, forged authentication, a source change after
the fiftieth reply, cancellation during socket cleanup, and NXDOMAIN before
the candidate is dialed. The suite runs with the Go race detector. These are
controlled native peers; installed-device and off-LAN acceptance remain
separate.

## Longer mixed Local sources

Schema six retains a contiguous physical packet prefix, a segment of literal
SS2022 streams containing at least one independent import, and the original
paired SS2022 final. A paired stream may appear before, between or after
imports. Consecutive paired streams are valid. Every stream must have its own
endpoint tuple and cipher key. The native compiler checks each paired member's
WireGuard identity companion and private agent, and keeps the exact imported
source and public proof for each independent provider.

For an original route with `P` packet members and `N` total nodes, positions
start at zero.

| Position | Original member | Evidence used for that position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` through `P - 1` | Paired WireGuard or AWG packet member | Authenticated private-node result |
| `P` through `N - 2` | Independently imported literal SS2022 | Public HTTPS benchmark reached through that specific imported path |
| `P` through `N - 2` | Paired literal SS2022 | The node's own authenticated private-agent result |
| `N - 1` | Paired SS2022 final | Authenticated private-node result and the selected application DNS proof |

Earlier extended routes with an all-imported stream segment keep their public
integer `paired_prefix_nodes` marker where that marker was already used. An
original deep Local plan exposes the exact ordered array of `private-node`
and `public-path` roles through `ExtendedLocalRolesJSON()`. A valid packet
count alone cannot identify the proof owner of a mixed-private stream.
Selected Server and Compare retain separate admission rules.

Native encrypted tests at nine and sixteen nodes exercise two WireGuard
prefixes, one AWG2 Fast prefix, and two AWG2 Strong prefixes. Each positive
transfers 8 MiB in both directions and proves the original private and public
hops, final and DNS. The corresponding late imported-key corruption is
rejected before final readiness. The twelve peer cases pass under the race
detector and join their original peers on cleanup.

The final canonical fixture also passes all twelve cases with one and with two
Go scheduler threads. A single-thread replay exposed a three-second deadline
intended for tiny proof responses cutting off an authenticated 8 MiB upload.
The controlled peer now changes its deadline only after validating the exact
benchmark request, using the existing private/public transfer budgets. The
mixed transfer caller additionally enforces a hard twenty-second deadline per
direction. The byte counts, original proof deadlines, wrong-key refusals and
joined cleanup remain required.

The physical traversal bound remains 96 and the existing input, encapsulation,
MTU, byte and deadline limits still apply. Source preservation at larger
counts does not establish encrypted traffic at every count or an adequate
MTU on a particular WAN. A source-family marker alone does not grant late
candidate-measurement authority; that operation requires its own original
native plan and qualification.

## Candidate measurements and named future profiles

The mixed family now has that separate qualification. Seven additional native
peer cases execute the original connected manager and the independently
compiled closed-prefix Box. A nine-node route with two WireGuard packet
members measures fifty authenticated replies after imported position seven;
a sixteen-node route with two AWG2 Strong packet members measures after
imported position fourteen. A sixteen-node route with nine WireGuard packet
members measures fifty real destination TCP handshakes at packet position
eight through both connected and closed managers. These packet and private
response results keep their separate metric names and scoring rules.

The tests also change the source after reply fifty, cancel during native
cleanup, and corrupt a late imported cipher. Each produces no score and joins
the original owner. The closed preparation preserves the original application
and DNS deny gate, selected position, tags, and original prefix. The source
seal tests reject a later source mutation, a foreign tag, and a different
selected position. A displayed packet-count marker cannot substitute for this
native authority.

At an original imported penultimate, the measured paired candidate can be
saved as the final of a distinct, explicitly named future profile. The real
HTTP/store tests additionally cover AWG2 Fast, two WireGuard packet members,
and the original routed hostname after one WireGuard or two AWG2 Strong
members. Save retains every preceding original reference and leaves Home's
selected path unchanged. Repeated Save, lost replies and late cancellation
retain the single committed profile identity. An ordinary packet choice
continues to use its separate insertion transaction and validates the complete
resulting graph.

At an earlier SS2022 stream, a measured paired candidate can also be saved
as an intermediate. The separately named Local profile preserves every
original packet member, imported or paired stream, and final. Reopening that
profile permits another measurement and named insertion. Consecutive paired
streams are supported. The packet transports must form a contiguous physical
prefix, followed by literal SS2022 sources with independent credentials and
endpoint tuples. Start Layer is Off throughout. Each original paired stream
keeps its own WG identity companion and private proof. Each imported stream
retains its public proof. The existing physical traversal and total source
size bounds apply.

The following original-source checks were executed for the generalized Local
family in the implementation linked below.

| Original members | Executed evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 5 and 8 | Connected and closed candidate runs reached the selected private SS intermediate or a following import. Each positive collected 50 authenticated responses. A wrong paired key, substituted private identity, late catalog change and cancellation during Close each suppressed publication. |
| 7 | A path containing consecutive private SS intermediates proved its original hops, DNS and final, then carried 8 MiB in each direction. |
| 9 | The route `WG → import → private SS → private SS → import → private SS → import → import → final` retained each proof owner. The race-enabled native run collected 50 samples per node, 450 total, and transferred 8 MiB in each direction through the final. |
| 10 and 12 | A ten-member closed prefix measured after position 8. A twelve-member connected path measured after position 9. Both returned 50 private-agent replies, with at least 50 fresh decryptions at every traversed stream. |
| 16 | A deliberately wrong private key at position 12 stopped after the original private proof at position 11. Position 13 and final DNS stayed untouched. The earlier independent-import family separately passed 16-member bidirectional traffic. |
| 96 | A source compiled at the existing physical traversal limit and returned every original role. Replacing a late private source invalidated the role and measurement authority. This case exercised the compiler and retained owners. |

The native fixtures use encrypted WG/AWG and SS2022 peers, native Box
managers, controlled interface routing and independent proof servers.
[Encrypted peer cases](../mobile/chain_component/mixed_local_traffic_test.go.tmpl) · [Recursive candidate cases](../mobile/chain_component/mixed_local_candidates_test.go.tmpl) · [Physical-depth source test](../internal/mobilemultihop/node_chain_extended_mixed_test.go)

The desktop HTTP and private store tests save a separately named
profile, reopen it, measure a fresh candidate and save another named
insertion. The eight-member source grew to nine and then ten members. The
tests check each complete ordered path, Home selection, source tokens, saved
and connected proposal logic, repeat Save, cancellation, reloading and the
startup Last capture. GTK, Swift and Windows callback tests check complete
proposals and reject forged suffixes or attempts to exceed the physical
depth. The malformed source-kind regression rejects a foreign kind even
if the record still contains a valid-looking private proof ID.
[Desktop transaction](../cmd/client/ordered_candidate_draft_final_test.go) · [Desktop source classification](../cmd/client/multihop_node_chain_imported_nodes.go) · [Desktop candidate controls](../deploy/test_desktop_ordered_candidates.py)

These mixed-private data paths require Local execution and Start Layer Off.
The subsequent [hostname and Fast continuation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-24-HOSTNAME-FAST.md)
qualifies the first original hostname followed by additional Off streams and
the longer literal Fast selected family. Layered hostname paths, selected
Server/Compare private candidate timing, and an unpaired provider without its
own private agent each require separate source and execution qualifications.
Local peer and structural results do not establish WAN MTU, Android/iOS device
behavior or installed desktop firewall behavior.

The eight-to-nine-node transition is checked against that complete native
compiler. The macOS editor now inserts the measured packet at its actual
chosen position before validating the full graph; its former append-then-move
sequence wrongly tested the packet after the imported suffix. Original source
tokens and every suffix member must still match. The GTK adoption callback
already inserts at the chosen position and passes the same transition with
stale-token, reordered-suffix, foreign-candidate, generation and busy-owner

Windows now looks up and deletes a preset by its exact literal name. AppKit
and iOS compare the original UTF-8 name where canonical Unicode equality could

GTK restores the returned layers and selected preset together in its private

another name. When a stored CUSTOM preset is missing, the mode chooser displays
its original name and a missing-preset label. A new profile cannot capture

The GTK profile manager captures the controller revision before preparing a saved profile. ### DNS catalog and native teardown follow-ups

Android's paired DNS editor and native graph now share the twelve known

hostname. Quad9's secondary IPv6 address receives the same explicit known
certificate name as the selector. The actual editor and generated DoT, DoH and

The macOS native interoperability job exposed a real composite teardown race:

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-EXTERNAL-FINAL-AND-SERVER-RESPONSES.md

# Ordered external exits, selected Server responses, and native ownership

This continuation follows the [recursive selected-hop record](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-RECURSIVE-SELECTED-CONTINUATION.md)
and the [reconciled requirements](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md). It implements a
distinct ordered external-final family, extends selected candidate responses to
the original Server winner, and carries AWG2 Fast and Strong entries through
recursive Compare-selected Local measurements. The original source, native
owner, credentials, selected execution, and cleanup boundary remain separate
from public presentation metadata.

## Paired entry Start Layers for Local external-final routes

A paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast or AWG2 Strong entry can use its original AES-256-GCM
or AES-256-GCM + XOR whitening Start Layer. The entry retains its own private
packet service, the selected native packet transport and the independently
captured encrypted UDP transport to the outer service. Every later Shadowsocks
2022 import, including the final, keeps Start Layer Off. Home DNS goes through
the paired entry. Custom DNS goes through the retained public final.

The named and Last records bind the WG pairing source, selected AWG variant
when applicable, and the separate Shadowsocks Start Layer asset in that order.
The original outer address, packet service and layer credential are excluded
from the imported route and candidate inventory. Per-position MTU validation
checks the original packet-to-layer detour, transport kind, physical owner
and complete stream suffix. The Linux worker checks independently running
packet and outer peers, refusal with a changed outer key, whitening key or
private packet destination, and successive candidate measurements through
the same original entry.

All eleven new cases passed on a Linux amd64 race-enabled native peer image.
The nine-member Strong/XOR route completed 450 prefix samples. Fast/XOR
completed two 50-response candidate rounds from a closed prefix and Strong/AES
completed two through the connected original owner. The prepared Go tree had
SHA-256 `dc74b0a6a86756407db32b7ef66508546255cacfca88ff25acdbd99689e81303` and
the peer image had SHA-256 `f85352d704eccc7d19ca8bef7dc3d8df34bfdebd3de998560b0bba25f211a289`.
The eleven raw transcripts cover this Linux run. The complete 106-case hosted
diagnostic and installed platform qualification require separate evidence.

## Paired AWG2 entries for Local external-final routes

The Local ordered compiler now accepts paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast and AWG2
Strong entries with independently imported literal SS2022 interiors and final.
The first AWG qualification used Start Layer Off. Fast and Strong retain the selected native AWG
endpoint parameters and the original WireGuard pairing identity. The external
final's captured predecessor must match the selected entry configuration and
exact AWG variant. Home DNS traverses that entry, while an explicitly selected
custom resolver traverses the public final.

Desktop saved and Last records require both the WG identity asset and selected
AWG transport asset in their original order. The two variants share the
`awg` base and retain independent mode names and source digests. The native
worker inventory adds Fast/Home and Strong/Custom routes, a mismatched
handshake-header control for each variant, and closed and connected candidate
continuations. Its acceptance parser requires the real peer's AWG parameter
readback and joined cleanup. The earlier WG and selected-private receipts
below apply only to their recorded inputs.

## Ordered paths with an independently imported final

The original qualification used Local paths with 3–96 members. The first member
was a paired WireGuard entry. Each following member, including the
final, is an independently imported literal-address Shadowsocks 2022 node.
Every Start Layer is Off. The compiler retains each complete source and rejects
duplicate identities, dependent keys, changed captures, incompatible DNS, or
another source family presented as this one.

The first paired entry remains the selected control. The actual last import is
the public exit. That distinction now survives desktop and mobile editors,
saved whole-connection profiles, source replay, startup, Last restoration,
map identity, live response, durable latency history, and throughput.
Saved profiles contain node references and settings; credentials remain in the
original private node records.

Desktop Connect requires the canonical `external_final: true` intent together
with the complete node order and original revision tokens. Missing, false,
aliased, detached, or incompatible intent is rejected. The public capability
field describes an eligible source shape; native ownership still comes from
the complete compiled source and original retained process.

Home DNS keeps its captured route through the paired entry. An explicit custom
resolver retains the final import's policy and route. An intermediate IPv6-Off
choice also constrains DNS lookup strategy without changing the captured
resolver or its detour. iOS named-profile validation distinguishes this complete
ordered Home path from a standalone external node without a Home route.

Only the original first transport receives physical bootstrap permissions.
An imported intermediate or final cannot acquire a direct physical route by
appearing in the public graph. The Darwin protection capture records the
distinct control and runtime identities and retains its Off, on-connect, and
always cleanup rules.

The final's measurements describe a public path. Its latency is an HTTPS
response after TLS, and its label identifies the cumulative path through the
custom node to the Cloudflare edge. It cannot claim a paired private-agent
identity. The 50-response capture and saved history carry the actual external
final ID alongside their original source, configuration, generation, position,
and request. Live response and the 8 MiB throughput result retain the same
actual exit. The desktop Performance capture binds every original node ID,
including short three-node paths.

The initial WireGuard implementation described here preceded the AWG2 and paired
entry-layer continuations above. Private interior nodes, hostname exits, non-Shadowsocks imports,
layers on imported members, and Server/Compare execution remain outside this
external-final constructor. Its closed candidate preparation measures TCP
through the original paired packet entry, and the public-response continuation
below measures independent imported candidates through later stream prefixes.
These are explicit functional boundaries, not evidence of universal
ordered-path support.

### Continue through an imported public candidate

The Local schema-8 family now admits a distinct
`routed-public-candidate-response` measurement after any original imported
interior, from position 1 through the penultimate position. The selected
candidate must be another independently captured, literal-address Shadowsocks
2022 import with Start Layer Off and its own expected public IP. The original
entry, complete prefix, retained suffix, public final, catalog revision, and
native owner remain bound throughout admission, measurement, and adoption.

Each successful candidate supplies 50 fresh HTTPS responses from
`https://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace`. The native path opens the candidate's encrypted
transport through the selected prefix and completes authenticated TLS before
starting the response timer. Each request carries a fresh nonce and disables
cache reuse; its complete bounded response must match the candidate's
independently captured expected exit IP.
The public result kind is `public-exit-response`; neither a TCP connection
nor a private-agent response can substitute for this score. Private candidate
registration, Server execution, selection epochs, and signed private-agent
claims remain separate protocols.

The source-only inventory filter validates the original complete route and
then excludes malformed imports and every ambiguous alias. An import cannot
reuse an original member's identity, socket endpoint, or cipher key. When two
candidate rows share an identity or credential, both are excluded while
independent alternatives remain available in their original order. This
filter returns captured input bytes; the final plan seal, original live owner,
revision checks, native proof, and operation deadlines still authorize work.

All five native interfaces expose the distinct response metric and two
explicit actions. **Use in draft** inserts the measured import immediately
after the selected prefix without saving. **Save profile with this hop**
creates a separately named whole-connection profile. Both preserve every
original suffix member and the actual public final, including when measuring
after the penultimate node. The paired first node remains Home's control.
The editor recaptures the inserted position before offering another trial.
A 96-node route can still measure independent candidates, but neither action
can insert a 97th node; a 95-to-96 insertion can reopen one final measurement.

The public catalog carries `public_response_source_nodes` and explicit Local
external-final metadata. Saved, connected, and draft confirmations bind the
actual request, view, position, metric, candidate, action, and complete proposed
path. Save and Use require the original native work to be joined at their
respective controller boundaries. Changed tokens, returned foreign source
maps, private/Server claims, incomplete samples, expired scores, revoked
catalogs, and canceled native owners cannot enable adoption.

Seven separately required encrypted fixture leaves cover the new continuation:
three original-and-recaptured routes with 100 HTTPS responses each, wrong
candidate cipher, wrong expected public IP, source revocation, and held socket
cancellation. Both independent candidate peer providers are closed and their
workers joined before a native receipt is issued. Build-all's native producer
and the selected-response diagnostic require this new inventory in addition
to the original 76 selected-response and six external-final leaves. These
seven new leaves require their own successful hosted run; the earlier
checkpoint below does not qualify this later implementation.

The compiled interface checks exercise the shipping callbacks against explicit
toolkit/transport boundaries: Windows passes 1,448 candidate assertions and
2,510 editor assertions; macOS passes 1,242 candidate assertions, 200 bounded
transport assertions, and 49,528 profile/editor assertions; GTK passes 558
candidate assertions and 41,718 editor assertions. Android passes 214 proposal
assertions and its 76-check product lifecycle, and iOS passes 121 dedicated
public-source assertions alongside the original 864-check prefix provider and
699-check saved-profile suite. Compiled counterfactuals reject removed endpoint,
source, suffix, cleanup, and callback ownership guards. These are source and
controller checks, not installed native-device acceptance.

A genuine TLS regression also closes a response-completeness hole: exhausting
the total HTTP wire budget can no longer look like an ordinary EOF for a
close-delimited body. The unchanged 16,385-byte wire and 8,192-byte body limits
must both leave a complete response before verification or scoring. Restoring
the prior reader in a test-only overlay fails the exact incomplete-response
assertion. Original TLS, socket ownership, and operation deadlines remain
unchanged. Cipher independence likewise compares complete decoded SS2022 key
chains, preventing alternate Base64 text from disguising the same key while
preserving every original source byte and native transport credential.

The actual 96-member desktop HTTP catalog also passes its unchanged
12-second admission deadline. The repair removes repeated parsing of the
same captured physical policy and MTU graph. A validated immutable source
classifies the positions once; every physical proof retains its own traversal
sets and captured socket comparison, and every MTU prefix uses the same
original plan validator and numeric ceiling rules. The closed-prefix path
accepts only its original unprojected constructor owner. Borrowed owners,
mutated captures, projected inputs, and invalid middle-node MTUs are refused.
The affected 25 shared roots passed 434 race-enabled verdicts, and the complete
MTU package and independent equivalence/refusal regression passed. The final
controller receipt below separately binds the whole integrated Go source.

The closed first-entry candidate preparation retains that same paired entry
as its durable policy and journal owner. Normal replacement, unsaved insertion,
and a separately named whole-connection profile preserve the original ordered
suffix and public final. A candidate for this family must be another independent
literal-address SS2022 import; a private interior or hostname is rejected.
The macOS candidate journal validates the complete captured saved-node inventory
and entry control at lengths 3–96 before applying protection. It grants no
application or DNS readiness while the candidate prefix is being prepared.

## DNS status uses the original ordered route

The generic imported-entry observer previously intercepted ordered routes
because their DNS registration shares the imported-runtime marker. The new
ordered observer runs before that generic observer and retains the actual
ordinary or selected execution owner.

A passing observation requires the complete original source, current profile
and control, actual process, selected winner, positive selection epoch where
applicable, and the native DNS proof and reader. Missing graph/native owners,
replaced profiles, a different runtime, cancellation, or an unproved selected
route cannot fall back to an ambient OS lookup.

The status reports the captured final resolver's verified policy. It does not
invent the duration of a new DNS query: its observation has zero newly measured
latency. A DNS benchmark or Retest remains a separate operation. Selected graph
observation also rejects incomplete, unready, DNS-unproved, public-unproved, or
failed native progress.

## Candidate responses through the selected Server

The new version-two candidate operation retains the original selected Server
trial, authenticated descriptor, complete source inventory, operation owner,
selection epoch, and finite grant. It is available to explicit Server and to
Compare whose actual winner is Server. Compare selecting Local continues to
use the original Local response owner.

The candidate's private source must already be independently provisioned in
the server's NodeChains registry. Its identity, source digest, transport tuple,
private API address, and credentials must match the requested candidate. A
client-local pairing, or an ordinary external-exit record without that full
identity source, does not satisfy the server's authority.

Clients send references and fixed challenge data. They do not send candidate
credentials or choose an arbitrary HTTP target. The server loads the original
private source, retains its inode and digest, and transfers it through the
owned private runtime file to the captured worker. A byte-equal replacement
file is a different owner and is rejected.

The worker accepts a bounded nonce/challenge frame, constructs the fixed
private-agent request, traverses the original Server prefix and candidate
transport, and returns the authenticated response MAC. Each completed score
requires 50 responses from that candidate and complete native drain. Wrong
MACs, replayed nonces, changed source, expired grants, stale epochs, and failed
cleanup cannot produce a score. The original 90-second grant and one-at-a-time
quota are preserved. Legacy version-one packet-prefix TCP establishment keeps
its original protocol and meaning.

Desktop catalogs opt in with `server_response=true`; subsequent operations
inherit that intent from the issued immutable view. The public
`response_executions` array describes eligible source geometry. It does not
certify server provisioning. An unstarted Compare draft has no invented winner
or selection epoch. Once selected, connected and terminal results bind the
actual winner and original epoch. Older unversioned clients retain their prior
Local-only behavior.

An absent candidate registration produces a distinct authenticated terminal
result only after the original native operation has joined and the live lease
has been checked again. Its MAC binds the complete request, original source,
candidate identity, endpoint, selected trial, epoch, and operation owner. The
result carries `candidate_disposition: "not-registered"`, no benchmark, and no
score. The next independently registered candidate can run on the same trial.
Desktop, Android, and iOS keep that row out of rankings and refuse Save or Use.
An ordinary error, forged receipt, substituted candidate, stale lease, failed
cleanup, or unknown disposition remains a fatal batch failure. It cannot be
reclassified as a missing registration to continue measurement.

The desktop native child now checks the measurement kind of the actual issued
operation. Private-response Local and Server operations no longer fail an
unrelated TCP-establishment-only mailbox check. Cancellation retains the
original operation kind and native join boundary.

## AWG2 recursive continuation

Compare-selected Local private-response measurements now retain original
WireGuard, AWG2 Fast, or AWG2 Strong entries through repeated independent
private/imported Shadowsocks streams. Use preserves the remaining suffix and
original paired final, and the next operation recaptures the changed draft.
The ordinary three-node start and the original 96-position source capacity
remain distinct from a claim of physical traffic at every depth.

The required encrypted selected-response inventory now contains 76 cases:
the previous 48 WireGuard cases plus 14 Fast and 14 Strong cases. The AWG cases
require actual client and peer parameter readback, authenticated responses,

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-25-imported-penultimate-candidates"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-IMPORTED-PENULTIMATE-CANDIDATES.md

# Selected imported penultimate candidates

This continuation preserves the surviving requirements in
[CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md). It extends the prior
[private penultimate implementation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-PRIVATE-PENULTIMATE-CANDIDATES.md)
without substituting source tests for native execution, release packages or
installed-device acceptance.

## Implemented route and operation

The original schema-six source has one paired WireGuard entry, independently
captured literal-address Shadowsocks 2022 interior imports, zero or one paired
private Shadowsocks 2022 interior, and one paired Shadowsocks 2022 final. Every
Start Layer is Off. The first interior is always imported; any private interior
occurs after it. The source and UI capacity is four through 96 members.

The penultimate member can now be imported, with either no private interior or
an earlier private interior. A paired private penultimate member retains its
previous behavior. The requested execution remains Compare (`auto`); the
authenticated private-response operation requires the original healthy Local
winner and its original positive selection epoch. It does not start another
Local graph or rerun Compare. Server selection cannot produce a private
candidate score or a saveable result.

The candidate must be a distinct paired Shadowsocks 2022 node. Every original
profile and private proof identity, including the old final, remains excluded.
The operation measures 50 authenticated private agent responses through the
original retained penultimate prefix. TCP connection establishment, a direct
probe or a public response cannot stand in for that measurement.

An explicit named Save creates a separate complete profile that replaces only
the final member. Its requested Compare setting and every original prefix
member remain intact. Explicit Load is required to adopt the named route.
Measurement and Save preserve the current Home profile and active connection.

## Controller and client ownership

The existing `response_source_nodes` field retains every original public
`id`, `mode` and `kind`, in order. Catalog, result, Save and cancellation retain
that same map and view token. A connected result also retains its selected
Local winner and positive epoch. The map is a description of the captured
source; it grants no measurement authority.

Connected cancellation before admission reserves the request identity against
its original issued view, even if another window has refreshed the catalog.
Missing or crossed views cannot cancel a mapped operation. Original retries
retain the joined cleanup boundary and return no candidate scores. A draft
cancelled before startup retains its source and required Local selection but
does not invent a selected winner, selection epoch or native DOWN receipt.

The shared runtime, desktop controller, Windows, GTK, AppKit, Android and iOS
must agree on this same source family and sole eligible stream position. The
complete source compiler, original native owner, original imported registry,
candidate inventory, retained selection epoch and joined cleanup remain
required independently of the public role map.

## Verification record

The full desktop controller compiled. Ten controller groups passed in three
separate invocations with unchanged 90-second child bounds. The connected and
draft named-profile tests cover all nine layouts: private penultimate at
4/9/16 nodes, all-imported interiors at 4/9/16 nodes, and an earlier private
interior at 5/9/16 nodes. They verify the exact public source map, original
positive epoch, 50-response description, named Save, cold Load, unchanged Home,
and original cancellation ownership. All three 16-node layouts separately
exercise pre-start connected/draft cancellation and Server refusal. These
controller tests model the native child's publications; the encrypted evidence
below supplies the actual transport observations.

The shared runtime passed 27 cases across those nine layouts, covering both
Compare winners and explicit Server execution, plus the three legacy cases.
Original pointer, registry and epoch controls, original member/profile/proof
exclusion, and per-position source admission remained required.

Actual shipping editor/callback tests passed on the desktop source: 2,393
Windows editor checks, 41,454 GTK editor checks and 49,215 AppKit profile checks;
candidate suites passed 410 Windows, 228 GTK and 379 Swift checks, with the
complete existing Swift mutation suite and 104 bounded transport checks. The
old Windows source fails the new nine-node all-imported case. These are
controlled callback and source tests, not rendered installed-host acceptance.

Android passed its actual store/Go compiler/callback/receipt/Save-Load harness:
222 baseline, 120 legacy/private-penultimate, 100 all-imported, 102 earlier-private
and 22 capacity checks, with its original causal controls. iOS passed the
source/receipt/named-proposal and real editor tests for the new families and
the retained legacy cases. Its catalog now checks every original proof role
against the actual saved record; an additional compiled mutation proves that a
private saved member cannot be reinterpreted as an import merely because both
public layouts are otherwise eligible. Existing source, receipt, cancellation,
selection, proposal and store mutation controls remained required.

Both composed recovered-native-UI and map-first gates passed on the integrated
source with the actual Java and Swift tools. Requirement reconciliation and
the full release-orchestration audit passed, including exact-source provenance,
private/public publication, Setup Center, durable state and release dependencies.

Two further failures observed on the preceding published head were independent
test projection omissions. The macOS public comparison transport fixture now
compiles the shipping profile-load transaction and its actual models; real
Foundation loopback cases and all four original transport mutants passed. The
iOS delivery boundary exposes the winner-aware candidate-position method used
by the shipping engine. Its zero-member, Server-only double grants no packet or
response position to either winner. The complete Swift 6 engine compiled and
its 47 ordered startup/stop/activity checks passed with that boundary. These
repairs preserve the production transport and source-ownership checks.

A later Windows throughput control also needed a narrower mutation target. Its
Local mutation had additionally disabled the selected-role check and therefore
failed at the wrong required witness. The two role controls now mutate their
own ownership condition independently. The unchanged production fixture's 264
assertions, 410 candidate callbacks and all six original mutation controls
passed on the pinned PowerShell runtime.

### Encrypted native evidence

The committed [Linux/amd64 receipt](evidence/imported-penultimate-candidates-linux-amd64-2026-11-25.json)
records all 28 source-bound cases and 56 exact root/leaf PASS records. Ten
positive cases each completed 50 actual authenticated challenges and then

Receipt SHA-256:
`7bfcc1940fad4fd97380aeb557b1fcf6365904fb76d2f79f95a29ffa40e0693d`.

`a6b1757178f0a9b2a545cc3913e561feae45f01965c59843b915a2bc6dabe604`.

`e30b5212da15849eee7112358eb994f66ac59f3a66bdc45521cebc69b7917d65`.
The receipt also retains ten original worker-source hashes and the pinned
dependency/archive identities. The first bounded compile reached linking at
its deadline and produced no accepted evidence. An unchanged warm-cache retry
passed the original 300-second bound; no case or build deadline was enlarged.

The runner's 31 controls passed. The ordinary required Linux release inventory
includes all 28 response leaves and requires exact receipt-set equality; this
adds no bypass through the manual diagnostic workflow. This evidence is the
registered shipping worker in an in-process Linux/amd64 encrypted fixture. It
does not establish the separate-process worker requirement, final exact-SHA
packages or installed-device traffic. At recording time, the preceding
published `a0d6c9c75fde9da6670b7a768c37bdb0117d24ec` build remained active. The
two observed fixture failures are repaired above; its remaining results cannot
qualify this later source tree.

## Boundaries retained

The new source capability does not grant selected private-response measurement
at an earlier imported position. The selected mobile capture currently seals
one response position; extending it needs a separately captured per-operation
position, exact insertion action, full suffix identity exclusion and independent
native qualification. Existing ordinary Local intermediate-profile behavior
retains its existing scope.

This change does not add a second paired private interior, an interior packet
hop, hostname resolution, an AWG entry, another transport or an enabled Start
Layer to this selected response operation. Ninety-six rows are a source/UI
capacity, not a claim of native or installed acceptance at that depth. The
required separate-process worker gate, exact-SHA release packages, legitimate
iOS provisioning, physical-device traffic and private/off-LAN deployment remain
independent acceptance requirements.

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-25-native-repairs"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-NATIVE-REPAIRS.md

# November 25 native client and Setup Center repairs

## Product behavior

- **iOS multihop editor.** Selecting an imported Shadowsocks exit retains the paired entry identity and order. Its entry-transport picker can choose WireGuard, Fast or Strong only from that control's actual original files; AWG additionally requires the original WireGuard pairing asset. The map editor retains the entry for Home DNS and the imported public exit. [Reconciled UI requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md)
- **Verified onboarding.** The guide can restart from step one when browser storage is corrupt or unavailable. Restart discards pending checks. When two checks overlap, only the newest request can update its result. Browsers with checks saved before response validation repeat verification once and retain their Full Guide step. Setup Center distinguishes zero observed peers, missing peer coverage and an unknown deployed revision.
- **Candidate measurement.** Desktop skips duplicate prefix members before reading their private files. Suffix collisions retain the original execution-eligibility rule, and independent sources are checked after file capture. Launch input can be reused only after graph ownership, mutable members, physical path, DNS, projection and digest checks. Raw and desktop physical graphs retain separate inputs.
- **Confirmed mobile selection.** iOS Connect retains the node the user tapped across the asynchronous admission boundary. A failed node selection cannot connect the previously selected external node or display a success message. Android's saved lowest-latency selection likewise retains a failed-save error. Independent profile actions occupy independent SwiftUI Form rows.
- **Onboarding request ownership.** Restart retires pending verification results. Run all checks reserves each check before sending its first request; a later individual retry owns only its own check. A superseded batch cannot enqueue a stale request or overwrite a newer success, failure or status message.
- **Download shutdown.** Closing the package manager closes admission before joining retained deliveries, so another retained job cannot admit a new stream while shutdown waits on an existing writer. The original READY-based retention deadline remains unchanged.
- **AmneziaWG imported exits.** The shared schema-8 source and all native editors now preserve a paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast or AWG2 Strong entry through Local imported Shadowsocks 2022 exits, saved profiles, Last restoration and public candidate insertion. Fast and Strong require their exact independent raw asset and mode. This source extension is qualified for release only by the mandatory encrypted native cases described below.
- **Paired entry Start Layer.** The same Local routes preserve the paired entry's Off, AES-256-GCM or AES-256-GCM + XOR whitening selection across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Each imported interior and final remains Off. Named and Last captures bind the original WG identity, selected AWG asset where applicable and separate outer-layer asset in order; candidates cannot reuse those credentials or endpoints.
- **macOS public-exit transport.** The shipping candidate transport accepts the exact five-field external-final draft envelope, binds it to the selected first node and retains every original source token. Previously the editor's valid existing WireGuard draft was rejected before dispatch because the transport allowed only four fields and required the last node as control.
- **Longer Server route provisioning.** The operator now accepts the existing schema-6 compiler's complete suffix, up to 95 members, and preserves each paired Shadowsocks stream's independent source identity. The offline router-agent checker assigns packet credentials only to actual packet members. These repairs keep a valid longer route from being rejected before its native lease can run.
