## Native follow-up repairs

The `9cda43e30` release run exposed two additional failures. The Windows Xray bootstrap reached its 90-second aggregate limit during the sixth case's expected post-retirement refusal. Four earlier authenticated transfers each took about five seconds, consistent with the pinned REALITY implementation's cold-detector wait; the log did not directly establish that cause. Commit `86e0272f4` uses the existing pinned detector observer at startup, with the original source inventory, race flags, child process/configuration checks and Windows compiler ownership. It retains all nine traffic cases and the 90-second limit and records each stage's elapsed time. Fifty ordinary source-authority, phase, scoped-reference and dependency tests passed.

The hosted rerun at `526760a3e` passed both native Windows bootstrap baseline jobs. The complete nine-case traffic root took 26.36 seconds on x64 and 25.30 seconds on ARM64. The separate wrong-credential root passed in 35.77 and 34.25 seconds, respectively; all three real detector completion/cancellation/configuration controls passed on each architecture. First authenticated transfers ranged from 5.136 to 178.255 milliseconds on x64 and 5.679 to 208.162 milliseconds on ARM64. These are fixture measurements, not general VPN performance claims. The original source-phase receipts are [retained with their run, job, artifact and checksum identities](evidence/windows-xray-bootstrap-2026-11-25/README.md). Separate WFP jobs and the complete gates on the release commit remain mandatory.

The Naive HTTP/2 native traffic test crashed during stream startup in its owner-close case. Source review identified request-header storage passed through integer addresses without pinning. Commit `67bac88cf` pins the enclosing header array, record backing and each NUL-terminated key/value before address conversion, then unpins after the native call returns. This follows the call-scoped storage lifetime in the pinned module's Cgo wrapper and leaves engine and stream shutdown behavior intact. All 31 existing checks passed, including the patched Go client race suite and ten ownership controls. The original native HTTP/2 traffic job remains mandatory on the release commit.

## Remaining acceptance

The ordered external-final source covers Local routes of 3–96 members with a paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast or AWG2 Strong entry, its selected Off/AES/AES+XOR Start Layer, and literal-address imported Shadowsocks 2022 interiors and exit with Start Layer Off. Its six added AWG and eleven added entry-layer encrypted cases passed locally; complete fresh hosted amd64 and ARM64 packaging remains mandatory. Other imported protocols, hostname/private interiors, layers on the imported members, and Server or Compare execution remain outside this external-final family. The first packet prefix retains the distinct Router TCP measurement; authenticated public candidate challenges begin after an imported interior. These are implementation boundaries, not canceled requirements. [Ordered external exits and their verification](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-EXTERNAL-FINAL-AND-SERVER-RESPONSES.md)

The resulting commit requires hosted native compilation and encrypted-path checks, matching client packages and checksums, ARM64 images, and generated production Compose. <a id="note-implementation-2026-11-25-private-penultimate-candidates"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-PRIVATE-PENULTIMATE-CANDIDATES.md

# Measuring a replacement final through a paired private hop

November 25, 2026

A user who selects Compare can measure a different paired final through the
original penultimate hop when Local wins. The editor can then save that measured
route under a new name. Choosing a candidate or completing the measurement
leaves the active connection and its saved Home profile in place.

## Qualified source and measurement

The new path uses an original schema-six route with a WireGuard entry, one or
more independently imported Shadowsocks 2022 hops with literal endpoints, one
paired Shadowsocks 2022 hop immediately before the final, and a paired
Shadowsocks 2022 final. Every Start Layer is Off. The three-member schema-two
route retains its existing candidate path through the imported middle hop.

Before Compare, the editor can identify the eligible stop from the original
source. After Compare, the shared runtime requires the actual Local winner,
its active trial and selection epoch, its captured configuration, and the same
imported-node registry used to prepare the route. The candidate plan borrows
that trial's prefix for the private response challenge. A result requires
50 authenticated responses. Selecting Server or receiving a Server winner
leaves the private-response operation unavailable. An existing route member,
including the outgoing final under another profile ID or private proof ID,
cannot become its own replacement.

Android and iOS/iPadOS carry the measured prefix position and identity from
the original capture through the candidate catalog, result and future profile.
On iOS, each page of candidate metadata must match that same position and ID.
The named proposal retains the original prefix, execution selection and the
measured final's own source. Draft cleanup finishes before the result can be
used for a separate profile. Explicit Load selects the saved route.

## Verified in the shared core and mobile clients

| Check | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Go selected-runtime plan | `TestCompareLocalPrivatePenultimateCandidate` exercised four, nine and sixteen nodes at zero-based positions 2, 7 and 14. Each size covered both Compare winners and an explicit Server request. The test rejected final-ID and private-proof aliases, a copied registry, and a changed selection epoch. `TestNodeChainCompareLocalImportedResponseCandidate` retained the three-node path. |
| Android editor, store and receipts | `android/test_android_node_candidates.py` passed 222 existing receipt and cleanup checks, 120 selected-response checks, and 22 catalog-capacity checks. Java exercised the original store, Go source compiler and selected callbacks at 3, 4, 9 and 16 nodes. The mutation controls covered source replacement, partial receipts, cancellation and cleanup ownership. |
| iOS/iPadOS catalog and proposal | `deploy/test_ios_node_candidates.py` passed 410 ordinary checks and 58 selected-response checks covering 3, 4, 9 and 16 nodes. The capacity, Local, Server and Compare phases also passed. All ten compiled mutations failed at their corresponding checks, including a metadata page carrying another prefix's ID. |
| iOS/iPadOS editor and trial | `deploy/test_ios_node_chain_imported_nodes_profiles.py` passed 696 shipping Swift checks and five source mutations. `deploy/test_ios_selected_draft_candidates.py` passed 164 checks of selected trial, private IPC, and state after shutdown. `deploy/test_ios_node_candidate_transaction.py` passed its source, epoch, cancellation, adoption, drain and foreign-owner controls with modeled operating-system and store boundaries. |

The source format accepts up to 96 nodes. This extension's shared and mobile
candidate checks establish the new operation at 4, 9 and 16. Existing 96-row
UI and request-capacity checks exercise representation and size limits. An
encrypted native run or installed-device acceptance at 96 nodes would require
separate evidence. Platform delivery and device acceptance are tracked in
[BUILDS.md](BUILDS.md).

## Desktop controller and editor verification

Windows, GTK and AppKit retain the complete original `response_source_nodes`
map alongside the candidate view, selected Local result and selection epoch.
The map contains only public node IDs, modes and roles. Each offered replacement
must compile as a complete future profile before the editor can offer Save.
The connected and draft catalogs omit candidates whose complete proposal is
not saveable. Results and Save acknowledgments retain the same view and source.

The actual Go HTTP handlers passed connected measurement, status, named Save,
duplicate-Save refusal and cold explicit Load at four, nine and sixteen nodes.
The controlled native-process boundary exercised the original private mailbox,
metadata-before-Start ordering, catalog pulses, uncommitted-file refusal and
joined MTU release. TCP handshake receipts failed the private-response
validator. The earlier packet-candidate and three-node response paths passed
their existing lifecycle controls. A sixteen-node temporary Server winner
refused the private catalog, joined its original cleanup, returned zero scores
with its actual winner and epoch, and refused named Save.

Connected Cancel now carries its original view token. Its bounded public
snapshot survives a competing catalog refresh and retirement of the completed
worker. Before admission, cancellation reserves the request nonce under the
same lock as its original view so a delayed POST cannot acquire another
candidate purpose. After admission, a completed cancellation requires the
original worker's joined cleanup. Both replies retain the original source and
contain no accepted scores. Draft cancellation before selection retains its
source without inventing a winner or selection epoch.

## Remaining hop-by-hop candidate coverage

The editor requirement calls for repeating measurement through each selected
prefix. A four-node schema-six route with a WireGuard entry, two literal
imported Shadowsocks 2022 hops and a paired final shows a remaining software
gap. The original source can compile a private-response candidate plan at
either imported hop. After Compare selects Local, the selected runtime refuses
the plan at both positions because this schema-six grant requires a **paired**
penultimate hop. A focused Go runtime check reproduced the same refusal at
positions 1 and 7 of a nine-node route and positions 1 and 14 of a sixteen-node
route. The requirement is recorded in [current requirements](CURRENT-REQUIREMENTS.md).

Measuring a distinct final through the last literal import is the smallest
remaining case. Measuring an earlier successor would also require preserving
the original suffix when the user saves the named proposal. Private responses
through a Server winner require their own authenticated measurement path.

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-25-recursive-selected-continuation"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-RECURSIVE-SELECTED-CONTINUATION.md

# Recursive selected-hop continuation and integration repairs

This continuation follows the [selected draft insertion record](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-SELECTED-DRAFT-INSERTION.md)
and the [reconciled requirements](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md). It removes the
single-private-intermediate restriction from the qualified Compare-selected
Local response family, connects the following measurement to the inserted row,
and repairs two independently reproduced product defects. Implementation,
controlled executable checks, hosted native qualification, and installed
acceptance remain separate evidence.

## Repeated measurements through the retained route

The selected response family retains its paired WireGuard entry, independently
imported literal-address Shadowsocks 2022 first stream, paired Shadowsocks 2022
final, and Start Layer Off on every member. Between the first imported stream
and the final, distinct imported and independently paired Shadowsocks streams
can now appear repeatedly in their original order. Compare must actually have
selected Local before a private-response offer can be measured or adopted.

Each operation retains its complete source, original native owner, trial and
positive selection epoch. Every private intermediate keeps its own companion
identity and credentials. Every imported intermediate keeps its public source
and measurement role. The server descriptor independently verifies the full
private identity inventory; an earlier accepted intermediate cannot lend its
identity to another position.

An eligible earlier position can measure and insert another candidate before,
between, or after retained private streams. Use in draft preserves the complete
prefix, suffix and original final. It writes no connection profile and does not
start an ordinary connection. Named Save remains separate; its penultimate
offer still replaces the final rather than silently changing the meaning of
Use. The following measurement captures the changed draft and requires a new
owner and new responses. A consumed measurement cannot certify another hop.

Insertion remains bounded by the original 96-position source capacity. A full
96-position path can retain its independently qualified penultimate named
replacement, but cannot insert a 97th member. This is a structural capacity,
not a claim of traffic through 96 installed devices. The three-member legacy
family retains its original behavior. Server-winning trials retain their
separate packet-prefix measurement capability and do not publish Local private
response scores.

The controller fixture now gives each paired test profile a domain-derived
cipher key. Its earlier repeated-byte fixture key collided with an imported
member at depth 16. The production compiler correctly refused that collision;
the independence rule remains unchanged.

## Native editor continuation

After successful Use and the original native DOWN acknowledgement, Windows,
macOS, Linux and Android start the next qualified candidate operation at the
inserted position. iOS already scheduled that next position. A retained suffix
no longer causes reopening the general picker to jump to the end of the route.

Each client recaptures the current complete draft and its linked sources before
the new measurement. Native editor lifetime, revision, selected position and
Home ownership remain part of admission. A changed or closed editor, replaced
source, unjoined previous chooser, or full source capacity suppresses automatic
continuation. The user still chooses whether to insert another measured result;
there is no automatic selection of a candidate, persistent Save, or Connect.

Android schedules that continuation only after the previous preparation has
closed its network and released its process-wide owner. Its deferred callback
then checks the same visible editor, revision, idle Home and current ownership
again. A duplicate, detached or stale callback cannot start a second operation.
Windows also rechecks the selected row and visible editor after the old chooser
returns, so a changed selection cannot adopt or continue the earlier request.

## Android location accessibility

The custom globe now exposes a labeled native accessibility click action for
Locate me, Cancel location request and Hide my location. Keyboard and assistive
activation use the same explicit permission, fresh-fix and retirement lifecycle
as the visible location control. Focusing the globe, selecting a node, touching
empty map space, or cancelling a touch does not request location. A late fix
from a retired listener cannot restore a hidden marker.

## Setup Center retention across clock corrections

The package lease begins once, at READY, and expires after 1,800 elapsed seconds.
Retry admission, the displayed countdown, delivery completion and the background
reaper now use that same fixed elapsed-time deadline. Linux boot time includes
suspend; platforms without that clock use a monotonic clock. The original UTC
`retained_until` remains a fixed public receipt rather than a renewed lease.

The original defect was reproduced with the production manager and owned files:
a two-hour backward civil-clock correction reported 9,000 seconds remaining,
while a two-hour forward correction deleted the newly ready workspace. Both
corrections now preserve the original elapsed lease. Repeat downloads and
interrupted transfers do not renew it. Explicit Delete, cancellation, shutdown,
owned-writer cleanup and cleanup-pending retries retain their existing meaning.

## Verification and build integration

- Complete `hopmeasure` and `multihoprelay` race suites passed. The focused
  `mobilemultihop` race run passed ten roots and 83 subcases. A separate depth
  run passed 39 distinct depths spanning 4 through 96, including 95 and 96; it
  is not described as all 93 possible depths.
- The complete unmodified desktop controller package compiled with the race
  detector. The full draft and connected runner attempts reached the original
  two-minute alarm in their nine-layout named-profile roots. Their completed
  cases passed, and the remaining draft depth-16 case passed independently.
  Neither timed-out aggregate is counted as a passing shipping phase. The
  original compilation, operation and runner deadlines remain unchanged.
- A subsequent focused run passed all five original selected draft controller
  roots and all 24 root/leaf verdicts using the complete unmodified race-enabled
  package and each original 120-second test deadline. It includes stale owners,
  expiry, capacity, three successive insertions, suffix retention, and insertion
  before, between and after multiple private hops at depths 6 and 16. The
  [receipt](evidence/recursive-selected-draft-controller-linux-amd64-2026-11-25.json)
  and [execution log](evidence/recursive-selected-draft-controller-linux-amd64-2026-11-25.log)
  retain the original source/image hashes and explicitly exclude any claim that
  the full connected or draft shipping phase passed.
- That race run exposed the expiry test changing a published deadline while its
  timer worker first read it. The production worker now receives the issued
  deadline by value while the controller lock is held; test-only expiry changes
  acquire that same lock. The original deadline and cleanup guards remain.
- The shipping GTK editor passed 41,560 checks under Xvfb and all 43 editor
  mutation controls. Its separate candidate suite passed 427 real-widget
  checks, 102 status guards and the retained receipt/native-DOWN controls.
  HTTP delivery was controlled; this is not a physical tunnel result.
- The AppKit continuation callback suite passed 49,252 checks and its stale
  revision control. Windows and Android callback checks exercise the actual
  inserted index, including before a retained suffix. The portable Windows
  suite passed 14,169 assertions and 34 causal controls before the final
  selection guard; the final callback group passed 2,434 checks including that
  guard. The real Android store/shared-Go fixture separately checks the returned
  inserted position. Android preparation continuation passed 75 UI and 92 owner
  checks with 11 rejecting controls each; its independent prefix handoff suite
  passed 98 checks and eight rejecting controls.
- The iOS insertion suite passed 70 checks. The Android candidate and iOS
  named-profile suites retained their source, cancellation, native-DOWN,
  private-stream and extended-route cases. These checks do not substitute for
  signed packages or installed-device runs.
- The Android globe executable model passed its 311 positive checks, 51
  imported-packet checks, explicit accessibility activation and cancellation,
  independent node selection and negative controls.
- The Setup Center four-suite retention audit passed, including forward and

- All 14 source/security commands from the requirements-closure workflow passed

  execution, signed release assets and installed-device acceptance.

Seven recursive encrypted native cases are added to the required selected
response inventory, increasing it from 41 to 48. They cover consecutive and
interleaved private streams, deeper original positions, wrong candidate keys,
late cancellation and a Server winner. These new cases require their own
hosted native results. Earlier 41-case receipts do not qualify the added seven.

The historical selected-response diagnostic still runs the pinned pre-feature
runtime and must observe its original refusal. It appends only the two current
source catalog predicates required to compile modern test declarations; it
does not replace the historical runtime method with the new implementation.
Its negative witness and current positive execution both passed locally.

Hosted checks also exposed stale GTK fixture extraction boundaries and outdated
forwarding assertions. The fixtures now compile the actual intended callbacks
and verify the displayed router, path token, requested Boolean state and fresh
readback. The macOS race prerequisite builder warms the actual tagged test
imports before the original bounded test invocation. Windows initializes its
pinned compiler toolchain before the independent WPF contract. No native,
source, packaging, signing, networking or release gate is removed.

## AWG2 Fast and Strong entry support

Compare Local now accepts the original paired WireGuard, AWG2 Fast, or AWG2
Strong entry for authenticated stream-prefix candidates. All three preserve the
literal-address first import, independent paired or imported stream interiors,
paired final, and Off Start Layer at every position. The three-node source can
grow into a recursive draft. The original 96-node physical limit still applies.
The native diagnostic inventories 48 WireGuard and 28 AWG cases. Its AWG
cases require real client and peer parameter readback, 50 authenticated
responses for each successful choice, and reloaded DNS and application traffic.
The diagnostic also checks that changing the packet key or handshake header
reaches the original encrypted peer and yields no decrypted connection.

## Remaining implementation and acceptance boundaries

The following describes this record's original source generation. The later
[external-final and Server response continuation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-EXTERNAL-FINAL-AND-SERVER-RESPONSES.md)
implements separately qualified families for both gaps and records their
remaining restrictions and native acceptance requirements.

The following source restrictions remain explicit; they are not described as
finished merely because unavailable paths fail closed:

- Authenticated stream-prefix candidate responses for an explicit Server or
  Compare Server winner need their own original remote measurement owner.
- Ordered paths of three or more members still require a paired final. Direct
  and pair external-exit support does not establish an imported final in those
  longer ordered paths.

The exact-source Build-all workflow remains responsible for release assets,
ARM64 server images, manifests and generated Compose. Full native platform
results, legitimate iOS provisioning, installed route/DNS/leak checks, off-LAN
operation, visual/accessibility acceptance, live private integrations and a
deliberate production deployment remain separate requirements. No new release
or whole-project completion is inferred from the local results above.

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-SELECTED-DRAFT-INSERTION.md

# Selected earlier-hop measurements and unsaved draft insertion

The [later recursive continuation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-RECURSIVE-SELECTED-CONTINUATION.md)
supersedes this record's single-private-intermediate restriction and its manual
desktop/Android continuation behavior. The original evidence below remains
attached to the source and case inventory that produced it.

This continuation implements the recursive editor interaction required by
[the reconciled product contract](REQUIREMENTS-RECONCILED.md). A measured candidate
can be inserted into the original unsaved draft after its temporary native owner
is fully DOWN. Named profile Save remains a separate action. Source, executable
fixture, hosted release, and installed-device evidence are recorded separately.

## Route qualification

The selected earlier-hop response family has an original paired WireGuard
entry, literal-address imported Shadowsocks 2022 intermediates, a paired
Shadowsocks 2022 final, and Start Layer Off on every member. Compare must have
actually selected Local. An original four- through 95-member source with no
private intermediate may measure through an eligible earlier imported stop.
Every operation captures the selected position, the complete original source,
the original trial and its positive selection epoch.

An earlier named proposal inserts the measured paired Shadowsocks member after
the measured stop, retaining every prefix and suffix member and the original
final. A penultimate named proposal preserves its existing behavior of replacing
the final. The candidate must be distinct from every original profile and
private proof identity, including identities in the unmeasured suffix.

The existing penultimate response family with zero or one original private
intermediate remains supported. Server-winning Compare trials do not publish
Local private-response offers or scores. This change does not grant these
Compare operations to AWG entries, hostname imports, enabled Start Layers, or
two-private-intermediate sources.

## Use in draft and named Save

The desktop draft picker exposes independent HTTP offers:

| Action | Captured offer | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use in draft | `draft_path`, `draft_action: insert-measured-hop` | Insert after the measured stop and preserve the entire suffix, including the original final. |
| Save a named profile | `proposed_path`, `proposal_action` | Save the separately compiled intermediate insertion or final replacement as a new complete profile. |

The two paths can differ at the penultimate stop. The desktop controller never derives
the draft insertion from the named final-replacement array. It compiles both
offers independently against their original sources, then recompiles and
revalidates the selected offer at adoption.

Use is available only from an original editor-draft operation. It carries no
profile name, writes no persistent connection profile, leaves Home selection
unchanged, and cannot start a normal connection. The desktop response binds the
original request, view, selected position and measurement; Compare also binds
its winning Local trial and selection epoch. It confirms the original native
DOWN and cleanup and returns the exact inserted path and public linked-profile
tokens to the owning editor revision. An ordinary Local operation has no
Compare selection epoch.

The original three-node selected response family can become a four-node draft.
The qualified all-imported selected family can similarly grow by one member up
to the 96-member source capacity. A selected source already containing a private
intermediate cannot use this operation to add a second one. Its independently
qualified named final-replacement offer remains available. A 96-member source
cannot insert a 97th member. Capacity checks are source and UI boundaries, not
evidence of a live 95-hop or 96-hop path.

The editor's subsequent measurement captures the edited draft anew, with its
new source, request and original native owner. On iOS the editor schedules the
next qualified position; Android and desktop offer the following Measure
action. It cannot reuse the consumed
candidate receipt. Each subsequent position still requires its own qualified
native path. Ordinary Local response drafts use the existing complete Local
compiler and original closed-prefix measurement owner. Existing routed-TCP
draft choices retain their original behavior and measurement meaning.

## Desktop and mobile integration

Windows, GTK and AppKit provide the separate draft action and preserve the
original final node. Their result callbacks reject a changed path, action,
source map, selected execution, epoch, or editor revision. Connected pickers
retain the named-profile workflow.

The macOS HTTP constructor now admits the corresponding bounded selected-draft
catalog, run, named Save, Use and Cancel requests, including deeper eligible
positions. Its checks still reject unknown fields, malformed scopes, positions,
tokens, duplicate nodes and paths inconsistent with the requested action.

The legacy connected response without an explicit source map is restricted to
its original three-node catalog shape. A larger selected route cannot obtain
that compatibility path merely by choosing the first imported hop.

Android and iOS retain their original compiled candidate proposals across native
DOWN. Draft adoption belongs to the captured editor transaction, preserves
the original suffix and final, and does not update Home or persistent profile
storage. An earlier insertion can reuse its matching compiled named proposal;
both clients freshly validate all linked sources before adopting it. Their
named Save/Load paths retain the execution choice and every unaffected member;
a penultimate named Save replaces the old final as specified above.

## Acceptance still requiring separate evidence

The authoritative Build-all run must package and publish the complete final
commit. An older green workflow or a partial run cannot certify these changes.

Physical route and leak checks, network transitions, off-LAN interoperability,
device UI/DPI verification, private server integrations and live AI providers,

<a id="note-implementation-2026-11-25-system-lifecycle-repairs"></a>

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-SYSTEM-LIFECYCLE-REPAIRS.md

# Setup Center, forwarding and native release repairs

This record accompanies the [selected draft insertion implementation](IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-25-SELECTED-DRAFT-INSERTION.md).
The changes below repair observed ownership and lifecycle problems without
changing the separate requirements for an exact-commit release or installed
acceptance.

## Retained Setup Center jobs

A generated package and its build workspace belong to the original job. A
successful or interrupted delivery keeps those same files available until the
original READY timestamp plus 30 minutes. Retrying a download does not renew
that deadline. Explicit Delete, deadline expiry and service shutdown now stop
and join an active writer before removing its input files.

Previously, a blocked socket could keep a job in `delivering`, bypass the expiry
scan and delay authenticated deletion. Delivery attempts now register an abort
callback and a completion event. Cleanup interrupts the original socket and
waits for that writer to finish. Late callbacks from an earlier attempt cannot
update a later attempt. Fallible metadata and file checks occur before the
writer is registered; all subsequent handler failures reach its final join.

The package builder now runs in an owned process group. Cancellation stops its
compiler descendants as well as its immediate Python process. The extracted
source and build tree are retained beneath the original job workspace, with
the original broker process and directory identity checked before use.
Unrelated processes and foreign replacement directories are not cleanup
targets. A failed directory cleanup remains visible as `cleanup-pending` and
is retried by the retained reaper. Shutdown refuses new jobs, joins existing
owners, and reports incomplete cleanup rather than silently discarding it.

## Interruptible GitHub sources

Exact-SHA GitHub Release retrieval remains first, followed by exact-SHA Actions
artifacts and the existing bounded local build fallback for supported desktop
packages. Mobile packages remain GitHub-built.

The original Release and Actions transfer implementations now run inside an
owned worker that can be stopped even during DNS lookup, connection setup,
response headers or a blocked body read. The parent retains cancellation
ownership, propagates progress, joins the worker and checks the identity of the
verified output before adoption. Cancellation is propagated through fallback
handlers instead of being converted into another retrieval attempt.

Missing `Content-Length` no longer suppresses cancellation probes. A network
open failure closes the already-created package descriptor. Partial-file
cleanup checks the original file identity and preserves a substituted file in
that failed-transfer cleanup handler. Later fallback or whole-job cleanup
still owns files inside the original retained workspace.
The existing SHA, digest, provenance, size, redirect and authorization checks
remain in the original transfer implementations.

Nineteen lifecycle tests passed, including independent reruns. They exercise real
blocked delivery sockets, Delete, original-deadline expiry, interrupted headers,
cleanup failure and retry, service SIGTERM, a compiler descendant that ignores
SIGTERM, and real loopback Release and Actions transfers stalled before or
after headers. The stalled upstream cancellation and shutdown cases completed
in less than two seconds, before the upstream source resumed. A separate live
process survived the compiler-group cleanup test.

The retained job also captures its original directory device, inode, broker
PID and nonce. READY pins the producer's file and requires its independently
verified whole-file SHA-256. A cancellable scan outside the job lock records
immutable 1 MiB chunk hashes before starting the retention period. Each
delivery opens and verifies that same file before headers, then checks every
read buffer before writing it to the socket. The final byte count and digest
must still match. Cleanup cannot borrow another job's directory or a copied
ownership marker.

In the actual HTTP/1.1 regression, the second chunk changed after headers while
the original file size and modification time were restored. The client
received only the unmodified first MiB, then an incomplete-download error;
no altered bytes were emitted. Replacement of the pathname after headers
still delivered the original opened file. Incorrect producer hashes prevent
READY, and cancellation remains available during package verification.

The package retention and private-bundle audits, production entrypoint tests,
exact-SHA Release tests, 23 broker source controls, 15 package-safety tests,
broker security and owned-temporary-directory tests also passed. These are
local production-code and loopback service checks; they do not establish a
deployed production Setup Center.

## Forwarding controls belong to the displayed router session

Desktop forwarding reads now return a path token derived from the original
proved router session, profile policy, active telemetry state and complete
immutable multihop route identity. AppKit, Windows and GTK retain the router
ID and token displayed by that read and submit both with an explicit Boolean
update.

The controller rejects an update after a foreign session, reconnect away and
back, or a changed graph before contacting the private router API. It checks
ownership again after the remote response. Remote readback must contain an
actual Boolean: missing, null or malformed `enabled` values cannot become a
successful false response.

The integrated controller suite passed the forwarding API, ordinary GET/PUT
and disconnected/external refusal roots, including stale requests that make
no upstream mutation. Shipping callback harnesses passed 163 GTK, 71 Windows
and 123 AppKit checks. Native session-mutation and map-first source gates are
kept separate from these controller and callback results.

## Windows firewall observation

The Windows ARM64 imported Naive H3 run at commit
`aa5a7610b1650d5385fad121c39de13f6a64bcb5` lost its original policy readback in
the whitening cells. Its first affected cell had already completed private

commit. A failed proof remains a refusal. No native deadline or ownership
condition was relaxed.

All 21 host runner controls passed. The regression compiles the original
foreground and monitor methods, rejects the preceding double-enumeration
implementation and exercises transaction failures. The original Windows ARM64
test package and actual kernel observer cross-compiled successfully; the
resulting image SHA-256 is
`80291bbcc10fdb8e2458ba62bdca602b0af80dc9db52e82c238d81a686fedb0f`.
This is compilation and host-runner evidence. The genuine Windows ARM64
kernel job must pass on the final published source before the native repair
can be accepted for release.

## Mobile preview assertions and complete depth coverage

The earlier hosted Android and iOS suites contained assertions that treated a
now-qualified Compare source preview as evidence of a live Local owner. The
corrected assertions distinguish the bounded preview from original runtime
ownership. The Apple five-node case retains the permitted penultimate import,

The complete Android gate passed 3,742 checks across 29 phases and all nine

It now runs in its own required 15-minute worker, in batches of up to eight

The [complete remaining-runtime receipt](evidence/shared-runtime-remaining-linux-amd64-2026-11-25.json)
records all 88 unique roots and 510 child cases passing with race detection.
The six generator invocations passed all 144 original fixture cases and account

The receipt retains verdicts and byte hashes for all 520 package source and

The [Linux/amd64 depth receipt](evidence/selected-source-depths-linux-amd64-2026-11-25.json)
records all 93 source depths passing with race detection in 12 bounded batches.

These depth tests qualify source construction, reopening, ownership and wire

## Required Xray shards and original Windows UI dependencies

The preceding Native Xray job spent almost its entire 45-minute limit in the

## IMPLEMENTATION-2026-11-26-OWNED-SOURCE-REPAIRS.md

# November 26: retain the original registered source generation

Ordered relay authorization now remains attached to the exact private file that
was registered and read. Replacing that file with another inode containing the
same bytes cannot keep an existing worker authorized. Changing its raw bytes
while retaining an equivalent normalized policy also retires the original
authority. A bootstrap checks this ownership before native I/O; a revoked owner
can still finish its original Stop and joined cleanup.

The agent captures the original inode, size, modification time and byte digest.
Its live checks retain the existing complete policy recompilation. The private
state reader keeps its existing four-MiB bound. The native worker now obtains
both its bytes and its retained identity from the same open descriptor, and
supplies that original identity on full revalidation. This closes the interval
between reading a file and separately inspecting its path.

The same rule now covers the independently registered response credential. A
confirmed in-place edit could retain the original inode, size and restored
modification time. Candidate response authority now also rechecks the raw
SHA-256 digest from its original open, so both that edit and an equal-byte
replacement retire the existing operation before another response can use it.

## Native source and required verdicts

Desktop imported-execution projection produces both the common process fixture
and its Linux native lease companion. The projector and both affected Darwin
source gates now require that exact pair and inspect both original outputs.
The resulting Linux native package compiled with the pinned Go 1.26.3 toolchain,
verified PQ archive, complete native build tags and race detector. Both required
original process roots were present in the executable. The observed image was
141,847,592 bytes with SHA-256
`811cd541e9575c7febe0bf33fbf277c57817a49ca8a9800ffc6bfe2be351f190`.
This is compilation evidence, not a claim that either projected process root
completed a physical network test in that build.

The existing mandatory worker command root includes
`private-source-generation`. Its original and run/pass verdict are now explicitly
required by the receipt verifier. The inventory contains 27 roots and 138
required root/leaf verdicts. An independently altered verifier input that omits
both records is rejected. The `response-source-content` child is also mandatory; omitting either its
run or pass record is rejected. No prior required case was removed.

The mobile bridge inventory also includes its fourth existing OpenVPN root,
the selected imported OpenVPN TCP candidate. Both real native build selectors
must retain all four roots. This repairs an obsolete three-root assertion.

while the execution service is unavailable.

endpoint, bus ID, immutable daemon owner, credentials, optional received process
descriptor and original physical observer. It retains complete manager/link
policy, including DNSEx ports and SNI, domains, default-route and security
settings, and LLMNRHostname. A fixed read-only native command transports an
ordered, bounded policy with an immutable whole-policy digest.

## C — Scoped resolved-policy bootstrap adapter

The 12-file draft was snapshotted against 68011cbb plus A's two typed
policy/protocol dependencies. Snapshot creation joined with exit 0; the final
hash read failed after access was lost. No new C tests compiled or ran.

The draft retains the originally created helper, captured operation deadline

copies mutable MAC bytes and explicitly translates Linux raw IFF bits into
Go network flags.

preflight and daemon/helper namespace composition are integrated. All new
deadline, cleanup, stub UDP/TCP, truncation, custom-port, wrong-policy/link,
